articles.title: Underdetected peripheral artery disease in people with hypertension: A narrative review of risk-stratified case-finding, diagnostic pathways, and equity in care.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common but often underrecognized in people with hypertension because symptoms are frequently absent or atypical and access to physiologic testing is uneven. This narrative review examines how hypertension care can support risk-stratified PAD recognition while keeping targeted case-finding distinct from universal screening. METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through 31 July 2026, supplemented by citation searching and review of major US and European guidelines and relevant US policy and coverage sources. Evidence was interpreted according to the question it could answer: association/prognosis, diagnostic accuracy, treatment effect, implementation, or policy status. RESULTS: Hypertension and PAD share age-related, metabolic, renal, and tobacco-related determinants, while pressure-related vascular injury provides biological plausibility for their association. Resting ankle-brachial index (ABI) is the initial physiologic test for appropriately selected people; toe-brachial index with waveforms is preferred for noncompressible ankle arteries, exercise ABI for persistent exertional symptoms despite normal or borderline resting values, and duplex ultrasound when anatomic definition will change management. Guideline-supported risk-based testing differs from universal screening of unselected asymptomatic adults, for which outcome benefit remains unproven. Detection is clinically meaningful only when linked to appropriate prevention, symptom management, foot protection, and referral. CONCLUSION: This narrative review supports a risk-stratified, treatment-linked approach to PAD recognition in hypertension care, but the proposed case-finding pathway itself has not been proven to improve clinical outcomes. Pragmatic trials of the complete care pathway are needed.

articles.title: Severity-Based Triage for Direct Transportation to Nearest Comprehensive Stroke Center: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The efficacy of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is time dependent. Patients initially transported to a primary stroke center (PSC) may require secondary transfer, potentially delaying EVT. For severely affected patients, bypassing the PSC for direct transport to a comprehensive stroke center may expedite EVT but risks delaying IV thrombolysis. Effects of prehospital bypass strategies on functional outcomes are thus uncertain. METHODS: For this systematic review and meta-analysis, PubMed and Web of Science were searched until December 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies comparing transport to the nearest stroke center with transport to a more distant comprehensive stroke center in patients with suspected stroke were included. Two investigators independently screened records, selected eligible studies, extracted summary data, and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to quantify associations between prehospital bypass, endovascular therapy, and functional outcomes. RESULTS: Literature search identified 1,991 distinct reports. Of 18 eligible studies, 2 were randomized controlled trials (RCTs, n = 1,540 patients), 11 before-after studies (n = 11,837), and 5 cross-sectional studies (n = 1,139), comprising a total of 14,516 patients (52% men/48% women). Risk of bias was high in nonrandomized studies. Patients undergoing prehospital bypass and control patients had similar likelihoods of receiving EVT (odds ratio [OR] 1.52, 95% CI 0.98-2.35) or thrombolysis (OR 1.12, 0.92-1.35). Prehospital bypass was associated with earlier groin puncture (median difference -63.9 minutes, 95% CI -84.1 to -43.7). Time to needle in bypass patients was longer than in control patients in RCTs (median delay 34 minutes, 23.1-44.9 minutes), but similar in nonrandomized studies. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) at 90 days was more frequent in bypass patients (OR 1.23, 1.04-1.45). In patients with intracerebral hemorrhage, bypass was associated with increased mortality (risk ratio 1.30, 1.02-1.64). DISCUSSION: For patients with LVO stroke, benefits of expedited thrombectomy may outweigh possible risks associated with longer prehospital transport times. However, evidence is insufficient to recommend the routine implementation of prehospital bypass protocols. Further research is needed to determine circumstances under which direct access to comprehensive stroke centers should be prioritized for patients with severe stroke symptoms.

articles.title: Association of Prethrombectomy Hemorrhagic Infarction on MRI With Further Transformation and Functional Outcomes: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated whether pretreatment MRI HI is associated with 90-day functional dependence, post-MT PH, and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO undergoing MT at 2 stroke centers (2015-2022). Patients required pre-MT T2*-weighted MRI. HI was graded (types I/II) per European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study III criteria in blinded fashion. The primary outcome was 90-day functional dependence (modified Rankin Scale 3-6). Secondary outcomes were post-MT ipsilateral PH and SICH. We used multivariable Bayesian and frequentist logistic regression to adjust for age, sex, NIH Stroke Scale, baseline disability, comorbidities, infarct volume, and procedural factors. RESULTS: p p p Among 479 patients (median age 72 years; 46% female; 50% received IV thrombolysis), pretreatment HI was identified in 25 (5.2%), with excellent inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ = 0.9). Functional dependence at 90 days occurred in 47% of the total cohort, ipsilateral PH in 9.4%, and SICH in 3.1%. In multivariable analysis, pre-MT HI was independently associated with 90-day functional dependence (Bayesian adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.66, 95% credible interval [CrI] 2.15-24.28, Pr[OR > 1] = 1.00; frequentist aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.91-18.52,= 0.002). Pre-MT HI also demonstrated a high posterior probability of association with post-MT ipsilateral PH (Bayesian aOR 2.76, 95% CrI 0.73-9.26, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.94; frequentist aOR 2.84, 95% CI 0.84-9.58,= 0.091) and SICH (Bayesian aOR 5.59, 95% CrI 0.63-34.92, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.95; frequentist aOR 6.02, 95% CI 1.00-36.11,= 0.049). DISCUSSION: HI detected on pretreatment MRI is an independent predictor of poor long-term functional outcomes and correlates with post-MT PH/SICH. Pre-MT HI may reflect significant blood-brain barrier disruption and microvascular fragility, serving as a marker of reperfusion vulnerability. Limitations include the retrospective design and the relatively low frequency of HI, PH, and SICH, which were addressed using Bayesian modeling to quantify uncertainty. Although not a contraindication to MT, identifying HI may aid in periprocedural risk stratification and serve as a candidate marker for future neuroprotective trials.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Blood Pressure Dynamics and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Optimal blood pressure (BP) management after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, and whether early BP dynamics differentially affect outcomes among female and male participants is unclear. METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion. Serial BP measurements obtained during the first 72 hours after randomization were used to estimate patient-specific mean BP trajectories and short-term BP variability with a location-scale mixed-effects modeling approach. Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS). RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory. DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT. TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04140110; the Registration Date, October 22, 2019.

articles.title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Trace Visualization of the Central Retinal Artery: A Favorable Sign for Late-Window Endovascular Therapy in Central Retinal Artery Occlusion.
articles.abstract: In acute central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO), vessel stenosis and hemodynamic impairment significantly affect visual prognosis. We report a 69-year-old man who presented with 18 hours of acute, severe right eye blurred vision. Fundus examination and optical coherence tomography confirmed central retinal artery (CRA) occlusion with inner retinal edema. Digital subtraction angiography revealed an aortic arch variation and severe C1 segment stenosis of the right internal carotid artery (ICA), accompanied by delayed ophthalmic artery filling and faint visualization of the CRA. After multidisciplinary consultation, the patient underwent ICA stenting. Postoperative imaging showed resolved stenosis and improved retinal perfusion; the patient's vision subsequently improved and stabilized. This case suggests that revascularization can facilitate visual recovery even beyond the traditional window. Furthermore, faint CRA visualization on digital subtraction angiography indicates residual flow, providing a potential rationale for recanalization therapy.

articles.title: In-Hospital Outcomes and Mortality After Revascularization for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia by Maintenance Dialysis Status: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2006-2020.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence on in-hospital outcomes after chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) revascularization in patients receiving maintenance dialysis is limited. METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression. RESULTS: Of 7,962 eligible hospitalizations, 411 (5.2% of the unweighted sample) involved maintenance dialysis. Maintenance dialysis was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.96), non-routine discharge (aOR 1.46), prolonged hospitalization (aOR 1.41), transfusion (aOR 1.43), sepsis (aOR 1.88), pneumonia (aOR 1.69), multiorgan failure or shock (aOR 1.80), and venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.06). Hospital charges were also higher (adjusted beta USD 17,497), whereas urinary tract infection odds were lower (aOR 0.68). DISCUSSION: Maintenance dialysis was associated with greater in-hospital morbidity and mortality among CMI-coded revascularization hospitalizations. The inability to distinguish stable from acute-on-chronic CMI limits interpretation as an elective cohort. Findings support individualized perioperative assessment without establishing causation or optimal treatment timing.

articles.title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference. DISCUSSION: + Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

articles.title: Association between neuromuscular electrical stimulation and intermittent pneumatic compression for the prevention of deep venous thrombosis among neurosurgery patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis. METHODS: Postoperative neurosurgical patients were retrospectively enrolled from a single centre between January 2020 and December 2021. These patients were assessed to have a high bleeding risk and received either NMES or IPC as mechanical prophylaxis. Univariable analysis was used to explore the risk factors for DVT, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent associations between DVT and potential variables after adjusting for confounding factors. RESULTS: p p p p Among 232 patients who underwent neurosurgery, 131 received IPC and 101 received NMES, with no overlap between the two groups. DVT was diagnosed in 62 patients (11 received NMES and 51 received IPC). After controlling for sex, age, operation duration and length of hospital stay, NMES use was associated with a lower incidence of DVT (OR = 0.268, 95% CI = 0.125-0.576, = .001). Moreover, men were less likely to have DVT than women (OR = 0.469, 95% CI = 0.242-0.910, = .025), older age was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 3.419, 95% CI = 1.594-7.334, = .002), and a longer operation duration was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 2.180, 95% CI = 1.042-4.560, = .039). CONCLUSION: This study found an association between NMES and reduced odds of DVT compared with IPC in neurosurgery patients. Although NMES may be more widely adopted in neurosurgery to decrease the incidence of DVT, further evidence is required to determine its effectiveness in clinical practice.

articles.title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
articles.abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

articles.title: Trends in incident hemodialysis access and mortality in China: results from China Renal Data System 2000-2024.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUNDS: Large‑scale multicenter data on vascular access among Chinese incident hemodialysis (HD) patients are limited. We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024. Vascular access trends and distribution at HD initiation were analyzed. RESULTS: 16,717 patients were enrolled (mean age 55.62 ± 10.93 years; 61.54% male; mean follow‑up 64.41 months). At HD initiation, 29.17% of patients used arteriovenous fistula/graft (AVF/AVG), while 70.83% used central venous catheter (CVC), comprising 60.78% with a maturing AVF/AVG and 10.06% with CVC alone. AVF/AVG use increased from 26.24% in 2015 to 35.77% in 2024, while CVC-only use decreased from 16.16% to 8.27%. Mortality rates per 100 person-years were 4.15 (95% confidence interval [CI] 3.93 - 4.38), 7.24 (95% CI 7.00 - 7.49), and 15.08 (95% CI 14.07 - 16.15) in the AVF/AVG, CVC with maturing AVF/AVG, and CVC-only groups, respectively. In the adjusted Cox model, patients using CVC with a maturing AVF/AVG or CVC alone exhibited 36% and 91% higher all-cause mortality risks, respectively, compared with those using AVF/AVG. CONCLUSIONS: Over the 25-year period, initial vascular access among Chinese incident HD patients gradually shifted from CVC to AVF/AVG, reflecting ongoing and considerable improvements in vascular access practice in China. CVC use at HD initiation was associated with higher all-cause mortality compared with AVF/AVG. These findings support early AVF/AVG creation in end-stage kidney disease patients to avoid CVC use at HD initiation.

articles.title: Variation and temporal trends in Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group billing for carotid endarterectomy across Vascular Quality Initiative centers.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement. METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023. A multivariable stepwise logistic regression model was created to identify variables associated with CC or MCC billing (with odds ratios [ORs]). We examined variations in CC or MCC billing percentages among centers and applied a multivariable model to compare observed-to-expected (O:E) CC or MCC billing rates to adjust for patient differences. Billing trends over time were analyzed using linear regression. RESULTS: Among 75,064 primary CEA admissions for Medicare beneficiaries, 39.5% were billed with CCs or MCCs (31.1% CCs, 8.4% MCCs) and 60.5% without. Eleven VQI clinical variables that indicated CCs were significantly associated with CC or MCC billing: dialysis dependence (OR, 22.30), postoperative neurological events (OR, 5.25), length of stay >2 days (OR, 4.98), pre-existing heart failure (OR, 4.08), any postoperative complication (OR, 3.70), reoperation (OR, 3.65), preoperative neurological event (OR, 1.70), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class (OR, 1.50), urgent/emergent procedure (OR, 1.28), postoperative intravenous blood pressure management (OR, 1.27), and institutional transfer (OR, 1.16). Across 371 VQI centers, CC or MCC billing rates varied 5.6-fold, ranging from 15% to 84% of admissions. After risk adjustment, observed-to-expected ratios still demonstrated 4.2-fold variation, from 0.45 to 1.90 across centers. The observed rate of CC or MCC billing increased over time, from 35.5% in 2015 to 46.1% in 2023 (P < .001). In contrast, the expected adjusted rates predicted by the model remained stable (P = .269). A discrete inflection point was identified between 2016 and 2017, after which higher billing rates persisted (P < .001). CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variation exists for MS-DRG billing for CEA across VQI centers. Billing rates for CCs or MCCs increased from 2013 through 2023. These findings suggest potential underbilling at some centers and overbilling at others. Leveraging Medicare-linked VQI registry data and the proposed model could help to improve coding and billing accuracy, optimize reimbursement, and reduce Medicare audit risk.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement. METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023.

articles.title: Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

articles.title: Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in hemodialysis patients.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively. RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

articles.title: Maternal and Fetal Safety Outcomes of Thrombolytics for Ischemic Stroke in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Aggregated Case Series.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The safety of intravenous thrombolytics for ischemic stroke in pregnancy is largely unknown. We performed a systematic review to identify published use of thrombolytics for stroke during pregnancy, with the aim of assessing maternal and fetal safety outcomes. To provide additional safety data, we included cases of thrombolysis for deep vein thrombosis, mechanical valve thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism in pregnancy. METHODS: We used the PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines to conduct the review. We searched 3 databases (OVID Medline, EMBASE, Scopus) for studies published up to October 2025. We analyzed outcomes in a Bayesian aggregated case series to compare rates of adverse outcomes in our cohort with those in the general population. Elective termination and spontaneous abortion were grouped together, given that it was often difficult to determine whether complications of thrombolysis may have played a role in the decision for termination. RESULTS: We included 123 studies of 216 patients (median age 31 years) treated with thrombolytics during pregnancy, of whom 85 had ischemic stroke. Six of the 32 total fetal deaths were deemed likely to be causally related to thrombolytics (3 in stroke). The risk of miscarriage in our thrombolysis population was 12.4% higher (95% credible interval [CrI]: 2.6%, 23.2%) than published general pregnant population rates, and the risk of stillbirth was 5.9% higher (95% CrI: 1.6%, 12.7%). The proportion of pregnant patients with symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage was similar between our pregnant cohort and young, nonpregnant patients receiving thrombolytics (risk difference -0.4%; 95% CrI: -0.8%, 2.7%). DISCUSSION: Thrombolytics were likely causally associated with a small minority of published cases of fetal death after thrombolysis in pregnancy. There was no signal of increased harm from thrombolysis to the mother, including similar rates of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage. In many cases, it was difficult to discern effects of thrombolytics on fetal outcomes from the effects of the disease itself; hence, our results should be interpreted with caution. Nonetheless, our findings broadly support the use of thrombolytics in otherwise-eligible pregnant patients but underscore the importance of the risk-benefit assessment in such patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: The study protocol was pre-registered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42024605043).

articles.title: Impact of True and False Lumen Origins on Target Vessel Instability in Post-Dissection F/BEVAR.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen. METHODS: This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI). Secondary endpoints included 5-year primary patency, freedom from secondary interventions (SIs), and type Ic and IIIc endoleaks. The analysis was performed on a per-vessel basis. RESULTS: A total of 1052 target arteries were analyzed, primarily including the celiac, superior mesenteric, and renal arteries, with individual hepatic and splenic arteries occasionally incorporated in the repair. Of the 277 patients included, 75% were men, and 19% were black, with a mean age of 66.8 ± 10.3 years. The mean aneurysm sac diameter was 66.0 ± 11.4 mm, with extent II thoracoabdominal aneurysms being the most prevalent (72.6%) among this cohort. Technical success was obtained in 96% of the cases. As primary outcome, the incidence of target vessel instability (TVI) was significantly lower (P<0.001) among the true-lumen vessels (16.4%) compared to false-lumen (29.9%) and dual-lumen arteries (43.8%). As for the secondary outcomes, the incidence of type Ic endoleak was significantly higher (P=0.001) in false-lumen vessels (9.6%) and dual-lumen vessels (8.6%) compared to true-lumen vessels (3.3%). There was no significant difference in the incidence of type IIIc endoleak (p=0.241) or target vessel occlusion (P=0.458). Target artery stenosis was significantly more common among arteries originating from the false lumen compared to true lumen (2.6% vs 0.4%, P=0.009). Fenestrations were associated with a higher incidence (30.5%) of TVI when compared to branches (5.9% P=0.005), however, this was observed only among dual-lumen vessels. Arteries incorporated by a fenestration and that had a dual-lumen origin, were associated with a higher occurrence of secondary interventions (23.7%) compared to true-lumen vessels (8.6%, P=0.010). The same was not observed among the arteries incorporated by a branch configuration. The time-to-event analysis demonstrated a significantly higher 5-year freedom from TVI in true-lumen vessels compared to false and dual-lumen ones (True lumen: 83.6%; False=70.1 %; Dual=56.2 %; Log-rank P=0.0002). Freedom from secondary interventions at 5 years was significantly higher in true-lumen vessels compared to dual-lumen ones (Log-rank P=0.0104), but not to false-lumen arteries (Log-rank P=0.0847). The 5-year primary patency did not differ significantly among groups (True lumen: 98.3%; False = 92.6%; Dual=93.9%; Log-rank P=0.1368). On Cox proportional hazards analysis, dual-lumen (95% CI 1.24-3.28, p=0.005) and false-lumen (95% CI 1.04 - 2.60, p=0.0325) target arteries were associated with an increased hazard of TVI, when compared to true lumen arteries, having 2.02 (P=0.005) and 1.65 (P=0.0325) times more risk of presenting TVI than a true-lumen vessel CONCLUSIONS: In F/BEVAR for post-dissection aneurysms, target vessel instability and secondary intervention are significantly lower in target arteries originating from the true lumen, when compared to false-lumen or dual-lumen vessels. Device design, with use of fenestrations or branches may also play a role, with a significant difference only observed in dual-lumen target arteries.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen. METHODS: This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI).

articles.title: Fenestrated Endografts Provide Superior Outcomes Compared to Branched Devices in Juxtarenal Aortic Repair.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Urgent endovascular juxtarenal aortic repair with custom-made fenestrated devices is not feasible due to its long elaboration time. Off-the-shelf branched devices can be used, however, durability of the target vessels, especially renal artery branches, is of concern. Our objective is to compare mid and long-term patency of target vessels (TV), especially renal arteries (RA) in juxtarenal fenestrated or branched aortic endovascular repair. METHODS: Single-center retrospective study identifying all patients undergoing fenestrated or branched endovascular repair (f/bEVAR) for juxtarenal aortic aneurysms (JAA) between 2011-2022. A FEVAR group with use of fenestrations to incorporate target vessels (TV) and a BEVAR group, with use of branches were created. Clinical and anatomical characteristics as well as perioperative technical success and complications were compared. The primary endpoint was the assessment of RA primary patency, freedom from endoleaks and instability (endpoint including occlusion, endoleak or need for reintervention) at follow-up. Secondary endpoints were the assessment of CT-SMA patency rates, freedom from endoleak and instability at follow-up and the evaluation of the anatomical and clinical factors associated with renal artery bridging covered stent (BCS) occlusion. RESULTS: From 2011-2022, FEVAR was performed in 212 patients and BEVAR in 57. There were no statistical differences in demographics. The BEVAR group presented more frequently as urgencies (61% vs 11% for FEVAR p <,001). 955 TV were incorporated, including 536 RA. Technical success was 99%. BEVAR patients experienced higher perioperative death rates (14% vs 3% in FEVAR; p 0,005) and major complications (53% vs 17% in FEVAR; p <,001). Primary patency of RA in FEVAR was 99% at 3 years vs 74% for BEVAR (p < ,001). Freedom from RA BCS endoleaks were 97% at 3 years for the FEVAR group vs 87% in the BEVAR group (p <,001). Freedom from RA instability at 3 years was 95% in the FEVAR group vs 63% for the BEVAR group (p <,001). For CT-SMA only freedom from instability showed significant better outcomes at 3 years in the FEVAR group (96% vs 88% for BEVAR ; p ,006). In the multivariate analysis, the use of branches was the only factor associated with loss of patency in the RA. CONCLUSIONS: In complex aortic repair for JAA, fenestrated devices achieved high patency rates while branched devices, mostly done for urgencies, are associated with significantly worse RA outcomes.
articles.englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Urgent endovascular juxtarenal aortic repair with custom-made fenestrated devices is not feasible due to its long elaboration time. Off-the-shelf branched devices can be used, however, durability of the target vessels, especially renal artery branches, is of concern. Our objective is to compare mid and long-term patency of target vessels (TV), especially renal arteries (RA) in juxtarenal fenestrated or branched aortic endovascular repair.

articles.title: Single vs. Dual Antiplatelet Therapy after Fenestrated and Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after fenestrated or branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR). DATA SOURCES: PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global were searched from inception to 12 July 2026, with a supplementary targeted PubMed search on 5 September 2026. REVIEW METHODS: Comparative studies of post-operative antiplatelet therapy were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach. Outcomes were synthesised narratively when clinical and methodological differences precluded meaningful pooling; an additional quantitative summary of study defined bleeding outcomes was also reported. RESULTS: Six retrospective cohorts comprising 3 623 patients were included, with 3 197 patients in separately extractable single or dual antiplatelet therapy groups. Several studies reported associations favouring dual antiplatelet therapy for target vessel patency. However, differences in outcome definitions, analytical units, and treatment classification precluded a common pooled estimate, and one association was attenuated after accounting for treatment changes. Evidence regarding ischaemic events, mortality, re-intervention, and endoleak was insufficient for reliable pooled comparisons. Five cohorts reported peri-operative bleeding using heterogeneous definitions and observation periods, of which a four study summary yielded an odds ratio of 1.30 (95% confidence interval 0.87 - 1.94) for dual vs. single antiplatelet therapy. Given the differences in outcome definitions, this does not estimate a common clinical effect. CONCLUSION: The current evidence comparing single and dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR is based on heterogeneous cohort studies, focuses largely on surrogate outcomes such as target vessel patency, and shows no clear benefit for dual antiplatelet therapy. Comparative bleeding risk as well as clinical outcomes of single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR remain uncertain. Future prospective studies are needed to better delineate superiority of one regimen over the other.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after fenestrated or branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR). DATA SOURCES: PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global were searched from inception to 12 July 2026, with a supplementary targeted PubMed search on 5 September 2026.

articles.title: Prediction of Stroke Outcome After Endovascular Thrombectomy From Clinical Characteristics: A Machine Learning Approach.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Predicting outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is challenging. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data. METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke. A total of 4353 patients who underwent EVT between 2016 and 2020 were included, with those from 2016 to 2019 assigned to the derivation cohort and those from 2020 to the validation cohort. The model was developed using 132 routinely collected clinical variables that can be rapidly obtained on patient arrival. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm, and the model was built using CatBoost. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 2 at discharge. RESULTS: Among 4353 patients treated with EVT, the derivation cohort included 2764 patients and the validation cohort, 1589 patients. In these cohorts, 973 (35.2%) and 547 (34.4%) achieved mRS 0 to 2, respectively. Boruta selected 47 predictors. CatBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.744 (95% CI, 0.710-0.776) in the derivation test set and 0.781 (95% CI, 0.755-0.803) in the validation cohort. Validation areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.792 (95% CI, 0.765-0.815) for mRS 0 to 1, 0.766 (95% CI, 0.744-0.787) for mRS 0 to 3, and 0.680 (95% CI, 0.631-0.729) for mRS 6. CONCLUSIONS: Our machine learning model predicted outcomes following EVT using only admission clinical data. This imaging-independent machine learning approach may support early prognostication and facilitate discussions of expected clinical courses.

This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data. METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke.

articles.title: Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI. METHODS: We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved). RESULTS: P Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23];=0.445; C statistic=0.77). CONCLUSIONS: One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

articles.title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results. METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points. RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results. CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

articles.title: Rivaroxaban Then Aspirin vs. Aspirin Alone after Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aspirin after an initial short course of rivaroxaban has been shown to be safe and effective for the prevention of venous thromboembolism after total hip or total knee arthroplasty, but uncertainty remains about the use of aspirin alone. METHODS: In this multicenter, double-blind, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients to receive once-daily thromboprophylaxis with either 81 mg of aspirin or 10 mg of oral rivaroxaban for the first 5 days after total hip or total knee arthroplasty. All the patients then received further thromboprophylaxis with 81 mg of aspirin daily for 9 additional days after knee arthroplasty and for 30 additional days after hip arthroplasty. Patients were followed for 90 days for symptomatic venous thromboembolism, which consisted of either proximal deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (primary effectiveness outcome), and for bleeding complications (primary safety outcome). The noninferiority margin for aspirin alone as compared with rivaroxaban-aspirin was 0.7 percentage points. RESULTS: A total of 5429 patients underwent randomization. Venous thromboembolism developed in 13 of 2718 patients (0.48%) in the aspirin-alone group and in 12 of 2647 patients (0.45%) in the rivaroxaban-aspirin group (risk difference, 0.02 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.34 to 0.39; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding events occurred in 45 of 2718 patients (1.66%) in the aspirin-alone group and in 54 of 2647 patients (2.04%) in the rivaroxaban-aspirin group (risk difference, -0.38%; 95% CI, -1.11 to 0.34). CONCLUSIONS: After total hip and total knee arthroplasty, the use of aspirin alone was not inferior to a strategy of using rivaroxaban followed by aspirin for the prevention of symptomatic venous thromboembolism, with no clinically relevant difference in bleeding events. (Funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research; EPCAT III ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04075240.).

articles.title: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Is Associated With Heart Failure in Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] in peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains uncertain. METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively studied 138 patients with intermittent claudication undergoing endovascular therapy. Patients were classified by Lp(a) level (≥30 vs. <30 mg/dL). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a higher incidence of MACE (31.1% vs. 9.6%; P=0.002), predominantly driven by heart failure. It independently predicted MACE (HR 4.23) and heart failure (HR 5.12), but not cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was associated with heart failure-driven MACE after endovascular therapy in patients with PAD.

articles.title: Training Structure and Satisfaction with Learning in European Vascular Surgery Training: Results from the European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) Surveys.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study describes the availability of modifiable structural training elements across European vascular surgery programmes to identify which of these elements are independently associated with trainees' satisfaction with learning and to contextualise them with trainer reported delivery constraints. METHODS: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale). Five modifiable structural elements were identified a priori: structured curriculum; training coordinator; dedicated or protected training time; assigned mentor; and simulation access. Associations were examined using an adjusted linear mixed effects model (LMM), with secondary models for coordinator resourcing and mentorship evaluations. Trainer data were analysed descriptively. RESULTS: Of 420 trainee responses (32 countries), 273 entered the complete case main LMM. Availability was inconsistent: structured curriculum 56.4%; dedicated or protected training time 34.3%; and simulation access 32.3%. In the adjusted LMM, learning satisfaction was higher with a structured curriculum (= 0.79, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.21 - 1.38; p = .008) and dedicated training time (= 0.62, 95% CI 0.05 - 1.19; p = .035). In secondary models, coordinators with dedicated educational time showed the largest association (= 1.76, 95% CI 1.05 - 2.46; p < .001), and mentorship with regular evaluations was associated with higher satisfaction (= 0.98, 95% CI 0.36 - 1.59; p = .002). Among 659 trainers (37 countries), mentorship importance was rated 8.26 out of 10, yet only 43.4% had dedicated mentorship time; the dominant barrier was clinical workload (84.1%). Desired improvements were dedicated mentorship time (64.4%), formalised programmes (54.3%), and regular feedback sessions (51.6%). CONCLUSION: A structured curriculum and dedicated training time were independently associated with higher trainee learning satisfaction across European vascular surgery programmes. Organisational roles such as training coordinators and mentors were associated with higher satisfaction in exploratory secondary analyses, suggesting these roles may be most beneficial when actively resourced with dedicated time and regular evaluations. Trainer constraints converged on protected time for training and mentorship.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: This study describes the availability of modifiable structural training elements across European vascular surgery programmes to identify which of these elements are independently associated with trainees' satisfaction with learning and to contextualise them with trainer reported delivery constraints. METHODS: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale).

articles.title: The IMA-PLUS Score for Predicting Type 2 Endoleak After Endovascular Repair: Development and External Validation in European and Japanese Cohorts.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Prophylactic embolisation of infrarenal branch vessels has been investigated to prevent type 2 endoleak (EL2) following endovascular repair (EVAR) of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), but patient selection is poorly defined. In this study, a computed tomography angiography (CTA) based risk score was developed and validated to predict EL2 after EVAR. METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective diagnostic study used prospectively collected data from the Zenith alpha for aneurysm Repair Registry (ZEPHYR) as the development cohort. Eligible patients underwent standard EVAR with pre-operative arterial phase CTA and at least one post-operative delayed phase CTA. The model was converted into a numerical score ("IMA-PLUS Score") and validated in two retrospective cohorts. Discrimination, calibration, and risk group thresholds were assessed. In validation cohorts, freedom from AAA expansion and EL2 associated reinterventions up to 5 years were analysed. RESULTS: Data from 245 patients of the ZEPHYR registry were included. EL2 occurred in 96 patients (39.2%). The IMA-PLUS Score includes inferior mesenteric artery diameter, number of infrarenal renal pole arteries, number of patent lumbar arteries, and median sacral artery patency, achieving a crossvalidated area under the curve (AUC) of 0.78. Using prespecified thresholds (low < 128, medium 128 - 200, high > 200), observed EL2 incidences in ZEPHYR were 19%, 59%, and 74%. In the Heidelberg cohort (n = 134; EL2 44%), AUC was 0.77 (95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.69 - 0.85) with EL2 incidences of 24%, 60%, and 89% across risk groups with good calibration; interobserver agreement for total score was high (intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.95). In the Tokyo cohort (n = 123; EL2 52.8%) AUC was 0.75 (95% CI 0.67 - 0.84); EL2 incidences were 36%, 76%, and 80%, with higher observed incidence than predicted. In validation cohorts, the IMA-PLUS Score was associated with AAA expansion and reduced freedom from EL2 associated reinterventions. CONCLUSION: The IMA-PLUS Score may support selection of patients for future studies on preventive management strategies.

In this study, a computed tomography angiography (CTA) based risk score was developed and validated to predict EL2 after EVAR. METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective diagnostic study used prospectively collected data from the Zenith alpha for aneurysm Repair Registry (ZEPHYR) as the development cohort.

articles.title: Fenestrated-Branched Endovascular versus Open Surgical Repair for Elective Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study compared outcomes between patients undergoing elective open surgical repair (OSR) and fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR) for thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) through a systematic review and meta-analysis. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane. REVIEW METHODS: A total of 5 980 articles were screened following the PRISMA protocol. Primary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital major adverse events (MAEs) and mortality, and late all cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia, stroke, bowel ischaemia, and new onset dialysis, as well as late re-interventions. A DerSimonian-Laird random effects model was employed to calculate risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for binary endpoints. Significance was defined as a p value of . Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and evidence certainty with GRADE. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 A total of 1 567 patients from five retrospective observational comparative studies were included. FBEVAR was used to treat TAAA in 824 patients (52.6%). Thirty day MAEs (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.34 - 0.78; p = .002; I= 77.0%), mortality (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37 - 0.97; p = .040; I= 29.0%), and dialysis (RR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06 - 0.54; p = .002; I= 80.0%) were significantly less frequent among patients undergoing FBEVAR. Conversely, late aortic related re-interventions were significantly more common in the elective FBEVAR cohort (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.04 - 3.13; p = .040; I= 18.0%). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.51 - 1.91; p = .96; I= 39.0%), bowel ischaemia (RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.09 - 2.33; p = .35; I= 81.0%), and stroke (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.37 - 2.06; p = .76; I= 0.0%), or late mortality (RR 1.29, 95% CI 0.87 - 1.92; p = .20; I= 57.0%). According to GRADE, certainty of evidence was low to very low across outcomes. CONCLUSION: Elective FBEVAR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of thirty day MAEs, mortality, and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis compared with OSR. In contrast, elective OSR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of late aortic related re-interventions, whereas overall re-intervention rates were similar between groups.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: This study compared outcomes between patients undergoing elective open surgical repair (OSR) and fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR) for thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) through a systematic review and meta-analysis. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane. REVIEW METHODS: A total of 5 980 articles were screened following the PRISMA protocol.

articles.title: Feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for nutcracker syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age. To evaluate the feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for NCS in terms of technical completion, conversion to open surgery, perioperative safety, postoperative recovery and symptom relief, and to explore whether heterogeneity was explained by reconstructive technique, age or sample size. Four electronic databases-PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) and the Web of Science Core Collection-were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, and the reference lists of the retrieved articles and of earlier reviews on this topic were screened by hand. Eligible reports were original studies of robot-assisted NCS surgery from which quantitative data could be obtained, provided the series comprised at least three patients; studies of non-robotic procedures, non-NCS cohorts, asymptomatic nutcracker phenomenon, stent implantation by the endovascular route alone, narrative reviews, conference proceedings, single-patient reports and duplicate cohorts were not considered. Screening and data collection were carried out independently by two investigators, and study quality was appraised with the JBI checklist designed for case series. Stata 17.0 was used for the single-arm proportional meta-analyses: individual proportions underwent Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation before being combined under a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with the summary estimates then expressed on the original scale, while continuous variables were harmonised to mean ± SD following Wan et al. and Shi et al. Cochran's Q test and the I-squared statistic were used to quantify heterogeneity. Subgroup comparisons were restricted to outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and were interpreted as exploratory analyses of study-level variation rather than as tests of independent effects. Ten studies comprising 140 patients were included (China, 4; USA, 4; France, 2; 9 retrospective and 1 prospective). Reconstructive techniques were left renal vein (LRV) transposition (5 studies, 45 patients), extravascular renal vein stent placement (3 studies, 29 patients) and renal autotransplantation (2 studies, 66 patients). Completion and conversion status could be ascertained in 111 patients from eight studies: 110 (99.1%) completed the planned reconstruction robotically and 1 (0.9%) was converted to open surgery; status was not reported for 29 patients in two studies and these patients were not counted as zero events. The pooled symptom improvement rate was 96% (95% CI 85%-100%; I-squared = 46.66%; 6 studies, 87 patients) and the complete symptom resolution rate 69% (95% CI 34%-96%; I-squared = 77.83%; 4 studies, 35 patients). The pooled incidence of Clavien-Dindo < 3 complications was 17% (95% CI 5%-33%; I-squared = 60.86%) and that of Clavien-Dindo >= 3 complications was 5.5% (95% CI 2.3%-9.8%; I-squared = 0%; 8 studies, 6 events); lymphorrhea/chylous ascites occurred in 15% (95% CI 0%-43%; I-squared = 79.16%) and postoperative reintervention in 3% (95% CI 0%-10%; I-squared = 0%). Pooled operating time was 204.52 min (95% CI 157.47-251.57 min; I-squared = 99.1%), estimated blood loss 54.21 mL (95% CI 37.56-70.86 mL; I-squared = 96.2%) and postoperative length of stay 2.72 days (95% CI 1.60-3.85 days; I-squared = 96.2%). Exploratory technique-stratified analyses suggested lower estimated blood loss, shorter operating time and shorter length of stay after extravascular stent placement than after LRV transposition or renal autotransplantation; however, several strata contained only one or two studies and these differences are descriptive rather than evidence of comparative superiority. Robotic-assisted surgery for NCS was associated with a high rate of technical completion among patients with ascertainable status, favourable symptom improvement and a low frequency of major complications. The apparent ordering of perioperative burden across techniques is consistent with differences in procedural invasiveness but may also reflect confounding by indication, centre effects and case selection. Owing to the single-arm design, short and inconsistent follow-up, absent patency data and very low certainty, these findings should be regarded as a pooled feasibility benchmark rather than as evidence of comparative effectiveness.
articles.englishSummary: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age.

articles.title: Acute aortic syndrome rule-out criteria: development and external validation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a rare but catastrophic event, presenting with non-specific symptoms that mimic common conditions, and carries a mortality approaching 80% when missed. Current clinical tools, including the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score (ADD-RS) and its refinement, the simplified AORTA score, achieve high sensitivity when combined with D-dimer but fail to identify a population at sufficiently low risk to safely avoid further testing. To address this gap, the Acute Aortic Syndrome Rule-Out Criteria (ARC) were developed and validated, a pragmatic bedside tool designed to safely exclude AAS in low-risk patients without additional testing. METHODS: A retrospective multistep derivation and validation study was conducted. The derivation cohort included patients with confirmed AAS from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD). Starting from existing scores, candidate predictors were identified from the IRAD dataset and sequentially added to achieve sensitivity ≥ 99%. External validation was performed in patients with suspected AAS across three prospective multicentre cohorts (ADvISED, PROFUNDUS, and DAShED). Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: The final seven-variable ARC included age >60 years, abrupt onset pain, severe pain, hypotension/shock, neurological deficit, pulse deficit, and known aortic disease. Patients were classified as positive if any ARC variable was present and negative only if all variables were absent. In the derivation cohort, ARC achieved a sensitivity of 99.2% (95% CI 99.1-99.3). In the ADvISED/PROFUNDUS cohort (4598 patients, 10.2% AAS prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100) with specificity 23.7% (95% CI 22.4-25.0). In the DAShED cohort (5346 patients, 0.3% prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 76.8-100) and specificity 36.4% (95% CI 35.1-37.7), ruling out 36.3% of patients without missing any AAS cases. CONCLUSIONS: ARC is an externally validated, pragmatic clinical rule demonstrating high diagnostic sensitivity in a large external validation cohort. When incorporated into existing diagnostic pathways, ARC has the potential to reduce unnecessary testing while maintaining diagnostic performance. Further prospective validation is required to confirm its clinical utility.

articles.title: Epigenome-Wide Association Study of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Identifies Central Role for Inflammatory Pathways.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Epigenetic mechanisms underlying susceptibility to abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) remain poorly understood. Identifying causal DNA methylation markers for AAA can elucidate the regulatory processes that drive aneurysm formation and accelerate translational applications. We leveraged the Veterans Affairs (VA) Million Veteran Program to identify methylation biomarkers and delineate underlying pathways. METHODS: We first conducted an epigenome-wide association study of incident AAA (1324 cases and 42 065 noncases), performed stratified analyses by population group and smoking status, and conducted Mendelian randomization to facilitate causal inference of the cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG)-AAA association. Chromatin state, island context, and transcription factor binding were implicated through functional annotation of identified CpGs. To identify genes impacted by change in methylation state, we aligned associations with transcriptional data obtained in blood, aorta, and liver. We performed expression quantitative trait methylation to capture CpG-gene-expression links across the genome. Network Mendelian randomization was used to test cardiometabolic and inflammatory mediation. Finally, we developed a methylation risk score for AAA using penalized regression and evaluated its performance against a clinical model in the Million Veteran Program and 2 external studies. RESULTS: AGER, C2 DDR1 LDLR TRIB1 Epigenome-wide association study identified 1253 CpGs associated with incident AAA, and Mendelian randomization supported a putative causal role for 143 of these associations. Functional annotation pointed to predominantly distal, enhancer-centered regulation and enrichment of inflammatory transcription factor programs (eg, activator protein-1 and nuclear factor κB). This distal architecture was consistent with expression quantitative trait methylation results, which showed a larger number of trans associations. Among 143 CpGs associated with AAA in Mendelian randomization analyses, we identified 213 CpG-gene expression pairs with strong colocalization support, including, and. Multi-trait colocalization further prioritized 8 CpG-gene expression-AAA links with evidence of a shared genetic signal. Network Mendelian randomization identified 135 putative mediation pathways linking CpGs to AAA, including 58 via cardiometabolic traits and 77 via inflammation-related traits. Blood lipid traits mediated >40% of the associations between AAA risk and CpGs near(cg19305903) and(cg14128479). Among inflammation-related mediators, circulating DAG1, NEXN, MMP9, IL1RN, and MMP13 were prioritized as potential intermediates. Additionally, a CpG selection process was used to develop a methylation risk score for AAA, which strongly associated with disease in both the discovery cohort and 2 external validation cohorts, even after adjustment for a full suite of clinical covariates. CONCLUSIONS: This study identified putative causal DNA methylation markers for AAA, and multi-omics analyses implicate activator protein-1-linked inflammatory transcriptional programs, blood lipids, and multiple inflammation-related proteins as key pathways underlying methylation-associated AAA risk.

articles.title: The Association Between Hospital Comprehensive Stroke Center Designation Status and Stroke Rate Reporting in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Implications for Hospital Performance Assessment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Michigan Structural Heart Consortium showed that transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) stroke rates were associated with hospital Comprehensive Stroke Center (CSC) designation, suggesting that hospital structural factors affect stroke reporting. We sought to determine whether CSC designation is nationally associated with reported stroke rates and the potential impact on hospital performance and Transcatheter Valve Therapy National Data Registry (TVTR) public reporting. METHODS: Consecutive TVTR cases from January 2016 through June 2023 were included, excluding sites reporting to the TVTR <1 year or performing <20 total TAVR procedures. The primary outcome was in-hospital stroke rate. Secondary outcomes were disabling stroke and 30-day stroke. Major bleeding, death, acute renal failure, and a composite end point were falsification end points to determine whether CSC status was uniquely associated with stroke. Multivariable hierarchical models were created starting with patient covariates and sequentially adding hospital variables to account for determinants of stroke. The impact of CSC status on hospital performance was estimated by correcting CSC hospital stroke rates in the validated TVTR 30-day composite model. RESULTS: P P P P P A total of 525 919 TAVRs at 800 sites were included, and 10 963 strokes (2.1%) were reported within 30 days: 8284 (1.6%) in-hospital and 2679 (0.5%) after discharge. A total of 4733 (0.9%) were disabling strokes. Multivariate analysis showed that CSC status and participation in TAVR trials were independent predictors of in-hospital stroke rate (=0.033 and 0.012) and disabling stroke (=0.033 and 0.007), but not falsification end points (=NS). Participation in TAVR trials and operator volume were independent predictors of 30-day stroke (=0.039 and=0.041). The impact of CSC status on the 30-day composite model showed performance improvement for 8 of 153 CSC hospitals. CONCLUSIONS: CSC hospital status and participation in TAVR trials are significant predictors unique for stroke. Correcting for the association of CSC status on stroke rate resulted in an estimated 8 of 153 hospitals improving their TVTR 30-day composite model performance. Further work is needed to account for potential ascertainment bias for stroke in public reporting.

articles.title: The complexity of provoked venous thromboembolism: one treatment plan does not fit all.
articles.abstract: The decision of whether to continue patients diagnosed with venous thromboembolism (VTE) on anticoagulation after the initial treatment period is often nuanced. Many patients will have ≥1 transient risk factor associated with a time-limited increased risk of VTE. Transient risk factors are further divided into major factors, such as joint replacement, or minor factors, such as prolonged travel, which determine the magnitude of risk for an initial VTE. In addition, major transient risk factors generally carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE than minor transient risk factors. However, many patients will also have ≥1 persistent VTE risk factor, which further increase the risk for recurrence. Some persistent risk factors, such as inflammatory bowel disease, are associated with a sufficiently high risk of recurrent VTE, for which guidelines recommend indefinite anticoagulation. There are multiple other persistent risk factors that carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE, such as chronic renal insufficiency and obesity. The HI-PRO (High-Risk Patients with Provoked Venous Thromboembolism) trial sought to assess the efficacy and safety of extended thromboprophylaxis for the prevention of recurrent VTE in patients with an initial provoked VTE and at least 1 persistent risk factor. The study found a lower risk of recurrent VTE in the thromboprophylaxis cohort, challenging the traditional time-limited treatment for provoked VTE, but heterogeneity of the study population and small sample size preclude identification of which subsets of patients could safely discontinue anticoagulation. We consider the conundrum of provoked VTE in this review.

articles.title: Association of Multimodal Collateral Profiles with Outcomes After Large Core Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives Methods Results Conclusions p p p : Cerebral collateral circulation markers in large core thrombectomy and their impact on functional outcomes have not been extensively reported.: We retrospectively analyzed health system medical records of large core (Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score <6 and/or computed tomography perfusion [CTP] cerebral blood flow <30% volume ≥50 milliliters [mL]) thrombectomy patients over a 19-month period. A good collateral profile (CCC+) was defined as the combination of computed tomography angiography Tan arterial score ≥2 and CTP cerebral blood volume index (CBVI) ≥0.8. A poor profile (CCC-) was defined as Tan <2 and CBVI <0.8. All others were categorized as having a mixed profile (CCC±). Multivariable Firth's penalized logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with the primary outcome, 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-3.: 88 patients with median (interquartile range, IQR) age 65.5 (56.5-77.5) years and core volume 78 (55-116) mL were included. Forty-seven patients (53.4%) had poor collateral profiles, 31 (35.2%) were classified as CCC±, and 10 (11.4%) as CCC+. In the multivariable Firth's penalized logistic regression model, CCC+ patients had higher odds of achieving a 90-day mRS of 0-3 compared with CCC- patients, though the difference was not statistically significant (odds ratio [OR] 1.117, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.235-5.311,= 0.889). No significant difference was observed between CCC± and CCC- patients (OR 0.869, 95% CI 0.293-2.577,= 0.800). Glucose was the only factor independently associated with 90-day outcomes (OR 0.742, 95% CI 0.602-0.915,= 0.005).: No independent association was detected between favorable or mixed cerebral collateral circulation and 90-day mRS 0-3 after large core thrombectomy, though the study was underpowered for the CCC+ comparison. Presenting glucose may inform the likelihood of achieving independent ambulatory status at 90 days.
