articles.title: Cross-Phenotype Genomics Reveals Heterogeneous Genetic Susceptibility Architecture Relevant to Menopause.
articles.abstract: Background Methods Results Conclusions p F5 F2 -5 : Menopause is accompanied by substantial interindividual variation in hormonal, metabolic, cardiovascular, skeletal, and thrombotic phenotypes. Although the genetics of reproductive ageing and individual menopause-associated traits are increasingly characterised, the cross-phenotype architecture of individual menopause-relevant germline variants remains less well defined.: We performed a variant-centred genomic analysis of 31 prespecified menopause-relevant germline variants. Cross-trait evidence comprised 766 variant-trait records across 52 phenotypes and was integrated with a targeted Pan-UK Biobank phenome-wide association study (PheWAS; 1462 tests across 57 endpoints), clinically relevant outcome analyses, linkage disequilibrium assessment, FinnGen R12 venous thromboembolism (VTE) associations, regional fine-mapping, and molecular annotation. Association strength, between-study heterogeneity, phenotypic breadth and sharing, and locus resolution were evaluated as distinct evidence dimensions.: In total, 25 of 31 variants showed at least one cross-trait association at< 1 × 10and 21 reached genome-wide significance. Phenotypic breadth varied markedly, from restricted profiles to 16 associated phenotypes, and strong associations frequently coexisted with substantial between-study heterogeneity. In Pan-UK Biobank, 222 associations involving 25 variants met false-discovery-rate correction, spanning hormonal, reproductive, cardiometabolic, skeletal, nutritional, hepatic, and neurological phenotypes. Cross-phenotype reconstruction identified recurrent connectivity through sex hormone-binding globulin, testosterone, adiposity, lipid, and skeletal traits, while linkage disequilibrium analyses distinguished phenotypic sharing from genetic redundancy. Clinically,rs6025 andrs1799963 showed strong VTE associations in FinnGen (OR 2.387 and 1.921, respectively), but markedly different locus resolution: rs6025 had posterior inclusion probability (PIP) 0.979 and constituted a single-variant 95% credible set, whereas rs1799963 had PIP 0.596 within a four-variant credible set.: Menopause-relevant germline variation exhibits heterogeneous cross-phenotype architectures in which association strength, phenotypic breadth, between-study consistency, genetic independence, and locus resolution are not interchangeable. This variant-centred framework provides a basis for evaluating inherited susceptibility relevant to menopause and hormone exposure, while prospective individual-level studies remain necessary before translation into risk prediction or treatment selection.

articles.title: Urgent Endovascular Treatment of a Pancreatitis-Related Pseudoaneurysm Identified on Follow-Up CT.
articles.abstract: Visceral artery pseudoaneurysm (VA-PSA) is an uncommon but life-threatening complication of acute-on-chronic pancreatitis, particularly in the presence of walled-off necrosis (WON). Early radiological recognition is essential because of the high risk of rupture. We present the case of a 51-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis who developed a pseudoaneurysm arising from the proper hepatic artery within a pancreatic head necrotic collection. Follow-up contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a new arterial-phase enhancing focus within the WON. Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) confirmed the pseudoaneurysm, which was successfully excluded with a covered stent placed via a right transfemoral approach. Post-procedural recovery was uneventful, and short-term follow-up CT showed persistent exclusion of the lesion.

articles.title: Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups. RESULTS: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

articles.title: Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Isolated Native Aortic Regurgitation: National Propensity-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is well established for aortic stenosis, while its application for isolated native aortic regurgitation (AR) was previously off label and technically challenging. Comparative data between TAVR and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are limited. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient characteristics and outcomes of off-label TAVR vs SAVR among patients with isolated native AR. METHODS: Using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Provider Analysis and Review database, patients ≥65 years of age who underwent TAVR or SAVR for isolated native AR (2017-2023) were identified. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to evaluate short- and long-term outcomes. Fine-Gray models accounted for death as a competing risk, reported as subdistribution HRs (SHRs). RESULTS: Among 9,859 patients, 1,742 propensity score-matched pairs were included, with balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 75.8 years vs 75.7 years; female sex 517 of 1,742 [29.7%] vs 528 of 1,742 [30.3%]). In the matched cohort, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization (OR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.28-0.39; P < 0.001) and lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-1.00; P = 0.048) but higher 30-day pacemaker implantation (OR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.33-2.25; P < 0.001). Through 5 years (median follow-up 2.58 years), TAVR was associated with increased repeat aortic valve replacement (SHR: 2.04; 95% CI: 1.13-3.66) but similar all-cause mortality (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.98-1.31) and heart failure-related readmission (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.98-1.21) between treatment strategies. CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization and comparable 5-year survival as SAVR, although pacemaker and long-term reinterventions rates were higher.

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses. METHODS: This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as <2+ (none/trace or mild) or ≥2+ (mild-moderate or worse) based on separation of Kaplan-Meier curves for the primary outcome. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure hospitalization up to 2 years. Propensity score-weighted Cox regression was used to estimate the independent impact of PVR severity on clinical outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with <2+ PVR. After propensity score weighting, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted HR: 3.77; 95% CI: 2.88-4.95), as well as higher risks of all-cause death, mainly cardiovascular, and heart failure hospitalization. These findings were consistent across both classical and paradoxical LFLG-AS phenotypes. CONCLUSIONS: In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.

articles.title: Prevalence and Consequences of Guideline-Directed Indications for Aortic Valve Replacement in the EARLY TAVR Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association valvular heart disease guidelines were published before several recent trials that provide greater support for early intervention in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the prevalence and clinical impact of American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Class II recommendations for AVR in the EARLY TAVR trial. METHODS: The EARLY TAVR trial randomized patients with asymptomatic severe AS to transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance (CS) with conversion to TAVR based on development of ACC/AHA Class I indications. Patients in the intention-to-treat cohort were stratified by presence of a Class II indication for AVR at randomization. The primary endpoint of the present analysis was the composite of all-cause death, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Interaction tests were performed to assess whether the treatment effect differed by level of guideline recommendation. Timing of conversion to AVR in the CS group according to the presence/absence of Class II indications was also assessed. RESULTS: interaction Of the 901 patients randomized to TAVR (N = 445) and CS (N = 446), 636 (70.6%) patients had no guideline recommendation, and 265 (29.4%) had at least1 1 Class II recommendation for AVR at the time of randomization. At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, patients with a Class II indication for AVR experienced higher rates of the primary endpoint (Class II: 24.5% vs no recommendation: 14.5%; HR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.30-2.44; P < 0.001) and were more likely to have acute valve syndrome at the time of conversion. Compared with CS, the relative benefit of early TAVR on the primary endpoint was similar regardless of the presence or absence of a Class II guideline recommendation (HR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.37-1.02 vs 0.61; 95% CI: 0.40-0.92; P= 0.96). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients in the EARLY TAVR trial, Class II indications for AVR were present in almost one-third of patients at baseline. The benefit of early TAVR was consistent regardless of the presence or absence of Class II indications. These findings support the strategy of early TAVR over CS in asymptomatic patients with severe AS, independent of guideline indications. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03042104; Unique Identifier: NCT03042104.

articles.title: Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch and Patient-Centered Outcomes After TAVR.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement has been widely studied for its association with clinical outcomes, but its effect on patient-reported health status remains less defined. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between PPM severity and health status through 3-year follow-up after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SCOPE I (Safety and Efficacy of the ACURATE Neo/TF Compared to the SAPIEN 3 Bioprosthesis) randomized trial categorized patients according to PPM severity using Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. Endpoints included survival and patient-reported health status, with an integrated outcome defined as being alive with good health status (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score ≥75 without a decline of >10 points from baseline). RESULTS: Among 662 patients, moderate and severe PPM occurred in 184 (27.8%) and 69 (10.4%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 1 and 3 years was 7.0% and 20.5%, with no differences across PPM categories. Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score was similar through 1 year but lower at 3 years in patients with severe vs no PPM (median 71.1 vs 83.9; P = 0.027). Fewer patients with severe PPM were alive with good health status at 3 years (30.6% vs 49.4%; P = 0.021). In multivariable analysis, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of the integrated outcome (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.27-0.96; P = 0.036), but this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for 30-day mitral regurgitation (OR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.30-1.15; P = 0.121). CONCLUSIONS: Among survivors, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of good health status at 3 years. This association was attenuated after accounting for 30-day residual mitral regurgitation, suggesting a possible contributory role. Given the post hoc design, the findings are hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Cardiac Damage and Clinical Outcomes in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The extent of cardiac damage in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with worse clinical outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the clinical impact of cardiac damage using the updated criteria incorporating the echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension. METHODS: This post hoc subanalysis of LANDMARK trial, which randomized 768 patients with severe AS to the Myval transcatheter heart valve (THV) series or to contemporary THVs (Sapien and Evolut series), used updated cardiac damage classification: stage 0, no cardiac damage; stage 1, left ventricular damage; stage 2, left atrial or mitral valve damage; stage 3, pulmonary artery or tricuspid valve damage; and stage 4, right ventricular damage. The impact of cumulative cardiac damage, defined as meeting all criteria for stages 1 to 4, was also assessed. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Cardiac damage stages were assessed in 596 patients (stage 0, n = 36; stage 1, n = 88; stage 2, n = 284; stage 3, n = 84; stage 4, n = 104), with a mean age of 80.2 (5.7) years and a mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score of 3.3% (2.4%). One-year mortality was 0%, 1.1%, 4.7%, 7.2%, and 20.4% in stages 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (log-rank P < 0.001). The area under the curve for predicting 1-year mortality was 0.739. Patients with cumulative cardiac damage had the highest mortality (23.6%). In the multivariable analysis, stage 4 was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality. CONCLUSIONS: The updated cardiac damage staging stratified 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement, highlighting the importance of comprehensive echocardiographic assessment in severe AS. (LANDMARK Trial: a Randomised Controlled Trial of Myval THV [LANDMARK]; NCT04275726).

articles.title: Prognosis of Patients with Delayed Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Rupture after Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Multicentre Retrospective Study in France.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The majority of patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) undergo endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Despite its high overall success rate, EVAR does not eliminate the risk of aneurysm rupture. This study aimed to evaluate the prognosis of patients undergoing surgical management for post-EVAR rupture. METHODS: A multicentre retrospective study of patients who presented with ruptured AAA after successful EVAR between 2007 and 2022 at 22 academic hospitals was conducted. The index EVAR procedures were performed between 2002 and 2020. Data were extracted from electronic hospital records and computed tomography scans. Death during follow up was ascertained using the French register of deceased persons. Survival probabilities at 30, 90, and 365 days were estimated with Kaplan-Meier estimators. Cox proportional hazards survival regression was used to identify determinants associated with increased risk of death. RESULTS: One hundred and nine patients (96 men) were included, with a mean age of 79.1 ± 9 years at the time of rupture. The median time from index EVAR to rupture was 50 months (range 0 - 179 months). Sixty-seven patients had open surgery (of which 37% underwent suprarenal cross clamping), 39 received endovascular treatment, and three underwent hybrid repair. Overall mortality was 26.6% at thirty days, increasing to 33.9% at ninety days, and 41.3% at 1 year. Neither the type of endoleak nor the type of repair was significantly associated with risk of death during follow up. Post-operative complications were frequent, including renal complications (44.0%), major haemorrhage (22.9%), respiratory distress (19.3%), and mesenteric ischaemia (6%). CONCLUSION: This study presented a large multicentre series of patients treated for ruptured AAA after EVAR. Despite considerable progress in stent graft technology, EVAR offers little protection in the event of late rupture, even among patients with type II endoleak only. The mortality rate in this study is within the range of those published based on de novo AAA rupture.

articles.title: Post-approval study preliminary 1-month outcomes of the first 100 patients treated with an off-the-shelf multibranch aortic device.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To report the preliminary 1-month outcomes from the post-approval study of the first 100 patients treated with the GORE® EXCLUDER® Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE). METHODS: This multicenter, nonrandomized, prospective study of the TAMBE aortic component included endovascular repair of an aortic disease involving the visceral vessels. Demographics, core-lab adjudicated imaging characteristics, perioperative metrics, and postoperative 1-month outcomes are reported. RESULTS: The first 100 patients treated were 30% female, 81% white, and the median was age 74 years. Anatomic classifications included 48 patients (49.0%) with Extent I-IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA), 21 (21.4%) with pararenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), 12 (12.2%) with juxtarenal AAA, and 17 patients with post dissection pathology (n=11) or 'other' (n=6). Enrollment and treatment of 45.0% of the patients were at sites without prior TAMBE device experience. Prior aortic surgery was noted in 48.0% of patients treated. For patients with Extent I-III TAAA (n=22), staging of the TAMBE procedure was planned with initial proximal thoracic endovascular aortic repair in 7 patients (31.8%). Median aneurysm diameter was 6.2 cm. The GORE® VIABAHN® VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis was used in all patients, with additional use of a VIABAHN® self-expanding stent in six patients. Intentional non-use of one or more portals (with planned plug occlusion) was a strategy used in 15 (15.0%) patients. Median procedure time was 280 minutes, and median length of stay was four days with 83 patients (83.8%) discharged to home. Branch target vessel technical success rate was 98.9% (average of 1.39 stents into the celiac, 1.44 superior mesenteric artery, 1.62 right renal, and 1.59 left renal per portal). Three patients (3.0%) died, all were procedure related. Major adverse events in 8 patients (8.1%, 3 had ≥1 event) included 1 (1.0%) respiratory failure, 4 (4.0%) permanent paraplegia, 4 (4.0%) renal function decline, and 1 (1.0%) bowel ischemia. No patient experienced a major stroke, aneurysm rupture, or myocardial infarction. A total of eight Type 1c or Type IIIa/IIIc endoleaks were detected in 6 (6.1%) patients. No conversion to open-surgical repair, rupture, or device migration/integrity issues were reported. CONCLUSIONS: The preliminary analysis of the FDA-mandated post-approval study 1-month outcomes in this prospective multicenter cohort treated with the TAMBE device demonstrates applicability to more extensive thoracoabdominal pathology with similar outcomes to the pivotal trial. Distinct findings for the TAMBE device in the real-world include successful treatment of post-dissection aneurysms, increased staging strategies for spinal cord protection with low paraplegia rates, and rapid adoption by many sites that did not participate in the pivotal trial. articles.title: Revascularization Outcomes in Patients with Femoropopliteal Peripheral Artery Disease Presenting with Claudication.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Supervised exercise therapy (SET) and optimal medical therapy (OMT), including smoking cessation, are first-line treatments for claudication. Revascularization is reserved for quality-of-life-limiting symptoms refractory to conservative management; however, the optimal revascularization strategy for femoropopliteal disease remains uncertain. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy (ET) and bypass strategies in patients undergoing revascularization for claudication. METHODS: We analyzed Vascular Quality Initiative data (2016-2024) for patients undergoing first-time elective revascularization for femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease (PAD) presenting with claudication. Three 1:1 propensity score-matched cohorts were constructed: ET vs single-segment great saphenous vein (SSGSV) bypass, ET vs prosthetic graft (PG) bypass, and PG vs SSGSV bypass. The primary outcome was one-year freedom from persistent claudication. Secondary outcomes included one-year loss of patency, reintervention, and all-cause mortality. Outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression. RESULTS: We identified 27,335 patients (30,483 limbs): ET 27,111 (88.9%), SSGSV 1,399 (4.6%), and PG 1,973 (6.5%). Matching yielded 1,294 ET-SSGSV pairs, 1,801 ET-PG pairs, and 1,242 PG-SSGSV pairs with well-balanced baseline characteristics. At one year, symptom-free rates were 92.0% for SSGSV, 90.0% for PG, and 89.6% for ET. Compared with SSGSV, ET was associated with a higher risk of persistent claudication at one-year (HR 1.48; 95% CI 1.10-2.00; P=0.010). No significant differences in one-year symptom relief were observed between ET and PG or between PG and SSGSV. Across all matched comparisons, loss of patency, reintervention, and mortality did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: SET and OMT should remain first-line therapy for claudication. Among patients proceeding to revascularization after unsuccessful conservative care, SSGSV bypass was associated with greater symptom relief than ET at one year, while all strategies achieved high symptom-free rates (≥89%). ET and PG demonstrated comparable outcomes across symptom relief, patency, reintervention, and survival. There were no significant differences between PG and SSGSV. Given vein-preservation considerations and procedural invasiveness in claudication, strategy selection should be individualized to anatomy, comorbidities and patient goals. Prospective studies are needed to clarify long-term durability, and quality-of-life effects.

Revascularization is reserved for quality-of-life-limiting symptoms refractory to conservative management; however, the optimal revascularization strategy for femoropopliteal disease remains uncertain. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy (ET) and bypass strategies in patients undergoing revascularization for claudication.

articles.title: Rapid Endovascular Hemorrhage Control in Trauma: Joint Position Statement from the American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma and the Society of Interventional Radiology.
articles.abstract: Timely hemorrhage control is a critical determinant of survival after traumatic injury, and advances in transarterial embolization have made rapid access to endovascular intervention an increasingly important component of contemporary trauma care. This joint position statement from the American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma and the Society of Interventional Radiology clarifies expectations for interventional radiology under ACS Verification, Review, and Consultation Program Standard 4.15 and provides practical guidance for integrating endovascular hemorrhage control into trauma centers. Standard 4.15 reflects a requirement for system readiness rather than a universal mandate that every vascular intervention begin within 60 minutes. Rapid intervention is expected when clinically indicated, particularly for patients with an endovascular target who are hemodynamically labile, and the relevant performance interval is the time from a shared decision by trauma surgery and interventional radiology to proceed with intervention to arterial puncture. Trauma centers should establish multidisciplinary activation pathways that enable rapid mobilization of personnel and resources while preserving clinical judgment regarding patient selection and competing priorities. Recommended strategies include standardized activation protocols, process mapping, parallel rather than sequential workflows, early patient transport when appropriate, documentation of key time points, structured debriefing, and continuous performance monitoring. Interventional radiologists should be integrated as essential members of multidisciplinary trauma teams rather than engaged late as procedural consultants. Applying the 60-minute expectation according to clinical urgency and monitoring decision-to-puncture time focuses Standard 4.15 on its intended objectives: institutional readiness, timely definitive hemorrhage control in appropriately selected high-risk patients, and continuous performance improvement.

articles.title: 5-Year Follow-Up of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With Self-Expanding Intra-Annular Versus Commercially Available Valves.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term outcomes of the self-expanding intra-annular Portico transcatheter aortic valve are not known. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to report the 5-year outcomes of the PORTICO IDE randomized controlled trial. METHODS: This multicenter trial randomized (1:1) patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis at high/extreme surgical risk to transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with the self-expanding intra-annular valve (study valve) or Food and Drug Administration-approved commercially available valves (CAVs; balloon-expandable or self-expanding supra-annular platforms). Assessments of the primary safety endpoint (30 days) and the primary efficacy endpoint (1 year) have been previously reported. Prespecified clinical outcomes and hemodynamic valve parameters are presented through 5 years. RESULTS: 2 We randomized 750 eligible patients (mean age: 83 years, 52.7% female) to the study valve (n = 381) or CAV (n = 369). Compared with CAV, the study valve showed similar 5-year all-cause mortality or stroke (55.6% vs 51.3%, P = 0.42). Cardiovascular mortality was numerically higher in the study valve group compared with the CAV group (33.4% vs 25.8%; P = 0.06). Naïve permanent pacemaker implantation was higher in the study valve group (36.6%) than the CAV group (20.3%; P < 0.0001) at 5 years. At 5 years, the study valve showed a lower mean transvalvular gradient (7.2 ± 3.0 vs 9.5 ± 6.5 mm Hg, P = 0.008), but similar valve area (1.78 ± 0.45 vs 1.71 ± 0.51 cm, P = 0.40) compared to CAV. CONCLUSIONS: In patients at high or extreme surgical risk, TAVR with the self-expanding intra-annular transcatheter heart valve had similar 5-year overall survival, stroke rates, and valve function compared with commercially available valves.

articles.title: 2 Zero-Iodinated-Contrast CO-Guided Atherectomy for Superficial Femoral Artery Chronic Total Occlusions in Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Materials and Methods: Results: Conclusions: 2 2 2 2 2 Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) who undergo complex femoropopliteal endovascular interventions are at heightened risk of contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI). This study assessed technical feasibility, short-term creatinine-based renal outcomes, and clinical outcomes of a zero-iodinated-contrast, carbon dioxide (CO)-guided atherectomy approach for chronic total occlusions (CTOs) of the superficial femoral artery (SFA).In this retrospective, single-center analysis, 25 non-dialysis patients with CKD underwent CO-only angiography-guided atherectomy for SFA CTOs. Renal function, procedural characteristics, distal embolization, limb-related outcomes, and duplex ultrasound-defined patency were evaluated. Serum creatinine was measured at baseline and within 48 h after the procedure.The mean age was 65.4 ± 9.8 years, and 36% of patients presented with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). Baseline serum creatinine was 2.16 ± 0.44 mg/dL, and the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was 29.5 ± 9.1 mL/min/1.73 m; 56% of patients had Stage 4 CKD. Technical success was achieved in all procedures. Cumulative CO-volume data were available for 24 patients, with a mean volume of 98.8 ± 37.6 mL, and the mean procedure duration was 38.2 ± 17.2 min. Distal embolization occurred in 20% of patients (5/25), including one event requiring catheter-directed thrombolysis; all embolic events were treated endovascularly, with near-complete recanalization in the thrombolysis case. Mean serum creatinine changed by -0.016 ± 0.086 mg/dL, and no creatinine-defined AKI was observed within the available 48-h assessment. No patient required initiation of dialysis. Follow-up outcomes were available for 24 of 25 patients (96%); one patient was lost to follow-up. Over a mean follow-up period of 26 months (with incompletely reconstructed surveillance), no duplex-defined restenosis, recurrent CTO, or target lesion revascularization (TLR) was documented among patients with available follow-up imaging; this is a descriptive observation within the available follow-up and does not establish universal or long-term freedom from restenosis.A zero-iodinated-contrast, CO-guided atherectomy strategy appears technically feasible for SFA CTO revascularization in patients with advanced CKD and was associated with observed short-term creatinine stability within the available 48-h assessment in this small retrospective cohort. These preliminary observations require validation in larger, prospective, controlled studies.

articles.title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial.
articles.abstract: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during endovascular treatment (EVT) may increase first-pass recanalization and dissolve microcirculatory thrombi, but its efficacy and safety are uncertain. We hypothesised that this strategy would improve functional outcomes versus EVT alone. This phase 3, randomised, adaptive-enrichment, open-label, blinded-endpoint multicentre study aims to evaluate whether intra‑arterial tenecteplase improves clinical outcomes for patients with acute ischemic stroke. Patients with large‑vessel occlusion eligible for EVT within 24 hours of symptom onset were randomly assigned (1:1) to the tenecteplase group receiving intra‑arterial tenecteplase during EVT or the control group receiving EVT alone. The primary endpoint was favorable functional outcome. Of 380 randomised patients (192 in the tenecteplase group and 188 in the control group), primary outcome data were available for 190 and 186 patients, respectively. Favorable 90-day functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) occurred in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 46.8% of the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 0.76, [95% CI 0.50-1.14], P = 0.19). This work suggests intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy did not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population. (Funded by National Science and Technology Major Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657444).

articles.title: The effect of renal denervation on blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease (RDN-CKD Study): Results of a multicentre, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled and blinded investigator-initiated trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular ultrasound renal denervation (uRDN) offers the opportunity to modulate sympathetic nervous system activity, thereby lowering blood pressure (BP) and potentially improving or stabilizing renal outcomes. OBJECTIVE: We hypothesized that in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension, endovascular ultrasound-based RDN will lower BP after 6 months. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, blinded, clinical trial, investigated the effects of uRDN or sham in patients with CKD stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension. The primary and secondary endpoints were changes in ambulatory BP (ABP) and office BP at 6 months. The study was prematurely stopped due to slow enrollment. RESULTS: Twenty subjects (uRDN: N  = 10, sham: N  = 10) completed the 6-month visit. At 6 months, the sham-corrected change from baseline in 24 h systolic ABP was -5.60 mmHg (95% CI -10.7, -0.54 mmHg; P  = 0.170). The sham corrected change from baseline in 24-h diastolic ABP was -5.90 mmHg (95% CI -9.25, -2.55; P  = 0.035) and from baseline daytime ABP -6.85 mmHg (95% CI -10.6, -3.08; P  = 0.030). Sensitivity analysis restricting the analysis to those patients who were fully adherent to medication ( N  = 7 in each group) found a sham-corrected change from baseline 24-h diastolic ABP of -5.71 mmHg (95% CI -9.40, -2.03; P  = 0.053) at 6 months. Based on the composite endpoint of 24 h ABP and office BP for systolic/diastolic BP, a win ratio of 1.71 (95% 1.26-2.34; P  = 0.014) was found for systolic BP and a win ratio of 4.59 (95% CI 2.94-7.16, P  < 0.001) was found for diastolic BP, indicating significant changes in BP following RDN. Estimated glomerular filtration rate remained stable over 6 months, with no difference between the groups. There were no safety signals associated with uRDN. CONCLUSIONS: This prospective randomized, sham controlled, blinded trial in patients with uncontrolled hypertension and CKD was prematurely stopped, resulted in small number of patients and we did not find a statistically significant effect on systolic BP, whereas a consistent reduction in diastolic BP following uRDN was observed. These data should guide the design of a larger confirmatory trial in patients with CKD.

articles.title: Pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular dysfunction in hemodialysis: an overlooked cardiorenal interface and a target for dialysis prescription.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension is an under-recognized cardiovascular complication of advanced chronic kidney disease, especially in maintenance hemodialysis. It links kidney failure, chronic volume stress, left-heart disease, pulmonary vascular remodeling, arteriovenous access flow, and right-ventricular dysfunction. This review frames pulmonary hypertension as central to the cardiorenal interface in hemodialysis and summarizes epidemiology, prognosis, mechanisms, diagnosis, and phenotyping. Echocardiography is the main screening tool, but pressure estimates should be interpreted according to dialysis timing and volume status. Right-heart catheterization remains essential to define phenotype and guide management. Treatment should target modifiable drivers: euvolemia without excessive ultrafiltration, optimized left-heart disease care, assessment of high-flow vascular access, and treatment of respiratory or hematologic contributors. Empirical pulmonary arterial hypertension-specific therapy should be avoided without hemodynamic confirmation. Pulmonary-artery denervation is promising in heart-failure pulmonary hypertension with mild to moderate CKD, but its role in hemodialysis remains unknown.

articles.title: Discontinuation of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors before non-cardiac surgery: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The best management approach for renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitor use before surgery is controversial. Some studies have suggested that continuation could increase the risk of clinically significant peri-operative hypotension and, thus, organ injury. By contrast, others believe that withholding them significantly increases the risk of severe hypertension and heart failure. To determine the most effective strategy, this systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials compared discontinuation vs continuation of RAS inhibitors in patients undergoing non-cardiac and non-vascular surgeries. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) databases were searched for randomized controlled trials that compared discontinuation vs continuation of RAS inhibitors in patients undergoing non-cardiac and non-vascular surgery. RESULTS: Five randomized controlled trials (n = 10 773 patients; 5388 randomized to discontinuation) were included. Discontinuation of an RAS inhibitor probaby reduced peri-operative hypotension (27.66% vs 34.06%; risk ratio [RR] 0.81, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.73-0.89; moderate certainty). The evidence is very uncertain about effects on peri-operative hypertension (9.46% vs 8.05%; RR 1.38, 95% CI 0.66-2.89; very low certainty). For major clinical outcomes, discontinuation suggested little to no difference in acute kidney injury (10.45% vs 10.69%; RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.66-1.45; low certainty), acute heart failure (5.38% vs 5.32%; RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.76-1.31; low certainty), myocardial infarction (1.22% vs 1.00%; RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.60-2.39; low certainty), stroke (0.42% vs 0.40%; RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.56-1.93; low certainty), and arrhythmias (1.80% vs 1.40%; RR 1.28, 95% CI 0.69-2.38; low certainty). CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that discontinuation of RAS inhibitors is likely to reduce peri-operative hypotension in patients undergoing non-cardiac, non-vascular surgery, but the evidence is very uncertain about effects on peri-operative hypertension and major clinical outcomes.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The best management approach for renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitor use before surgery is controversial. Some studies have suggested that continuation could increase the risk of clinically significant peri-operative hypotension and, thus, organ injury. By contrast, others believe that withholding them significantly increases the risk of severe hypertension and heart failure.

articles.title: Staphylococcus aureus Rapid Infrarenal Aortic Rupture During Persistent Methicillin-SusceptibleBacteraemia: Serial CT Evolution and Staged Endovascular Treatment-A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance Case Presentation Conclusions Staphylococcus aureus S. aureus 2 : Persistentbacteraemia can seed an atherosclerotic aorta. Early CT may show only wall thickening and periaortic inflammation, mimicking a degenerative penetrating aortic ulcer (PAU) when no ulcer crater is visible.: An 80-year-old woman (BMI 19.5 kg/m) presented with hypogastric and lumbar pain. Multiphasic CT showed a calcified infrarenal aorta with periaortic inflammation but no haemorrhage. Blood cultures obtained on two occasions confirmed persistent methicillin-susceptiblebacteraemia. Interval CT angiography showed an enhancing circumferential cuff and a small anterior contrast focus without a definite ulcer crater. Eight days after the initial CT, hypotension developed; CT angiography showed focal aortic wall disruption, active extravasation, and a large retroperitoneal haematoma. Emergency aorto-bi-iliac EVAR controlled the bleeding. An inferior mesenteric artery-fed type II endoleak filled the fresh rupture cavity and was treated by coil embolisation via mesenteric collaterals. One-month CTA showed a patent graft without endoleak. At six weeks, the patient remained clinically well with healed wounds and no need for further vascular intervention. CRP fell from 148.1 mg/L on postoperative day 5 to 49.4 mg/L at six weeks and 24.2 mg/L at approximately 12 weeks; the next outpatient review was scheduled in three months, although microbiological clearance remained undocumented.: Serial imaging and persistent MSSA bacteraemia support probable infective aortitis with focal wall disruption; an infected degenerative PAU remains possible. Persistent bacteraemia, focal pain, and a progressive periaortic cuff should prompt early vascular review and short-interval imaging.

articles.title: Associations between Antidiabetic Drug Classes and Aortic Aneurysm Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a potentially life threatening condition that often remains asymptomatic for prolonged periods. Although type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) increases cardiovascular risk, epidemiological studies have paradoxically reported a lower incidence of AA in patients with T2DM. Antidiabetic therapies may contribute to this inverse association, but class specific effects remain unclear. This study evaluated associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA. METHODS: This was a nationwide, population based, retrospective cohort study of adults with T2DM in Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database between 2009 and 2022. Associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models with time varying medication exposure, adjusted for demographic characteristics, diabetes severity, comorbidities, tobacco related diagnoses, and concomitant medications. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were considered exploratory. RESULTS: Among 3 295 564 adults with T2DM (mean age 60.0 years; 52.8% men) followed for 8.5 ± 4.7 years, 45.5% received at least three antidiabetic drug classes. In multivariable time varying Cox models, metformin (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.78, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.75 - 0.82), thiazolidinediones (aHR 0.71, 95% CI 0.65 - 0.77), sulfonylureas/meglitinides (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.78 - 0.85), and α-glucosidase inhibitors (aHR 0.83, 95% CI 0.77 - 0.89) were associated with lower AA risk. DPP-4 inhibitors (aHR 0.95, 95% CI 0.90 - 1.00), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors (aHR 0.90, 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), and glucagon like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) (aHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50 - 0.95) also showed inverse associations, whereas insulin use was associated with higher AA risk (aHR 1.14, 95% CI 1.08 - 1.20). The inverse associations of conventional oral antidiabetic agents remained robust across sensitivity analyses. In contrast, the inverse associations for DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors, and GLP-1RAs were attenuated and no longer statistically significant in patients with an index date from 2011 onward. CONCLUSION: In this nationwide T2DM cohort, conventional oral antidiabetic agents were consistently associated with a lower observed AA risk. Although newer glucose lowering therapies showed similar inverse associations, these findings were less robust and warrant cautious interpretation and prospective confirmation.

Although type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) increases cardiovascular risk, epidemiological studies have paradoxically reported a lower incidence of AA in patients with T2DM. Antidiabetic therapies may contribute to this inverse association, but class specific effects remain unclear.

articles.title: Modelling medial degenerative features by enzymatic digestion to evaluate disease-relevant structure-function relationships in the thoracic aorta.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: To clarify aortic microstructure-function relationships, we used improved, disease-motivated enzymatic digestion models of medial degeneration to evaluate individual extracellular matrix (ECM) components (i.e., elastin, collagen, and proteoglycans) and their influence on biomechanical properties of ascending aortic tissue. METHODS: Thin, 200 µm medial porcine ascending aortic sections were progressively digested with elastase or collagenase for selective degradation of these ECM components. Full thickness human aortic tissues were treated with chondroitinase, hyaluronidase, and heparinase to completely remove proteoglycans. Low- and high-strain modulus, transition-zone behavior, strain-energy density, and energy loss were derived from planar biaxial tensile testing. Degradation of elastin was captured with two photon excitation fluorescence imaging. Degradation of collagen was captured with picrosirius red staining and polarized light microscopy. Proteoglycan content and organization was confirmed by Alcian blue staining. RESULTS: Degradation of elastin fibers reduced low-strain modulus, strain-energy density, transition zone stress, and energy loss. Collagen degradation similarly reduced strain-energy density and decreased strain at the onset of transition, with reductions in high strain modulus and energy loss with increased degradation. Proteoglycan removal decreased energy loss and reduced strain-energy density and strain at onset of transition, and increased high strain modulus. CONCLUSIONS: Through targeted modeling of ECM degenerative features, we have delineated the overlapping effects of major matrix constituents, underscoring the complex, multifactorial nature of structure-function relationships in aortic disease. We also identified multiple microstructural pathways to increasing energy loss and the vulnerability of aortic tissue to failure. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Thoracic aortic dissection results from the progressive degeneration of the aortic wall extracellular matrix, yet the contributions of individual matrix constituents to this mechanical failure remain understudied. To address this gap, we developed a disease-motivated enzymatic model that enables controlled, graded modification of key extracellular matrix constituents in aortic tissue, better replicating the partial degeneration observed in vivo than existing approaches. Using this framework, we systematically evaluated the biomechanical consequences of elastin, collagen, and proteoglycan degeneration. Here, we revealed multiple microstructural pathways to altered viscoelastic behavior, which is associated with increased susceptibility to aortic failure. These findings provide new mechanistic insight into structure-function relationships in aortic disease and help explain how matrix degeneration contributes to tissue vulnerability and dissection risk.

METHODS: Thin, 200 µm medial porcine ascending aortic sections were progressively digested with elastase or collagenase for selective degradation of these ECM components. Full thickness human aortic tissues were treated with chondroitinase, hyaluronidase, and heparinase to completely remove proteoglycans.

articles.title: Intravenous Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke - New Directions.
articles.abstract: In the past 5 years, substantial changes have been made in the use of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Integrating IVT with endovascular thrombectomy, which improves outcomes in patients with stroke due to large cerebral vessel occlusion, has been a particular challenge. This review discusses the underlying vascular targets for IVT and thrombectomy, the increasing use of tenecteplase instead of alteplase, broadening indications for the use of IVT, and ancillary drugs and dosing methods that may augment the success of IVT.

articles.title: Ginkgo biloba Extract for Intermittent Claudication in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives Methods Results Conclusions Ginkgo biloba p p p : Intermittent claudication (IC) secondary to peripheral artery disease (PAD) causes exertional leg pain and discomfort, which limits functional walking capacity. The clinical efficacy ofextract (GBE) as a therapeutic agent for IC is debatable. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of GBE compared with a placebo in patients with IC due to PAD.: Databases including PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and CINAHL were searched until 24 April 2026. Eligible studies included randomized, double-blind, controlled trials (RCTs) comparing placebo. Primary outcome was absolute claudication distance (ACD) at the end of the study. Secondary outcomes were initial claudication distance (ICD), ankle-brachial index (ABI), ankle pressure, and adverse events. Walking outcomes across various treadmill protocols were standardized to estimate caloric expenditure (kcal). A random-effects model was used to pool the effect estimates across trials. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2).: A total of 14 RCTs comprising 893 participants represent the total number randomized were included. GBE was associated with a statistically significant but modest improvement in ACD compared with placebo (mean difference [MD], 3.50 kcal; 95% CI, 0.02 to 6.98;= 0.049). This benefit was significant in trials with a 24-week duration (MD, 4.67 kcal; 95% CI, 2.26 to 7.08;< 0.001) but not in 12-16 weeks trials (MD, 1.35 kcal; 95% CI, -2.39 to 5.09;= 0.48). No significant changes were observed for ICD or resting ABI/ankle pressure. GBE was well tolerated, with an overall adverse event incidence comparable to placebo.: In patients with IC due to PAD, GBE therapy improves absolute walking performance, with a significant effect observed in trials evaluating 24 weeks of treatment. Given its favorable safety and tolerability profile, GBE can represent a clinically relevant and well-tolerated therapeutic option to support functional walking capacity, particularly for patients unable to tolerate or use conventional pharmacological agents.

articles.title: N-Butyl Cyanoacrylate Use for the Management of Type II Endoleak in Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Different endovascular techniques are available for type II endoleak management. This scoping review aimed to summarize the available evidence on the use of N-Butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) for type II endoleak management.This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A protocol was registered on Open Science Framework. A systematic search using the PCC (Population, Concept, Context) framework was performed in PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library. Findings were systematically presented using structured tables summarizing NBCA techniques, efficacy and safety outcomes.Following full-text assessment, 65 studies were included, comprising cohort and comparative studies, case reports, technical reports and preclinical studies. Single-arm cohort studies reported technical success rates of 90-100%, complication rates of 0-40% and variable durability outcomes, with clinical success ranging from 88 to 100%, endoleak resolution from 40 to 100% and aneurysm sac increase from 13 to 50%. Comparative studies reported improved outcomes with ethanol addition to the NBCA-ethiodized oil mixture compared with NBCA-ethiodized oil alone, shorter procedure times with direct puncture versus intra-arterial approach and more durable mid-term outcomes with selective embolization of contributing branches. Individually reported complications highlighted embolization risks and technical reports focused on catheter utilization. Pre-emptive embolization showed favorable outcomes on sac diameter reduction and endoleak type II occurrence.NBCA demonstrated technical feasibility for type II endoleak management, with variable durability. Considerable heterogeneity existed in access techniques, mixture ratios and outcome reporting. Preventive use demonstrated promising outcomes. Given the retrospective designs, limited sample sizes and heterogenous outcomes, adequately powered prospective studies are warranted.

This scoping review aimed to summarize the available evidence on the use of N-Butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) for type II endoleak management.This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A protocol was registered on Open Science Framework.

articles.title: Secondary TEVAR After Frozen Elephant Trunk: Indications and Timing.
articles.abstract: Frozen elephant trunk (FET) stabilizes the arch and proximal descending aorta, but complete distal remodeling is achieved in only a subset of patients with aortic dissection. Persistent false lumen perfusion, aortic growth, and distal stent graft-induced new entry lead to secondary thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), and reported distal reintervention rates range from about 13% at 5 years in pooled data to 33% in a center with routine staging. This narrative review examines the indications for and timing of secondary TEVAR after FET. PubMed was searched to September 2026, and 97 publications were included. Evidence obtained in patients treated with FET is distinguished from evidence extrapolated from primary type B dissection and from the authors' interpretation. We summarize the predictors of incomplete remodeling, including stent graft length, residual re-entry location, chronicity, aortic diameter at the distal stent level, early remodeling trajectory, and heritable aortopathy, and we contrast planned completion with surveillance-based reactive TEVAR, including technical aspects and spinal cord protection. Direct evidence on timing after FET is limited to retrospective series and one pilot randomized trial of TEVAR 1 to 3 months after type I repair; most data on the time-dependent loss of flap plasticity come from primary type B dissection. No universal timing rule is supported. We propose a phenotype-driven approach, not yet validated, in which timing is referenced to dissection onset and individualized to aortic anatomy, disease progression, and clinical condition.

Persistent false lumen perfusion, aortic growth, and distal stent graft-induced new entry lead to secondary thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), and reported distal reintervention rates range from about 13% at 5 years in pooled data to 33% in a center with routine staging. This narrative review examines the indications for and timing of secondary TEVAR after FET.

articles.title: A National Consultant Information Programme Data Analysis of Deep Venous Interventions in England.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to characterise contemporary deep venous interventions (DVIs) performed within the English National Health Service (NHS), describing procedural mix, patient heterogeneity, anatomic distribution, and short and midterm outcomes. METHODS: National data on DVIs performed between 1 June 2020 and 31 May 2023 were extracted from the National Consultant Information Programme. Percutaneous transluminal venous procedures (PTVs) and venous thrombolysis were identified using pre-defined procedural and diagnostic code hierarchies. All cases underwent structured patient level validation to ensure concordance between indication, treated venous anatomy, and procedural intent. The primary outcomes were ninety day and one year mortality. Secondary outcomes included procedural volume variation. Re-interventions were recorded descriptively. RESULTS: In total, 2 339 DVIs were performed, of which 1 617 PTVs and 604 venous thrombolysis procedures were validated. Patient cohorts were heterogeneous, most commonly chronic kidney disease (CKD) (41.8%), chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) (16.0%), and venous compression syndromes (14.0%). Anatomic distribution differed markedly by indication: CKD procedures predominantly involved upper limb and central veins, whereas CVI and venous compression were overwhelmingly confined to the lower limbs and iliocaval system. Among 650 patients with primary lower limb venous disease (CVI, venous thrombosis, or venous compression), 76.3% underwent iliac or inferior vena cava interventions. Overall mortality varied substantially by indication, being highest in patients with malignant neoplasms and lowest in primary lower limb venous disease. Thrombolysis was most frequently performed for lower extremity venous thrombosis and was associated with low short and midterm mortality in this group. CONCLUSION: This service level analysis of DVIs in England demonstrates distinct clinical populations with marked differences in anatomy, indication, and outcomes that vary substantially by indication and comorbidity. Mortality was lowest in elective primary lower limb venous disease and highest in patients with advanced systemic illness such as malignancy and renal disease. Future work should focus on indication specific venous registries and risk adjusted outcomes to aid benchmarking, service level organisation, and patient care.

articles.title: Propensity Score Matched Analysis of Outcomes of Conservative and Invasive Management of Patients with Chronic Limb Threatening Ischaemia: The PROCLION Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Current guidelines recommend revascularisation for patients with chronic limb threatening ischaemia (CLTI). However, revascularisation may be burdensome in these frail patients. The objective of this study was to compare the clinical and patient reported outcomes in patients with CLTI treated with conservative best supportive care versus primary invasive endovascular and/or surgical revascularisation. METHODS: This was a multicentre prospective cohort study in the Netherlands. Propensity score matching was used to create similar groups based on known factors influencing the odds of undergoing revascularisation. Twelve month amputation free survival (AFS), major amputation rates, mortality, and patient reported outcomes after primary conservative treatment were compared with primary invasive treatment (intention to treat; ITT). Outcomes after invasive treatment at any time were compared with definitive conservative treatment (per protocol; PP). RESULTS: A total of 365 patients with CLTI were included in 18 centres. In the ITT analysis, patients were matched 1 : 1, resulting in two groups of 121 patients. Twelve month AFS was 73.0% for patients after conservative treatment and 72.1% after invasive treatment (risk difference [RD] -0.9%, 95% confidence interval [CI] -10.2 - 8.4%). There were no significant differences in amputation and mortality rates. In the PP analysis, patients were matched 1 : 2, with 51 in the conservative group and 102 in the invasive group. Again, no significant differences were found for AFS, amputation rate, and mortality. Patient reported outcomes improved after 1 year in both groups (VascuQoL: ITT conservative group from 14 to 16.2, and invasive group from 13.8 to 16.5), but no significant differences were found in ITT or PP comparisons. CONCLUSION: The current study suggests that the 12 month clinical outcomes of primary conservative and invasive treatment for CLTI are similar. Conservative management may therefore be a viable first choice treatment option in selected patients with CLTI.

articles.title: Delayed Renal Artery Stump Pseudoaneurysm and Arteriovenous Fistula Following Nephrectomy Complicated by Pulmonary Coil Migration: Successful Laparoscopic Management.
articles.abstract: Background: Case Description: Discussion: Conclusions: Renal arteriovenous fistula (RAVF) and renal artery pseudoaneurysm (RAP) are rare vascular complications that may occur following renal surgery, trauma, or endovascular interventions. Delayed presentation after nephrectomy is exceptionally uncommon.We report the case of a 59-year-old woman with a pseudoaneurysm of the left renal artery stump associated with a high-flow renal arteriovenous fistula who was diagnosed three decades after left nephrectomy performed for complicated nephrolithiasis. The patient presented with episodic left flank pain without haematuria. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) and selective angiography confirmed the presence of a pseudoaneurysm and a high-flow arteriovenous fistula. Endovascular coil embolization was initially attempted; however, the coil migrated through the high-flow fistulous tract into the peripheral left pulmonary arterial circulation. Because the patient remained asymptomatic and haemodynamically stable and the coil was located peripherally, the procedural risk of retrieval was considered to outweigh the anticipated benefit. The coil was therefore left in situ under clinical and imaging surveillance. Because substantial arteriovenous shunting persisted after the unsuccessful embolization, definitive laparoscopic ligation of the left renal artery and vein stumps was successfully performed approximately one month later. During the two-year follow-up, two CTA examinations and Doppler ultrasonography confirmed complete occlusion of the fistula and pseudoaneurysm, with no recurrent abdominal symptoms or pulmonary complications related to the migrated coil.Although post-nephrectomy arteriovenous fistulas presenting 28 and 45 years after surgery have previously been reported, the combination of a renal artery stump pseudoaneurysm, a high-flow fistula, pulmonary coil migration, persistent arteriovenous shunting, and subsequent successful laparoscopic management is particularly unusual. This case highlights the technical challenges of endovascular treatment in high-flow fistulas and the role of surgical management following unsuccessful embolization.Delayed renal artery stump pseudoaneurysm associated with renal arteriovenous fistula after nephrectomy is an extremely rare condition. Although endovascular embolization remains the preferred first-line treatment, surgical management may be necessary in cases complicated by technical failure or embolization-related complications.

articles.title: Venous Thromboembolism and Pregnancy: Prevention and Treatment.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy-related venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. Physiologic changes in pregnancy, along with patient-specific and pregnancy-specific risk factors, increase this VTE risk. The prevention and treatment of pregnancy-related VTE is often complex and requires the careful consideration of variation in clinical guidelines, VTE risk profile, bleeding assessment, careful delivery planning and patient preference. The mainstay of treatment for an acute VTE in pregnancy is the use of low-molecular-weight heparin. In this review, we highlight three clinical cases to review clinical approaches to the prevention and treatment of VTE in pregnancy in these scenarios. Importantly, this review goes over the current understanding of the pathophysiology and clinical practice experience for pregnant patients with VTE. We also explored the variation in professional clinical guidelines on VTE prophylaxis and treatment strategies in pregnancy, and how these guidelines may be interpreted in the context of patient care for optimal outcomes.

articles.title: Treatment Strategies and Outcomes of Aneurysms Affecting Small and Medium Arteries in Neurofibromatosis Type 1. A systematic review.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)-associated arterial aneurysms are rare and characterized by vessel fragility and heterogeneous presentation. Evidence guiding optimal management remains limited. This systematic review aimed to evaluate treatment strategies and outcomes in NF1-related arterial aneurysms. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251169825). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for studies reporting management and outcomes of NF1-associated arterial aneurysms. Case reports, case series, and observational studies were included. Data were independently extracted by two reviewers. Primary outcomes included treatment strategies, technical success, complications, and mortality. Isolated aortic aneurysms or aortic dissections were not considered the primary target of the review. However, studies reporting concomitant aortic disease and aneurysmal involvement of non-aortic arteries were retained when relevant data on NF1-associated vasculopathy and its management were available. RESULTS: Eighty-six studies including 99 patients (mean age 42 years; 44.4% male) were analyzed. Aneurysms were most frequently located in cervico-vertebral (45.2%) and visceral arteries (24.0%). Multifocal disease was present in 12.1% of patients. Overall, 65.7% of patients presented with aneurysm rupture or acute hemorrhage. This high proportion should be interpreted cautiously because of the substantial publication bias inherent to a literature predominantly based on case reports and small case series. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently used approach (68.7%), followed by open surgery (19.2%), hybrid repair (5.0%), and conservative management (9.1%). Endovascular treatment showed a reported technical success rate exceeding 90%. Recanalization (6.3%), delayed thrombosis (4.2%), and new aneurysm formation (5.3%) were observed. Open repair was mainly used for anatomically complex or endovascularly inaccessible lesions. Overall mortality was 8.1%, primarily in patients presenting with rupture. CONCLUSIONS: NF1-associated aneurysms require an individualized, anatomy-driven management strategy. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently reported treatment and appears to be a viable option in anatomically suitable patients, while open and hybrid techniques remain important for selected complex lesions. However, the available evidence is derived predominantly from case reports and small case series and does not permit comparative assessment of treatment strategies. Lifelong imaging surveillance is mandatory due to the risk of recurrence and new aneurysm formation.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)-associated arterial aneurysms are rare and characterized by vessel fragility and heterogeneous presentation. Evidence guiding optimal management remains limited. This systematic review aimed to evaluate treatment strategies and outcomes in NF1-related arterial aneurysms.

articles.title: Beyond Risk Scores: Concordance of a Multidisciplinary Decision Support Instrument with Real Life Treatment Decisions for Patients with Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Treatment decisions for patients with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) are ethically complex and must be made under time pressure. This prospective observational study assessed how a previously developed decision support instrument (DSI) for rAAA aligns with real life treatment decisions and determined a reference threshold for interpreting its output. The DSI estimates the proportion of experts from the original multidisciplinary expert panel who would be expected to favour operative treatment (OT) for a given patient profile. METHODS: Consecutive rAAA patients were included between March 2024 and January 2026 from two Dutch hospitals. Treating vascular surgeons completed the DSI after the actual treatment decision (OT or palliative care). DSI outputs were analysed in relation to observed treatment decisions. A threshold sweep analysis was performed to identify a contextual reference threshold reflecting the level of DSI estimated expert support at which OT was generally pursued. Post-operative outcomes were assessed in OT patients for clinical context. RESULTS: Fifty patients were included; OT was chosen in 43 patients (86%). DSI estimated expert support was higher for patients receiving OT compared with palliative care (median 98% [interquartile range 97, 99%] vs. 83% [59, 89%]; p < .001). The contextual reference threshold was 93%, with concordance of 94% (95% confidence interval 83.8 - 97.9%). Case analysis highlighted challenges in capturing unresponsiveness due to profound hypovolaemic shock and assessing cardiac burden acutely Among patients surviving OT, relatively high health related quality of life was observed. CONCLUSIONS: The DSI shows concordance with real life treatment decisions for rAAA. A contextual reference threshold above which operative treatment was generally pursued could be empirically derived. Although refinement is needed to better identify certain high risk patients, these findings represent an important first step in the validation pathway and provide proof of concept for behavioural artificial intelligence technology methodology.

articles.title: Safety and Effectiveness of the GORE VIABAHN FORTEGRA Venous Stent for the Treatment of Symptomatic Inferior Vena Cava Obstruction With or Without Combined Iliofemoral Obstruction.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This prospective, non-randomised, clinical investigational trial investigated the safety and effectiveness of the GORE VIABAHN FORTEGRA Venous Stent for treatment of symptomatic inferior vena cava obstruction, with or without combined iliofemoral obstruction. METHODS: Subjects were enrolled at 17 sites across the USA, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. The primary endpoint was a composite measure including primary patency and freedom from stent embolisation at 12 months, and 30 day freedom from pulmonary embolism and device or procedure related death, major bleeding, and vascular injury requiring surgical or endovascular intervention. The hypothesis driven secondary endpoint was change in revised venous clinical severity score (rVCSS) pain score from baseline to 12 months. RESULTS: Eighty nine subjects were treated with an investigational iliocaval venous stent. Fifty nine (75%) of 79 evaluable subjects experienced freedom from a primary endpoint event, exceeding the performance goal of 58% at 12 months (90% confidence interval 66.6 - 82.7%) (p < .001). Of the 63 subjects reporting any pain at baseline, 51 (81%), saw an improvement in rVCSS pain score at 12 months, with a median difference of -2.0 (p < .001). CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular treatment of symptomatic iliocaval obstruction with the purpose designed investigational venous stent is safe and effective. Results demonstrate robust primary patency rates, an acceptable safety profile, and reduced pain.

articles.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Surgical Site Infections in Vascular Surgical Procedures in the Groin.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Vascular procedures in the groin are common and carry a high risk of surgical site infection (SSI). Several risk factors have been established but others are less clear, not least due to the heterogeneity of studies. This study aimed to provide generalisable data on SSI and associated factors after open vascular procedures in the groin. METHODS: This was a retrospective, dual centre cohort study including all patients undergoing open vascular surgery in the groin during a twelve year period at two centres. The primary endpoints were SSI rates at thirty and ninety days. Secondary endpoints were mortality at thirty days and 1 year. RESULTS: After exclusion of 165 early peri-operative deaths (5.6%) from the original 2 968 patients, 2 803 were analysed of which 1 424 (50.8%) included a bypass and 1 130 (40.4%) an endarterectomy, while 570 patients (20.3%) underwent minor procedures. The incidence of SSI was 6.3% (176 of 2 803) at thirty days and 8.2% (170 of 2 087) at ninety days. Of these, 40.1% (n = 83) were superficial, 32.8% (n = 68) involved the fascial layer, and 27.1% (n = 56) involved the vessels. All cause mortality was 6.6% (197 of 2 968) at thirty days and 14.1% (418 of 2 968) at 1 year, the latter significantly associated with SSI at thirty days (hazard ratio 2.23, 95% confidence interval 1.32 - 3.75; p = .003). On multivariable regression analysis, higher body mass index (odds ratio [OR] 1.08; p < .001), previous percutaneous interventions on the index vessels (OR 1.47; p = .030), use of a bovine pericardium patch (OR 1.98; p = .007), and creation of a supra-inguinal bypass (OR 1.91; p = .008) were associated with increased odds of SSI. Furthermore, lymphatic complications were strongly associated with subsequent SSI on univariable analysis (OR 3.766; p < .001). CONCLUSION: The odds of experiencing SSI depend on several patient and procedure related factors. Lymphatic complications were strongly associated with subsequent SSI. Therefore, future prospective studies should investigate whether strategies to reduce lymphatic complications also reduce SSIs.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Vascular procedures in the groin are common and carry a high risk of surgical site infection (SSI). Several risk factors have been established but others are less clear, not least due to the heterogeneity of studies. This study aimed to provide generalisable data on SSI and associated factors after open vascular procedures in the groin.

articles.title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
articles.abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

articles.title: Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain. METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization. RESULTS: P P P During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall=0.71;for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]). CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.

Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.
