articles.title: Venous thromboembolism reporting in fusion-positive NSCLC treated with tyrosine kinase inhibitors: A systematic review of safety reporting and protocol-level provisions in phase I-IV clinical trials.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant complication in patients with fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the completeness and consistency of thromboembolic safety reporting in clinical trials of tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC. Protocols, publications, and online trial registry updates were systematically reviewed to assess thromboembolic event ascertainment, reporting practices, protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions, and VTE-related eligibility criteria. RESULTS: A total of 108 reporting sources from 61 study entries (58 unique trials) were reviewed. Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis were the predominant reported events. VTE-related information was highly fragmented across reporting sources: 14 study entries reported events exclusively through full-text publications, 19 exclusively through online trial updates, and 15 through both sources. Study protocols rarely prespecified thromboembolic events as dedicated safety outcomes, more commonly addressing them in eligibility criteria, anticoagulant therapy provisions, or differential diagnosis guidance. More than 40% of study entries lacked protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions and nearly 60% lacked VTE-related eligibility restrictions. Marked heterogeneity was observed in event definitions, reporting practices, safety ascertainment, and observation periods. CONCLUSIONS: In fusion-positive NSCLC trials, heterogeneity in event ascertainment and reporting, rather than a true scarcity of thromboembolic events, represents a major limitation of the available evidence. Greater standardization of safety reporting and integration of trial registry and publication data may improve the completeness, comparability, and interpretability of future studies.

articles.title: Plasma proteomics enhances genetic risk prediction and biological understanding of venous thromboembolism.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: VTE Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and the third most common vascular cause of death globally. While clinical and genetic risk factors have improved VTE risk stratification, they do not fully capture underlying disease biology. We hypothesized that integrating large-scale plasma proteomics with a validated polygenic risk score (PRS) would reveal novel biological understanding and improve risk stratification. METHODS: VTE In 44,138 UK Biobank participants, we examined associations between PRSand 2,911 plasma proteins using multivariable linear regressions. We evaluated proteins as predictors of incident VTE using Cox regression models. We employed bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) using cis-acting protein quantitative trait loci (cis-pQTLs) instruments and genome-wide association summary statistics to infer potential causality. A protein-based risk score (ProteinRS) was developed with Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) logistic regression and compared against a clinical risk model. RESULTS: VTE PRSassociated with 265 proteins after false-discovery-rate correction (FDR < 0.01). Pathway enrichment analysis of these proteins highlighted cell adhesion, cell-junction organization, and transmembrane receptor signaling. Time-to-event analyses identified 354 proteins that predicted incident VTE (FDR < 0.01). MR implicated 14 proteins in potential causal pathways to VTE, while genetic liability to VTE affected the levels of 44 proteins. A 60-protein ProteinRS improved discrimination beyond clinical factors (area under the curve (AUC) 0.664 vs 0.647; P = 0.024). Participants above the 80th percentile of ProteinRS had a 49% higher hazard of VTE (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.49, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.17-1.90) and those below the 20th percentile had a 48% lower hazard (HR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.34-0.79) relative to the 20-80th percentile. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating genetic and proteomics data uncovered molecular pathways that link genetic susceptibility to VTE, highlighted actionable protein targets, and modestly enhanced risk prediction. Plasma proteomics therefore holds promise for precision prevention of VTE.

articles.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps drive immunoinflammatory remodeling in abdominal aortic aneurysm: from inflammatory amplification to precision therapy.
articles.abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a chronic vascular disorder characterized by progressive aortic wall dilation, extracellular matrix degradation, and an increased risk of catastrophic rupture. Currently, no effective pharmacological therapy is available to prevent or slow AAA progression. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have emerged as a critical pathological platform linking dysregulated innate immunity to vascular structural deterioration. In the AAA microenvironment, local inflammation, oxidative stress, metabolic disturbances, altered mechanical forces, and platelet activation collectively contribute to the induction of NETosis. Persistent NET formation promotes immunoinflammatory remodeling of the aortic wall by activating inflammatory sensing pathways, including TLR9, cGAS-STING, and NLRP3, modulating macrophage responses, inducing vascular smooth muscle cell ferroptosis and phenotypic switching, and exacerbating proteolytic degradation, oxidative injury, and immunothrombotic responses. During disease progression, NETs may transition from early drivers of inflammatory amplification to sustained regulators of vascular remodeling, while in advanced AAA they may synergize with intraluminal thrombus formation and structural destabilization to accelerate disease progression. Circulating NET-associated biomarkers represent promising candidates for complementing conventional imaging-based risk assessment; however, their specificity and predictive value require further validation. Therapeutic strategies targeting PAD4-mediated NET formation, the oxidative metabolic environment, NET-associated effector molecules, DNase I-mediated NET degradation, and nucleic acid sensing pathways have demonstrated potential in preclinical studies. This review systematically summarizes the emerging roles of NETs in AAA pathogenesis and discusses future precision strategies integrating biomarkers, multi-omics profiling, and imaging-based risk stratification with stage-specific therapeutic interventions.

articles.title: Long-term patency outcomes after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation in patients aged 80 years or older: a competing-risk analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Whether chronological age predicts arteriovenous fistula (AVF) durability remains uncertain. We compared primary patency between patients aged ≥80 and <80 years using competing-risk analysis and examined relevant vascular characteristics. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 416 consecutive patients undergoing first autogenous AVF creation during 2017-2020, with follow-up through March 2025. Intraoperative vessel diameters, macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis and preoperative ankle-brachial and toe-brachial indices were prospectively recorded. Death before primary patency loss was treated as a competing event. Cumulative incidence was estimated using Aalen-Johansen and compared using Gray's test. Associations were assessed using Fine-Gray and cause-specific Cox regression, with age modeled continuously in a sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Among 416 patients, 109 (26.2%) were aged ≥80 years. Median follow-up was 48 months. Older patients had more macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis (67.0% vs 47.9%; P<.001), lower ankle-brachial (1.09 vs 1.16; P<.001) and toe-brachial indices (0.69 vs 0.76; P=.002), and more venous diameters <2.5 mm (22.0% vs 13.4%; P=.030). The cumulative incidence of primary patency loss did not differ between groups (Gray P = .710), with 36-month estimates of 43.2% and 38.0%. Age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.12; 95% CI, 0.74-1.70), whereas each 10-year increase was associated with higher risk in a sensitivity analysis (sHR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.04-1.39). Proximal anastomosis was associated with lower risk (sHR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.37-0.88), and venous diameter <2.5 mm with higher risk (sHR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.05-2.75). Assisted primary and secondary patency did not differ. Fewer than 10% of fistulas were permanently abandoned by 60 months in either group, and 60-month survival among older patients was 82.0%. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients selected for autogenous AVF creation, age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss, whereas a continuous-age sensitivity analysis suggested a modest increase in risk per decade. These findings suggest that an age threshold alone should not determine AVF candidacy in otherwise suitable patients, although interpretation is tempered by loss to follow-up.

articles.title: Insulin Dependence Erodes the Cardiac and Survival Advantage of Asymptomatic Status After Carotid Revascularization.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with adverse outcomes after carotid revascularization, with insulin dependence conferring risk beyond DM alone. How this risk varies by symptom status and intervention type remains unclear. We evaluated the independent association of insulin-dependent (IDDM) and non-insulin-dependent DM (NIDDM) with 30-day and 1-year outcomes after carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), and carotid artery stenting (CAS), stratified by symptom status. METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for carotid interventions performed January 2005-January 2025. Patients were stratified by insulin-dependence and symptom status at presentation. Endpoints were 30-day and 1-year myocardial infarction (MI), ipsilateral stroke, all-cause mortality, ipsilateral stroke or death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; MI, ipsilateral stroke, or mortality). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, and procedural covariates estimated odds ratios (ORs). RESULTS: Of 275,668 patients meeting inclusion criteria, 73,582 (26.7%) had DM: 44,041 (59.9%) NIDDM and 29,541 (40.1%) IDDM. At 30 days there were 1,645 MIs, 2,051 ipsilateral strokes, 1,806 deaths, 3,626 strokes or deaths, and 5,029 MACE; at 1 year, 2,378, 2,924, 8,269, 10,750, and 12,646, respectively. Controlling for comorbidities and procedure type, IDDM was independently associated with elevated odds of 30-day MI (OR 1.63), ipsilateral stroke (OR 1.24), mortality (OR 1.19), and MACE (OR 1.19), but not ipsilateral stroke or death. Excess IDDM risk was concentrated among asymptomatic patients (30-day MACE OR 1.35 vs 1.07 in symptomatic patients; interaction P<0.001). Asymptomatic IDDM patients had higher 30-day MI odds (OR 1.54, P<0.001) than symptomatic patients without DM, with equivalent 30-day MACE (OR 1.05, P=0.41) and higher 1-year MACE (OR 1.19, P<0.001). Relative to CEA, TCAR and CAS were associated with higher 30-day ipsilateral stroke odds (OR 2.10 and 1.93, respectively, P≤0.01 for both) without differences in MI or mortality; an interaction with insulin dependence was nonsignificant for every endpoint. CONCLUSIONS: Insulin-dependent, diabetes was independently associated with substantially elevated odds of MI, ipsilateral stroke, mortality, and MACE after carotid revascularization, with risk sustained at 1 year. For cardiac and survival endpoints, asymptomatic patients with IDDM occupied a risk stratum comparable to symptomatic patients without diabetes. Asymptomatic status may therefore not confer the same composite risk advantage in insulin-dependent patients, with the excess being cardiac- and survival-driven. These findings support more cautious, individualized counseling and shared decision-making for asymptomatic patients with IDDM and identify insulin dependence as a clinically important, currently underemphasized modifier of perioperative risk.

articles.title: Femoral Artery Access Outcomes and Technical Considerations in Vascular Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Femoral artery access in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (VEDS) poses unique technical challenges due to structurally fragile arteries. This study evaluated femoral access-related complications in patients with genetically confirmed VEDS and sought to identify procedural and biologic factors that may inform access planning for endovascular procedures. METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis of patients with pathogenic/likely pathogenic COL3A1 variants who underwent endovascular procedures requiring femoral artery access. Data were obtained from the global GEN-VEDS Natural History Study and a retrospective single center cohort. Demographics, genotype, procedural indication, access and closure techniques, access-related complications, and outcomes were abstracted from clinical record. Major access-related complications were defined as femoral artery dissection, pseudoaneurysm, rupture, or closure device failure requiring open operative repair. RESULTS: A total of 117 femoral artery access sites were used in 105 endovascular interventions among 60 patients between 1989 and 2025. Median age at intervention was 39 years, and 53.3% of patients were male. Among 99 procedures with known access modality, 84 were performed percutaneously and 15 involved planned open femoral exposure. Manual compression was used in 33 percutaneous access sites, with no major access-related complications. Percutaneous closure devices were used in 39 access sites; major complications occurred in 5 access sites across 5 procedures, all requiring unplanned surgical exposure and repair. One additional percutaneous access site required unplanned open repair for access-related arterial injury and external iliac artery dissection before any closure device was attempted. Of percutaneous closure device failures, Perclose ProGlide and Starclose had the highest rate of failure (18.8% and 33.3% respectively). Three of four affected patients had large amino acid substitutions or exon skip mutations; the remaining patient had a small amino acid substitution but underwent 16-Fr sheath placement. No access-related complications occurred after planned open exposure. CONCLUSIONS: Femoral artery access in VEDS requires deliberate individualized planning. In this cohort, manual compression for smaller-caliber access (<6 Fr) was associated with favorable outcomes, whereas major complications occurred predominantly following attempted percutaneous closure. Planned open exposure, despite use in procedures involving larger sheath sizes, was not associated with access-related complications and may warrant consideration in selected circumstances, including procedures requiring larger sheath sizes, known prior closure-related arterial injury, and high-risk genotypes.

articles.title: Contemporary patterns of lower extremity revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia in the United States: 2016-2022.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality. Although revascularization improves limb outcomes in CLTI, contemporary practice patterns and real-world outcomes remain poorly characterized, particularly amid conflicting evidence from randomized trials regarding optimal revascularization and nonoperative management strategies. Our study utilized the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) coupled with U.S. Census data to characterize contemporary trends of incidence, revascularization approach, and in-hospital outcomes for adults hospitalized for CLTI. METHODS: We utilized the NIS (2016-2022) to generate survey-weighted national estimates of U.S. adult hospitalizations for CLTI. Age-normalized incidence rates per 100,000 person-years were calculated using population denominators from the U.S. Census Bureau. Admissions with secondary diagnoses of trauma or arterial dissection were excluded. Our outcomes evaluated the incidence of CLTI hospitalizations and rates of in-hospital revascularization type (open, endovascular, or no revascularization), major amputation, and mortality. Outcomes by revascularization strategies (open vs. endovascular) were stratified a priori by sex, frailty (Risk Analysis Index), diabetes status, and clinical presentation subgroups. Mann-Kendal trend tested monotonic temporal trends. RESULTS: trend trend trend trend trend trend An estimated 46,915 adult CLTI hospitalizations were included (mean age 69.7 years, 40.0% women, 69.5% White). Overall CLTI incidence was 7.28 per 100,000 person-years, initially declining until nadir in 2020 with reversal and steady rise thereafter. A total of 28,763 (61.3%) CLTI hospitalizations included revascularization (n=14,252 [49.5%] open and/or n=16,950 [58.9%] endovascular). The proportion of open revascularization decreased (p=0.016), while endovascular remained stable (p=0.368), and hospitalizations without revascularization increased (p=0.016) over time. Endovascular revascularization rates did rise among females, non-frail patients, and those presenting with rest pain (all p>0.05). Overall, in-hospital amputation (n=6,270 [13.4%]) and mortality (n=1,086 [2.3%]) remained stable (p>0.05). However, the proportion of patients discharged alive and without amputation increased most substantially among hospitalizations without revascularization (p=0.007). CONCLUSION: We provide contemporary analysis of U.S. hospitalizations for CLTI, demonstrating increasing rates following 2020. Overall, in-hospital rates of open revascularization declined in favor of nonoperative strategies corresponding with the greatest increase in alive discharges without amputations. Relative selection of endovascular strategies varied notably by sex, frailty, and clinical presentation. Our findings underscore the need for further investigation into optimal CLTI patient selection and coordinated integration of non-operative care, such as medical optimization, with revascularization strategies.

articles.title: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy. STUDY LIMITATIONS: The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints. CONCLUSIONS: Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

articles.title: Revascularization of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis: Cognitive Results of the CREST-2 Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prespecified cognitive secondary outcomes of the CREST-2 randomized clinical trials of patients 35 years or older with 70% or greater asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Enrollment was December 2014 through July 2024, and follow-up ended July 2025. Five cognitive tests were administered before treatment and annually up to 4 years. Cognitive performances from 146 clinical sites were centrally assessed by telephone, blinded to treatment. INTERVENTIONS: Two trials compared carotid stenting plus intensive medical management (CAS + IMM) with IMM alone and carotid endarterectomy plus IMM (CEA + IMM) with IMM alone. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Five cognitive tests, assessing learning, memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed, administered to all patients, were assessed for unadjusted and adjusted mean z scores using a linear mixed model. The minimal clinically important difference was 0.50 SD between treatment groups. The prespecified primary analysis was the fully adjusted composite z score at 4 years. Secondary analyses assessed the individual tests and at the test intervals. RESULTS: Among 2366 US study patients, 2165 (91.5%) participated in cognitive assessments, 1078 in the CAS trial (529 CAS + IMM; 549 IMM alone) and 1087 in the CEA trial (543 CEA + IMM; 544 IMM alone); mean age was 70.1 years (SD, 7.7) and 37.8% were female. Following baseline, 4954 test batteries were administered for a mean of 2.24 (SD, 1.09) follow-up years. There were no treatment-related differences in the fully adjusted estimated composite z scores at 4 years for either the CAS trial (CAS + IMM, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.13 to 0.30] vs IMM alone, 0.18 [95% CI, 0.09 to 0.27]; between-group difference, 0.03 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.15]) or the CEA trial (CEA + IMM, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33] vs IMM, 0.23 [95% CI, 0.15 to 0.32]; between-group difference, 0.02 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.14]). There were no significant differences between revascularization plus medical management vs IMM alone for any individual cognitive test. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In patients with severe asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis, revascularization with either CAS or CEA plus IMM, compared with IMM alone, did not significantly improve cognitive function at up to 4 years of follow-up.

articles.title: Revascularization in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Hemodynamic Impairment and Cognitive Outcomes: The CREST-H Substudy of the CREST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients. OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This substudy was conducted within a multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial. Adults (aged 35-86 years) without dementia with eighth-grade education or higher and unilateral asymptomatic ICA stenosis greater than or equal to 70% were enrolled from January 2018 to July 2024 at 61 sites in North America (last follow-up in July 2025). Of 607 participants screened from 2485 in CREST-2, 392 were enrolled. Magnetic resonance or computed tomographic perfusion imaging tested for baseline hemodynamic impairment defined by delayed time-to-peak (TTP) arrival of intravenous contrast in the hemisphere ipsilateral minus contralateral to the stenotic artery. INTERVENTION: Carotid revascularization (endarterectomy or stenting) plus intensive medical management (IMM) vs IMM alone. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the difference in composite cognitive z score over 1 year based on 5 cognitive tests. The primary analysis tested for an interaction between treatment group (revascularization vs IMM alone) and degree of baseline hemodynamic impairment among those with reduced baseline cognition (cognitive z score ≤-1.0 SD). RESULTS: Of 392 participants enrolled (mean age, 71 years; 125 [32%] females), 61 were excluded for missing baseline imaging and 40 for missing cognitive examinations or other covariates, leaving 291 with complete data. Fifty-one had reduced cognition at baseline (25 in the revascularization group and 26 in the IMM alone group). TTP ranged from no interhemispheric TTP delay to a more-than-2-second delay. Mean (SD) cognitive z scores were -1.36 (0.51) at baseline and -1.17 (0.47) at 1 year in the revascularization group and -1.34 (0.83) at baseline and -1.01 (0.97) at 1 year in the IMM alone group. The primary analysis showed no difference in cognition by treatment group over 1 year, adjusting for treatment group × hemodynamic status interaction and other covariates (adjusted difference in cognitive z score, -0.15 SD [95% CI, -0.54 to 0.24]). The interaction was not significant (β estimate = 0.018 [95% CI, -0.025 to 0.061]; P = .40). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this substudy of a randomized clinical trial, there was no differential effect of revascularization vs IMM alone on cognition over 1 year by cerebral hemodynamic status among those with baseline reduced cognition, suggesting that revascularization does not improve cognitive dysfunction by restoring flow to the brain in chronic asymptomatic carotid stenosis. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03121209.
articles.englishSummary: IMPORTANCE: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients. OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.

articles.title: Performance of Western HA-VTE risk models in East Asian populations: a prospective multicenter study.
articles.abstract: Hospital-associated venous thromboembolism (HA-VTE) causes significant morbidity, but risk prediction models are inconsistently validated, especially in non-Western populations. We prospectively validated 5 HA-VTE risk scores (Caprini, Padua, IMPROVE [International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism], Kucher, and Intermountain) in a prospective multicenter cohort of 2948 adult inpatients from 17 Chinese hospitals. Symptomatic VTE events were recorded through 3 months of follow-up. The 90-day HA-VTE incidence was 2.54%. All 5 models showed moderate discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], 0.726-0.759). Caprini, Padua, and Intermountain models did not differ significantly (DeLong test, P> .05). Caprini had the highest sensitivity (0.83) but classified 42.6% of patients as being at high risk. Padua and Intermountain favored specificity (0.75-0.81) with lower sensitivity (0.64-0.67). Clinical model selection should align with specific balances between sensitivity and utility. In surgical inpatients, Caprini performed best (AUC, 0.804; sensitivity, 0.90; negative predictive value, 1.00), although its more than 40 input variables limit practical use. Calibration was generally acceptable. Performance varied across subgroups. The prophylaxis subgroup showed attenuated performance, with reduced discrimination (eg, Caprini AUC decreased to 0.682) and less stable calibration. Western HA-VTE models have moderate predictive value in East Asian inpatient populations. Performance differs across subgroups. Local recalibration and development of simpler, population-specific scores are needed.

We prospectively validated 5 HA-VTE risk scores (Caprini, Padua, IMPROVE [International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism], Kucher, and Intermountain) in a prospective multicenter cohort of 2948 adult inpatients from 17 Chinese hospitals. Symptomatic VTE events were recorded through 3 months of follow-up.

articles.title: Surgery Versus Ultrasound-Guided Foam Sclerotherapy for the Treatment of Isolated Anterior Saphenous Vein Incompetence: A Single-Center Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p Isolated anterior saphenous vein (ASV) incompetence is a clinically relevant source of symptomatic anterior thigh varicose veins, which may cause pain, heaviness, swelling and serious complication such as superficial vein thrombosis. Therefore, targeted management is often required, yet evidence guiding treatment remains limited. This single-center, randomized trial compared high ligation surgery in combination with phlebectomy and ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy (UGFS).Thirty-nine limbs of 35 patients (19 allocated to surgery, 20 to UGFS) were treated and followed up at 1 and 3 years. The primary outcome was ASV-territory recurrence defined as reflux time > 0.5 s along the ASV in the UGFS group or new anterior thigh varicosities connected to the previous saphenofemoral junction in the surgical group at 3 years. Secondary outcomes were the same duplex endpoint at 1 year, recurrence of clinically visible varicose veins, and groin neovascularization at 1 and 3 years.ASV-territory recurrence was numerically higher after UGFS (63% vs. 33%) at 3 years, although the difference was not statistically significant, whereas recurrence was higher after UGFS than surgery at 1 year (65% vs. 11%;< 0.001). Clinical recurrence rates did not differ significantly between groups at 1 and 3 years. Neovascularization was observed exclusively in the surgery group at 1 year and remained more frequent at 3 years (44% vs. 5%).Our findings suggest better short-term disease control with surgery than with UGFS for isolated ASV incompetence, whereas the prespecified primary endpoint of ASV-territory recurrence at 3-years did not differ significantly between groups. Both surgery and UGFS may therefore be considered for selected patients, with treatment choice guided by patient-centered factors, including vein anatomy, invasiveness, and patient preference.

articles.title: Sequential decision-making in endovascular stroke therapy: benefit and harm of the next retrieval attempt after failed reperfusion.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: After failed reperfusion in endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), interventionalists must outweigh the expected benefit of an additional retrieval attempt with the outcome of the current angiographic result. Framing EVT as an infinite-horizon optimal stopping problem, the present study provides a per-pass evaluation of the expected benefit of EVT continuation versus procedural termination after unsuccessful reperfusion, based on large-scale real-world registry data. METHODS: Patients from the German Stroke Registry - Endovascular Treatment (GSR-ET) between 2015 and 2023 were screened. Inclusion criteria were (1) age ≥ 18 years, (2) anterior circulation LVO, (3) 1-15 retrieval attempts and (4) availability of relevant clinical data. Primary endpoint was the rate of good functional outcome, defined as modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score 0-2 at 90 days. For each retrieval attempt, patients were stratified into successful reperfusion (mTICI 2b-3) and persistent occlusion (mTICI 0-2a). The net expected benefit of EVT continuation, Δ(k), was defined as the difference between the mRS 0-2 rate at pass k + 1, and the mRS 0-2 rate for unsuccessful reperfusion at pass k. A positive Δ(k) indicates that continuation is favored at that decision node k. The pass at which Δ(k) first becomes non-significant identifies the empirical, optimal stopping threshold. RESULTS: Among 9,495 included patients, successful reperfusion (mTICI 2b-3) was achieved in 8,405 (89%), and 3,428 (36%) achieved good functional outcome at 90 days. Up to six retrieval attempts, Δ(k) was positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05), indicating that continuation of EVT was associated with superior expected outcome at each of these decision points. At pass seven, Δ(k) became negative and lost statistical significance (p = 0.53), identifying this as the empirical optimal stopping threshold. CONCLUSION: Continuation of EVT up to six retrieval attempts confers a significant functional benefit over termination after unsuccessful reperfusion. These findings provide a decision-theoretic basis for individualized intraprocedural decision-making and suggest that functional independence can be achieved beyond conventionally assumed pass thresholds.

Framing EVT as an infinite-horizon optimal stopping problem, the present study provides a per-pass evaluation of the expected benefit of EVT continuation versus procedural termination after unsuccessful reperfusion, based on large-scale real-world registry data. METHODS: Patients from the German Stroke Registry - Endovascular Treatment (GSR-ET) between 2015 and 2023 were screened.

articles.title: Two-Year Outcomes of the Prospective THRILLER Registry on Popliteal and Infrapopliteal Endovascular Interventions for CLTI.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization. OBJECTIVES: The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies. METHODS: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Overall, 78.4% (831/1,060) of the limbs were Rutherford 5 and 8.1% (86/1,060) were Rutherford 6; 41.3% (382/926) were WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection) stage 4. Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P < 0.001) and AFS (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.50-2.86; P < 0.001). For AFS, the excess risk of Rutherford 6 was greatest in the first 3 months (HR: 14.13; 95% CI: 4.94-40.38 vs Rutherford 4; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.

METHODS: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals.

articles.title: JTH in Clinic: Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Prophylaxis of Pediatric Patients at Risk of VTE.
articles.abstract: As the incidence of venous thromboembolism (VTE) increases in hospitalized children, there is an urgent need to improve VTE prevention strategies in this population. Implementation of thromboprophylaxis, which includes mechanical and pharmacological interventions, varies in practice due to limited pediatric-specific data and, until recently, a lack of evidence-based guidelines. However, recent randomized clinical trials and well-designed multicenter observational studies have provided improved evidence on the safety and efficacy of anticoagulants for VTE prevention in specific pediatric subpopulations supporting the development of risk assessment models to help identify subgroups of children at high risk for VTE. Based on these data, the American Society of Hematology and International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis recently developed the first evidence-based guideline for anticoagulant prophylaxis in children at risk of VTE. While this guideline is an exciting step towards preventing VTE-associated harm, VTE prevention remains complex due to unique pediatric risk factors and changing physiology with age, resulting in heterogeneous VTE and bleeding risk profiles. In this case-based review, we apply the new guideline and supporting evidence to guide decisions regarding the use of thromboprophylaxis in pediatric cases commonly encountered in clinical practice, highlighting the nuances of VTE prevention in critically ill children. We review the complex decision-making process required prior to initiation of pharmacologic prophylaxis, including assessment of VTE risk, bleeding risk, and shared decision-making with families. Additionally, we highlight the importance of multidisciplinary teams in VTE prevention and anticoagulant stewardship, as well as the similarities and differences in pediatric versus adult practice.

articles.title: Association of Completion Imaging Modalities and Carotid Endarterectomy Outcomes in the Vascular Quality Initiative.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Completion imaging after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) confirms technical success and identifies defects requiring correction. However, the comparative effectiveness of imaging modalities in detecting clinically significant problems remains unclear. This study evaluated completion imaging patterns, intraoperative re-exploration as a surrogate for detection efficacy, and associated postoperative outcomes. METHODS: CEAs performed between 2012-2024 in the VQI were analyzed. Completion imaging was categorized as none, Doppler, duplex ultrasound, or angiography. Intraoperative re-exploration rates were compared across modalities to assess detection of technical defects requiring revision. Postoperative outcomes were analyzed among patients who required re-exploration. Inverse probability weighted (IPW) logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios. Temporal trends were also analyzed. RESULTS: Among 208,786 CEAs, 24% had no completion imaging, 48% used Doppler, 24% duplex, and 4% angiography. Angiography had the highest intraoperative re-exploration rate (none 0.9%, doppler 0.9%, duplex 2.3%, angiography 3.6%; p<0.001). Among the 2,723 patients who required re-exploration, postoperative stroke occurred in 8.3% with no imaging, 12.5% with doppler, 3.7% with duplex, and 22.5% with angiography (p<0.001). In IPW-adjusted analyses, intraoperative duplex was associated with significant reduction in postoperative stroke compared to: no imaging (aOR 0.43, 95%CI 0.27-0.69), doppler (aOR 0.28, 95%CI 0.19-0.40), and angiography (aOR 0.13, 95%CI 0.09-0.20), all p<0.001. Overall, Angiography had the worst stroke outcomes. Doppler and angiography performed worse than duplex across additional endpoints, including ipsilateral stroke, TIA, any neurological event, return to OR, and 30-day mortality. Despite the stronger safety profile of duplex, it remains underused, as most CEAs performed in the last 15 years have utilized doppler or no imaging. CONCLUSIONS: Re-exploration and stroke outcomes after completion imaging reflect each modality's safety and efficacy in detecting significant technical defects. Duplex ultrasound demonstrated the lowest stroke rates and overall complications compared with angiography, doppler, and no imaging, suggesting its superior efficacy and safety. Doppler showed intermediate performance, while angiography carried the highest risk among patients who required re-exploration. Despite strong evidence favoring duplex, the majority of surgeons performing CEAs still rely on doppler or omit any completion imaging. Greater use of duplex ultrasound and incorporation of intraoperative duplex assessment into vascular training may improve intraoperative assessment, although further prospective evaluation is warranted.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Completion imaging after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) confirms technical success and identifies defects requiring correction. However, the comparative effectiveness of imaging modalities in detecting clinically significant problems remains unclear. This study evaluated completion imaging patterns, intraoperative re-exploration as a surrogate for detection efficacy, and associated postoperative outcomes.

articles.title: Risk of Venous Thromboembolism in Kidney Transplant Recipients with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Kidney transplant recipients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) may be at higher risk of venous thromboembolism than non-ADPKD recipients. METHODS: We conducted an observational study of adult kidney transplant recipients at a single center, the University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG; n=1179, 393 with ADPKD), and replicated key analyses in the multicenter Swiss Transplant Cohort Study (STCS; n=4415, 710 with ADPKD). The primary endpoint was time to first venous thromboembolism after transplantation or death related to venous thromboembolism (identified through medical record review), analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox regression. Data were pooled for subgroup analyses and to assess determinants of post-transplant venous thromboembolism risk. RESULTS: Venous thromboembolism occurred more often in ADPKD than non-ADPKD kidney transplant recipients (log-rank p=0.04 and p<0.001 for UMCG and STCS, respectively). The 10-year cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence was 13.5% [95% CI: 9.4, 17.5], versus 9.6% [95% CI: 7.0, 12.1] in ADPKD versus non-ADPKD recipients in UMCG, and 21.0% [95% CI: 17.0, 24.7] versus 15.1% [95% CI: 13.5, 16.6] in STCS. Median [Q1, Q3] time to venous thromboembolism were similar across cohorts (UMCG: 1.7 [0.4, 4.9], STCS: 1.4 [0.2, 4.8] years). Venous thromboembolism risk was highest in the early (<2 years) post-transplant period. After adjustment for venous thromboembolism risk factors, ADPKD remained independently associated with post-transplant venous thromboembolism in both cohorts (UMCG HR 1.80 [95% CI: 1.21, 2.69]; STCS HR 1.39 [95% CI: 1.13, 1.72]). The association between ADPKD and risk of venous thromboembolism was more pronounced in males. Hemoglobin levels after kidney transplantation were approximately 7.0 ± 0.8% higher in ADPKD recipients, particularly in males, with corresponding higher risks of erythrocytosis during follow-up. Incorporating longitudinal hemoglobin as a time-varying covariate attenuated the association between ADPKD and venous thromboembolism, suggesting that the association was at least partially driven by higher hemoglobin levels. CONCLUSIONS: Kidney transplant recipients were at high risk for venous thromboembolism, and those with ADPKD are at an even higher risk.

articles.title: Whole-transcriptome single-cell spatial landscape of instability in human carotid atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Carotid atherosclerotic plaque instability is a major cause of ischemic stroke. While current clinical guidelines for carotid endarterectomy rely primarily on stenosis severity and patient symptomatology, unstable plaques can cause strokes even with low to moderate stenosis, suggesting that factors beyond plaque stenosis may drive its instability. This study aimed to characterize the cellular and spatial features of plaque instability at both single-cell and subcellular resolution. METHODS AND RESULTS: single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on carotid endarterectomy samples from patients with clinically and histologically classified stable or unstable plaques, consisting of more than 53,000 cells. Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), macrophages, and T-lymphocytes accounted for ∼85% of plaque-resident cells, with unstable plaques showing increased abundance of inflammatory synthetic VSMCs, GZMK+ cytotoxic T-lymphocytes, and antigen-presenting macrophages. In contrast, stable plaques were enriched in contractile and fibroblast-like VSMCs, alongside MRC1+ resident-like macrophages. To then spatially map these populations, CosMx™ high-plex spatial transcriptomics was integrated utilizing the unprecedented whole-transcriptome (∼18,934 targets) Human Discovery RNA panel. This revealed a distinct spatially disorganized plaque architecture in unstable plaques, characterized by infiltration of inflammatory synthetic VSMCs and effector T-lymphocytes distributed across both the fibrotic cap and lipid core, alongside distinct multicellular microenvironments enriched for adaptive immune engagement. This was in contrast to stable plaques, which exhibited more structured, macrophage-dominant spatial microenvironments and neighborhoods. We lastly profiled ∼90,000 paired peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to assess the plaque macroenvironment. PBMCs surrounding unstable plaques displayed exclusive enrichment of CD14+CD16+ intermediate monocytes and effector T-lymphocytes, which were depleted surrounding stable plaques. Ligand-receptor interaction analyses within CCL and CXCL-mediated pathways revealed enhanced immune-stromal signaling between PBMC-derived monocytes and plaque-resident VSMCs in the unstable plaque group, with coordinated chemokine-driven interactions indicating a shift toward VSMC- and T-lymphocyte mediated recruitment of circulating immune cells. CONCLUSIONS: These results demonstrate that carotid plaque instability is driven by spatially coordinated expansion of inflammatory VSMCs and effector immune cells within the plaque and from the circulation, with a shift from predominantly innate immune-dominant characteristics in stable plaques toward adaptive immune-enriched responses in unstable conditions. This integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic approach refines an integrated immune-stromal framework linking local plaque remodeling with systemic immune activation, highlighting key tissue-resident and circulating contributors to instability and establishing a foundation for mechanism-informed diagnostics and targeted therapeutic strategies beyond stenosis severity.

articles.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Anticoagulation Alone in Intermediate-High Risk PE: Improved Functional 90-Day Outcomes in STORM-PE RCT.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Up to 50% of pulmonary embolism (PE) survivors experience long-term functional limitations and reduced quality of life (QoL). Reperfusion strategies can rapidly relieve right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction and prevent clinical deterioration or hemodynamic collapse; however, these approaches have never been evaluated in a randomized trial against anticoagulation alone using patient-centered outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate whether mechanical thrombectomy with anticoagulation improves functional, QoL, and safety outcomes compared with anticoagulation alone in patients with acute intermediate-high risk PE over 90 days. METHODS: STORM-PE enrolled 100 PE patients randomized 1:1 to computer-assisted vacuum thrombectomy (CAVT) with anticoagulation or anticoagulation alone across 22 international sites, with RV-to-left-ventricular (RV/LV) ratio change at 48 hours as the primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints included major adverse events within 7 days, functional and QoL outcomes, mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence through 90 days. RESULTS: For all patients, median time from randomization to last follow-up visit was 91.0 days [Q1-Q3: 80.5-100.0]. At 90 days, 66.0% (31/47) of CAVT and 64.2% (34/53) of anticoagulation patients completed the 6-min walk test. The CAVT arm exhibited a longer 6-min walk distance compared with anticoagulation alone (478.7 ± 159.5 m vs 368.0 ± 127.8 m, P = 0.003). More CAVT than anticoagulation patients were NYHA functional class I (97.4% [37/38] vs 75.6% [34/45], P = 0.005) at 90 days. Dyspnea and QoL scores were comparable between groups, with no differences between arms for all-cause mortality, PE-related mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence within 90 days. CONCLUSIONS: In STORM-PE, CAVT with anticoagulation resulted in improved functional outcomes at 90 days compared with anticoagulation alone, with equivalent safety rates. This trial supports CAVT as an effective and safe reperfusion strategy for intermediate-high risk PE. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT05684796.

articles.title: Timeless therapeutics: cardiac indications for vitamin K antagonists in clinical practice.
articles.abstract: Anticoagulation is a critical component in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases. Large randomised controlled trials have demonstrated that direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are effective and safe for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and treatment or prevention of venous thromboembolism. Nevertheless, for specific cardiac indications and patient characteristics, vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) rather than DOACs are either preferred, or the benefit of DOACs in comparison to VKAs remains uncertain. These include, among others, mechanical heart valves, AF associated with moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis, left ventricular or atrial thrombus, and older patients with frailty. As VKAs will continue to play a vital role in the management of patients with cardiovascular diseases in the foreseeable future, this review discusses cardiac indications and patient characteristics that necessitate the use of VKAs and general management principles of VKA therapy.

articles.title: Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery.
articles.abstract: The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor's spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4's groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates.

articles.title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes reveal hepatic regulatory mechanisms of residual feed intake during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to characterize hepatic molecular features associated with residual feed intake (RFI) during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes. RFI was measured in 478 individually caged male Langya chickens from 96 to 133 days of age. After the feeding trial, the chickens were ranked in ascending order of RFI and classified into low-RFI (LRFI) and high-RFI (HRFI) subpopulations using the population mean RFI as the cutoff. Eight healthy chickens were then randomly selected from each subpopulation to form the LRFI and HRFI groups (n = 8 per group). Following slaughter and tissue collection at 133 days of age, hepatic transcriptomic and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomic analyzes were conducted. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) were subsequently subjected to enrichment and correlation analyzes. Compared with HRFI chickens, LRFI chickens had lower feed intake (FI) and higher eviscerated carcass yield and breast muscle yield. They also had lower abdominal fat percentage and muscle fat width, whereas BWG and metabolic body weight were similar between groups. Liver profiling identified 850 DEGs and 282 DAMs. Integrated KEGG analysis identified 15 pathways significantly enriched in both datasets. The amino acid metabolism-related pathways among these shared pathways collectively pointed to aromatic amino acid (AAA)-related metabolism, including biosynthesis of amino acids, phenylalanine metabolism, phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis, and tryptophan metabolism. A total of 16 DEGs and 29 DAMs were mapped to these pathways and showed widespread significant correlations. Among them, IL4I1, AFMID, ASS1, PHGDH, MAOB, IDO2, HAAO, and PAH were identified as candidate genes associated with RFI. These results characterized hepatic molecular features associated with RFI during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. These findings indicate that hepatic AAA-related metabolism may play a potential role in RFI divergence during the late growth stage in slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. The identified AAA metabolism-related pathways provide a focused set of candidate genes, metabolites, and pathways for further investigation of their roles in RFI and feed efficiency, and provide a theoretical basis for molecular breeding and breed conservation of slow-growing broilers.

articles.title: Early versus late venous thromboembolism in patients with newly diagnosed high-grade gliomas.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurs in 20-30% and 9.2% of patients with glioblastoma and grade 3 IDH mutant (IDHmut) gliomas respectively, with highest risk during the first months post-surgery. We sought to identify risk factors for early versus late VTE in high-grade gliomas and evaluated the recently proposed 'GliomaPredictVTE' tool. METHODS: We included 894 patients with newly-diagnosed glioblastoma and grade 3-4 IDHmut gliomas from 2010-2023. Competing-risk analysis estimated VTE cumulative incidence (CumInc), segmented linear regression model identified the change-point between early versus late VTE, and competing-risk regression model identified significant risk factors. GliomaPredictVTE-predicted 6- and 12-month VTE risks were compared to observed CumInc. RESULTS: The estimated 6- and 12-month VTE CumInc was 21.5% and 26.4%, respectively for IDHwt glioblastoma versus 6.3% and 8.3%, respectively for IDHmut gliomas. The VTE CumInc increased rapidly during the first 6 months post-surgery, followed by a more gradual rise thereafter, with a change-point around 6 months. On multivariable analyses, 'Early VTE' (within 6 months post-surgery) was significantly associated with older age, limb weakness, ambulation dependence, and radiotherapy alone; 'Late VTE' (6 months to 5 years) with older age and smoking. GliomaPredictVTE substantially underestimated VTE incidence in our population, with a mean predicted 6- and 12-month risks of 11.0% and 17.4%, versus observed CumInc of 19.9% (p < 0.001) and 23% (p = 0.008), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Distinct risk profiles between early and late VTE support prospective studies of primary prophylaxis in high-risk patients, particularly in the first 6 months post-surgery. GliomaPredictVTE significantly underestimates VTE incidence in this population.

articles.title: Self-Expanding Stent-Assisted Reconstruction of Distal Supra-Aortic Vessels in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Comparative Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background Methods and Results Conclusions n n p p p p : Supra-aortic vessel reconstruction during total aortic arch replacement in acute Stanford type A aortic dissection patients with dissected distal supra-aortic vessels remains technically challenging; proximal supra-aortic vessel replacement alone carries a high risk of neurological complications secondary to intimal inversion. This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone.: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023. Patients were divided into two groups according to intraoperative anatomy and surgeon decision: self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction (SAVR,= 26) and proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone (PRVA,= 23). Neurological outcomes related to supra-aortic vessel intimal inversion, operative parameters, blood product transfusion, and short-term complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 18.2 ± 4.1 months (range, 12-24 months). The SAVR group exhibited significantly lower supra-aortic vessel stenosis rate (3.8% vs. 30.4%,< 0.001) and zero cases of intimal inversion-related luminal collapse versus five cases in the PRVA group (0 vs. 5,= 0.02). Numerically fewer cases of symptomatic stroke (0% vs. 8.7%,= 0.09) and radiographic cerebral infarction (3.8% vs. 13.0%,= 0.17) were observed in the SAVR group, though the differences did not achieve statistical significance. Red blood cell and fresh frozen plasma transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation duration, and ICU stay length were significantly lower in the SAVR cohort. Cardiopulmonary bypass time and 30-day mortality were comparable between groups.: Self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction represents a promising technical option during total arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection with distal supra-aortic dissection, associated with superior branch vessel patency and favorable numerical trends in neurological and recovery-related endpoints, with a comparable early-term safety profile. Potential benefits require further validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Case Report: Fetal giant congenital hemangioma with arteriovenous malformation: to be or not to be.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study reports a rare and life-threatening case of a giant congenital hemangioma with arteriovenous fistula in a neonate and describes its clinical management and outcomes. METHOD: A female neonate with a giant right forearm hemangioma with arteriovenous fistula, detected prenatally at 23 weeks, was managed by a multidisciplinary team. Postnatally, the infant developed severe pulmonary hypertension and active bleeding from the mass. Diagnosis was confirmed via computed tomography angiography and arteriography. Emergency intervention with combined embolization coil and sclerotherapy was performed, followed by oral propranolol therapy. RESULTS: Following the combined intervention and pharmacotherapy, the condition of the infant improved significantly. The severe pulmonary hypertension resolved, and the tumor size progressively reduced. CONCLUSION: Congenital hemangioma combined with arteriovenous malformation can lead to severe, life-threatening complications. A prompt, multidisciplinary approach involving embolization, sclerotherapy, and pharmacotherapy can achieve favorable outcomes, underscoring the importance of early recognition and integrated perinatal management.

articles.title: Effect of Microvascular Disease on Re-amputation Risk after Unilateral Amputation due to Diabetes or Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between manifestations of microvascular disease (MVD) and other factors on re-amputation risk within 12 months following incident unilateral lower extremity amputation. METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of 8 924 patients with first unilateral transmetatarsal, transtibial, or transfemoral amputation secondary to diabetes and or peripheral arterial disease, identified through a Veterans Affairs database. Re-amputation was defined as any subsequent ipsilateral soft tissue or bony revision or amputation to a higher level. The presence of MVD was determined using a composite variable that required the involvement of each subcomponent (neuropathy, nephropathy, and retinopathy), and also by evaluating each of the subcomponent MVD variables separately. Twenty-nine additional risk factors were evaluated in relation to the primary outcome of re-amputation. A competing risk analysis estimated the cumulative incidence of re-amputation. The effect of risk factors on re-amputation risk was estimated by computing subdistribution hazard ratios (sub-HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: The twelve month re-amputation risk was 38.0% (transmetatarsal), 27.2% (transtibial), and 14.1% (transfemoral). The combined MVD variable was not significantly associated with re-amputation risk. However, re-amputation after transmetatarsal amputation was significantly elevated in patients with retinopathy, leukocytosis, or those who were on kidney dialysis, with the highest risk in those with all three (sub-HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.8 - 2.6). Similarly, for transtibial patients, the risk was higher in the presence of retinopathy, leukocytosis, and kidney dialysis, and in those with a prior ipsilateral revascularisation and those on warfarin. The highest risk was observed in those with all factors present (sub-HR 2.1, 95% CI 1.6 - 2.7). CONCLUSION: This study identified an important association between the pre-amputation diagnosis of retinopathy and risk for subsequent failure of primary healing and need for re-amputation. Presence of retinopathy should be considered when evaluating potential failure of healing during amputation level decisions.

articles.title: Outcomes of Total Endovascular Repair of Aortic Arch and Thoraco-abdominal Aortic Aneurysms in the International Multicenter Aortic Research Group in a Selected Group of Patients with Extensive Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to report outcomes of total endovascular aortic repair (TEAR) using arch branched endovascular aortic repair (aBEVAR) and thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR). METHODS: Clinical data from 16 participating centres in the International Multicenter Aortic Research Group from 2014 to 2024 were retrospectively analysed. All patients who underwent TEAR were included. The primary outcome was aortic related mortality (ARM). Secondary outcomes included stroke and or transient ischaemic attack (TIA), spinal cord ischaemia (SCI), and freedom from target artery (TA) instability, re-interventions, and new cardiovascular events (CVEs) within 1 year. RESULTS: Of 98 patients scheduled for TEAR, 95 (97%) completed both stages, including 46 (48%) with chronic post-dissection aneurysms and 49 (52%) with degenerative aneurysms. A multistage approach with aBEVAR followed by TAAA FBEVAR was used in all patients, with a median interval between stages of 11 months (interquartile range [IQR] 5, 14). One (1%) rupture occurred between the staged procedures (successfully managed with off the shelf TAAA multibranch stent graft). Custom made and off the shelf TAAA FBEVAR devices were used in 79 (83%) and 16 (17%) patients, respectively. There were 12 (13%) stroke and or TIAs (aBEVAR, ten; TAAA FBEVAR, two); five (5%) had a modified Rankin Scale score > 3. Sixteen patients (17%) experienced SCI (aBEVAR, two; TAAA FBEVAR, 14) with three cases (3%) of paraplegia. Four patients (4%) died within thirty days; these were the only cases of ARM. Median follow up was 32 months (IQR 3, 61). Of 67 patients (71%) with available one year follow up, there were six (9%) with TA instability and five (7%) CVEs. Estimated three year survival was 79 ± 5% with a cumulative incidence of re-intervention of 31 ± 6%. CONCLUSION: Multistage TEAR with aBEVAR followed by TAAA FBEVAR was associated with low ARM, re-intervention, and TA instability. Stroke and SCI remain significant and must be carefully weighed during patient selection and treatment.

METHODS: Clinical data from 16 participating centres in the International Multicenter Aortic Research Group from 2014 to 2024 were retrospectively analysed. All patients who underwent TEAR were included.

articles.title: Early Outcomes of Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis in Aortic Arch Pathologies: A Nordic Multicentre Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the feasibility and early clinical outcomes of the Gore thoracic branch endoprosthesis (TBE) in the treatment of aortic arch pathologies. METHODS: This multicentre retrospective study, conducted and reported in accordance with the STROBE statement, included consecutive patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair with TBE between February 2024 and July 2025. No restrictions were applied regarding the type or extent of aortic disease, use of staged procedures, or concomitant adjunctive endovascular interventions. Primary endpoints were technical success, thirty day death, and overall survival, while endoleak occurrence, primary target vessel patency, stroke, and spinal cord ischaemia (SCI) were secondary. RESULTS: Sixty-four patients (median age 73 years [interquartile range {IQR} 59, 77]; 69% men) were included. Indications for treatment included degenerative aneurysm (n = 26; 41%), chronic dissection (n = 18; 28%), subacute dissection (n = 11; 17%), and acute dissection (n = 9; 14%). The left subclavian artery was the target vessel in 59 cases (92%), followed by the brachiocephalic trunk in three (5%) and the left common carotid artery in two (3%). Technical success was achieved in 95% of cases (n = 61), with failures attributed to two type Ia endoleaks and one type IIIa endoleak. The thirty day mortality rate was 3% (n = 2). Early unplanned re-interventions occurred in four patients (6%). No strokes or SCI were observed. Median follow up was 6 months (IQR 2, 10). There were no late deaths, and primary patency of all branches was 100%. One late unplanned re-intervention, unrelated to the TBE device, was required. During follow up, 12 patients (19%) had endoleaks, including type II (n = 4), type Ia (n = 4), type Ib (n = 2), type III (n = 1), and type V (n = 1). Estimated freedom from type Ia endoleak at 12 months was 93 ± 3%, while estimated overall survival at 12 months was 97 ± 2%. CONCLUSION: TBE demonstrated high technical success and acceptable early outcomes across a range of aortic arch pathologies. However, the relatively high rate of endoleaks and need for early re-interventions highlight the importance of careful patient selection and close continuous post-operative surveillance.

METHODS: This multicentre retrospective study, conducted and reported in accordance with the STROBE statement, included consecutive patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair with TBE between February 2024 and July 2025. articles.title: Sex differences in cardiovascular disease burden, risk factors, and disease spectrum in Europe: a global burden of disease 2023 analysis within the ESC Atlas framework.
articles.abstract: Despite growing recognition of sex disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD), contemporary, harmonized analyses of sex-specific burden in the European region that could inform targeted prevention strategies, remain limited. Sex-specific patterns in CVD burden and risk factor exposure across 55 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) member countries were examined using data from the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. Risk factor exposure was quantified using age-sex-standardized summary exposure values for 10 established cardiovascular risk factors. Disease incidence and mortality for major CVD categories, including maternal hypertensive disorders, were estimated by calculating age-sex-standardized rates per 100 000 person-years using the 2013 European Standard Population. Analyses were performed by sex at country, regional, and ESC-wide levels and over time (1990-2023). In 2023, in the ESC region, the overall CVD burden was broadly similar in men and women, with women accounting for 55% (6.0 million) of cases and 50% of deaths (1.5 million). This apparent parity, however, concealed marked sex differences in disease composition, risk exposure, and geographic disparities. Compared with men, women had a lower proportion of CVD due to ischaemic heart disease (21% vs 38%) and a higher contribution from peripheral arterial disease (23% vs 19%). Major differences were also apparent in risk profiles, particularly for behavioural risk factors-with summary exposure values of tobacco and alcohol being 10%-20% points higher in men than women; contrasting with cardiometabolic factors, such as high body mass index and low physical activity, that were often 5%-15% points higher in women than men, and more modest differences in environmental and biological risks, including air pollution, fasting glucose, or cholesterol. Cardiovascular disease burden further varied widely across countries and disparities affected women more strongly than men, with an approximately three-fold difference between the lowest- and highest-incidence countries in women, compared with a two-fold difference in men, and even larger disparities in mortality and premature mortality (up to 25-fold in women). Maternal hypertensive disorders substantially shaped both the scale and composition of CVD burden in women, accounting for 25% of incident CVD in women and exhibiting substantial geographic variation, with up to 18-fold differences in incidence across countries. These findings challenge conventional approaches that treat CVD as a homogeneous condition. In particular, the substantial contribution of non-ischaemic conditions and maternal hypertensive disorders to the burden in women, alongside distinct patterns of risk exposure and wider geographic disparities, underscore the importance of adopting a life-course and sex- and gender-informed approach to cardiovascular prevention and policy.

Risk factor exposure was quantified using age-sex-standardized summary exposure values for 10 established cardiovascular risk factors.

articles.title: Lesion Water Content on CT Predicts 12-Month Outcome and Modifies Thrombectomy Effect in Large-Core Stroke-A Secondary Analysis of the TENSION Trial.
articles.abstract: In large-core ischemic stroke, outcomes after thrombectomy remain heterogeneous, and imaging markers that capture treatment-modifiable injury beyond lesion extent are needed. We investigated whether lesion water content on noncontrast CT, quantified as net water uptake (NWU), predicts 12-month functional outcome and modifies the effect of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). This secondary analysis of the randomized TENSION trial included 198 patients with admission CT suitable for NWU quantification and available 12-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores; 168 had paired 24-h CT for follow-up NWU (NWUFU) assessment. The primary outcome was ordinal 12-month mRS. Multivariable ordinal and logistic regression tested associations and the NWU × EVT interaction, with discrimination assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Median baseline NWU was 16.4% and NWUFU 28.9%. At 12 months, 45 patients (23%) had mRS 0-3 and 111 (56%) had died. Higher baseline NWU independently predicted worse 12-month mRS (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR], 1.10 per percentage-point; 95% CI, 1.05-1.16; P < 0.001) and modified the EVT effect (interaction acOR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.30; P = 0.002), with greater discrimination than ASPECTS. NWUFU was the strongest single imaging predictor (acOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; P < 0.001; AUC, 0.78 for mRS 0-3) and superseded baseline NWU when co-modeled. Among 97 90-day survivors, higher NWUFU independently predicted late mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.18; P = 0.019). Lesion water content may therefore provide a clinically accessible CT biomarker linking treatment-modifiable injury at baseline with realized post-treatment injury and long-term outcome.

articles.title: AI-enhanced intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery: from augmented reality navigation to foundation models.
articles.abstract: Robotic surgical platforms have improved instrument dexterity, tremor filtration, and ergonomic control, yet intraoperative decisions still depend on a surgeon interpreting a moving, partially observed field under time pressure. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to close parts of this loop by recognizing anatomy, tracking instruments, anticipating events, and-experimentally-planning or executing selected actions. This review maps the computational technologies that support intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery and appraises the clinical evidence for them.Because the direct robotic evidence base is still uneven, we explicitly distinguish three kinds of material: (i) studies conducted on robotic systems during surgery; (ii) non-robotic surgical evidence from laparoscopic and thoracoscopic procedures that use the same vision and workflow methods; and (iii) preclinical, preoperative, and perioperative work that is conceptually relevant but not intraoperative. Robotic and non-robotic settings are labeled throughout the tables and text. We further separate non-AI image guidance-indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence and registered overlays-from AI-based inference, and we include image-guided endovascular robotics as a complementary setting in which fluoroscopic perception, vascular-topology reasoning, and closed-loop instrument control are particularly advanced.We organize the field into four computational layers: perception, anatomical and procedural reasoning, action planning, and control and execution. Augmented-reality and fluorescence navigation can improve orientation and selected intermediate outcomes, and several randomized trials now exist. Computer-vision systems can recognize anatomy, phases, instruments, and adverse events, and in endovascular work they can track guidewires and reason over vascular topology. Foundation models broaden language and multimodal capabilities but remain, in surgery, largely preclinical. Autonomous subtasks have shown promise in phantoms, animals, and a small number of carefully bounded tissue tasks; no system has demonstrated safe, accountable patient-level autonomous decision-making.Navigation and AI-assisted systems have improved orientation, reduced ischemia, and accelerated recognition of critical events in some studies. Whether these intermediate gains improve patient outcomes, generalize across institutions, or justify their cost remains unknown. The question is not whether AI can interpret surgical scenes, but which decisions can be delegated, with what evidence, uncertainty limits, oversight, and outcome measures.

articles.title: Multi-modality non-invasive cardiovascular screening and sex-specific outcomes: the Viborg Screening Program.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Cardiovascular screening has been shown to reduce mortality in trials involving men. This study evaluated the effect of cardiovascular screening in both sexes, with all-cause mortality as the primary outcome. METHODS: The Viborg Screening Program, a prospective, population-based study in Denmark, in which the intervention consisted of inviting all 67-year olds to screening for carotid plaque, lower extremity artery disease, abdominal aortic aneurysm, hypertension, cardiac arrhythmia/ischaemia, and diabetes mellitus. This cohort included invitees from the first 5 years (2014-2019). Controls were 67-year olds without screening access. Effects were evaluated using propensity score matching (1:3 ratio, nearest-neighbour matching) and analysed using Cox proportional hazards models under the intention-to-invite principle. Sex-stratified analyses of all-cause mortality were conducted post hoc. RESULTS: Among 5505 invitees, three died before inclusion and 4602 participated (83.6%). Ninety individuals lacked registry information. After matching, 5412 invitees and 16 236 controls were included. During a median follow-up of 5.8 years, 372 (6.9%) invitees and 1444 (8.9%) controls died [hazard ratio (HR) 0.76, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.68-0.85; P < .001]. The number needed to invite to save one life was 49. The HR for cardiovascular mortality was 0.76 (95% CI 0.56-1.03), for major adverse cardiovascular events 1.10 (95% CI 1.01-1.19), and for major adverse limb events 0.70 (95% CI 0.50-0.98). All-cause mortality HRs were 0.73 (95% CI 0.63-0.84) for men, 0.82 (95% CI 0.68-0.98) for women, 0.70 (95% CI 0.61-0.80) for those without prior cardiovascular disease (CVD), and 0.97 (95% CI 0.78-1.21) for those with prior CVD. CONCLUSIONS: Multi-modality non-invasive cardiovascular screening reduced 5-year all-cause mortality among 67-year olds, also when stratified by sex. Prioritizing individuals without known CVD may enhance population-level impact.
