articles.title: Emergency Endovascular Repair of a Large Ruptured Isolated Internal Iliac Artery Aneurysm in a 98-Year-Old Patient: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Case Presentation: Conclusions: Isolated internal iliac artery aneurysm (IIAA) is rare and carries a high mortality when ruptured. Management is particularly challenging in very elderly, anticoagulated patients in whom open repair may carry substantial perioperative risk. Herein, we report a case that illustrates device selection when a marked common iliac-external iliac size discrepancy precludes bridging with the available iliac limbs.A 98-year-old man receiving apixaban presented with lower abdominal pain, nausea, and diarrhea. Computed tomography demonstrated a ruptured right IIAA measuring 79 × 72 mm in the axial plane, with retroperitoneal hematoma. A marked size discrepancy between the common iliac artery (20 mm) and external iliac artery (approximately 10 mm), together with vessel tortuosity, made common iliac-external iliac bridging with an iliac limb unsuitable with the devices available. Emergency endovascular aneurysm repair with a full aortic bifurcated endograft was combined with coil embolization of the inferior gluteal artery and gelatin sponge embolization of the sac. The contralateral internal iliac artery, which harbored a 31 mm aneurysm, was preserved. A suspected type IV endoleak had resolved on CT at day 4, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 8 without complications. At 6-month follow-up, the aneurysm sac had decreased from 79 × 72 mm to 72 × 62 mm in the axial plane with no evidence of endoleak, and he remained ambulatory without pelvic ischemic symptoms.A full aortic bifurcated endograft combined with coil and sac embolization may be a feasible bail-out option when a marked common iliac-external iliac size discrepancy precludes bridging with the available iliac limbs, even in a nonagenarian receiving apixaban.

articles.title: Patient Selection and Evidence for Intervention in Deep Vein Thrombosis and Pulmonary Embolism.
articles.abstract: Intervention for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) should address a clinical problem that anticoagulation alone may not resolve. This narrative review separates whether to intervene, which procedure to choose, and how to maintain benefit. The review covers publications through 10 September 2026, with a later STORM-PE follow-up report identified separately. Anticoagulation remains foundational. In acute iliofemoral DVT, selected patients may gain earlier symptom relief or less severe post-thrombotic disease, but trials do not support routine thrombus removal. In established post-thrombotic obstruction, C-TRACT showed better six-month clinical severity and quality of life with stenting and enhanced antithrombotic treatment, alongside more bleeding. In selected stable PE, HI-PEITHO reduced a seven-day clinical composite from 10.3% to 4.0%, mainly through fewer episodes of decompensation; a survival benefit remains unproven. Procedure comparisons and imaging trials answer narrower questions than benefit over medical care. Limb-threatening DVT and unstable PE require urgent rescue assessment. A five-scenario table and clinical examples connect this evidence to symptoms, anatomy, recovery goals, bleeding risk, and the feasibility of continuing treatment and follow-up.

articles.title: Preprocedural Serum Albumin and Early Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury After Elective Carotid Artery Stenting: Incremental Prognostic Information Beyond the PCI-Derived Mehran Score.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: 2 p We assessed whether preprocedural serum albumin adds prognostic information to the PCI-derived Mehran score for early contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after elective carotid artery stenting (CAS).This single-centre retrospective cohort included 121 consecutive elective patients (January 2020-April 2026). The primary model combined the reconstructed Mehran score with albumin < 3.5 g/dL, a conventional threshold fixed in advance. Because the score uses actual contrast volume, the combined model applies only after CAS. The outcome used KDIGO serum creatinine thresholds (≥0.3 mg/dL or ≥1.5 times baseline) from routine second-day testing. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples.Early CA-AKI occurred in 32 patients (26.4%). Adjusted odds ratios were 1.35 per Mehran point (95% CI 1.13-1.60) and 11.68 for albumin < 3.5 g/dL (95% CI 4.14-32.97). AUC increased from 0.768 to 0.865 (95% CI 0.794-0.937; likelihood ratio χ= 24.58,< 0.001). Corrected AUC, calibration slope, and Brier score were 0.860, 0.96, and 0.132. In exploratory decision curves (20% threshold), corrected net benefit was 0.168 for the combined model and 0.133 for Mehran alone.Low preprocedural albumin added prognostic information to the PCI-derived score and may help select patients for closer renal surveillance after CAS. External validation and prospective impact studies are needed before clinical use.

articles.title: From hypoxia to thrombosis: a hypothesis-driven framework for pulmonary embolism risk in deep underground environments.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is one of the most severe manifestations of venous thromboembolism, yet current diagnostic and preventive frameworks have largely been developed in ground-based clinical settings. Deep underground environments represent complex occupational exposure systems characterized by relative hypoxia or oxygen fluctuation, normobaric to mildly hyperbaric pressure, high humidity and heat, airborne particulates, radon accumulation, restricted ventilation, limited mobility, circadian disruption, and enclosed psychosocial stress. These factors may interact dynamically with oxygen sensing, cardiopulmonary compensation, venous return, endothelial function, and coagulation-inflammation pathways. However, the relationship between deep underground exposure, thrombogenesis, PE recognition, and prevention remains insufficiently conceptualized. Direct epidemiological evidence linking deep-underground occupational exposure to incident venous thromboembolism or PE remains scarce, and existing PE prediction tools have not been specifically validated in deep-underground occupational populations. Therefore, this review does not assume that underground exposure independently increases PE incidence or that established clinical tools are inadequate. Instead, we develop a hypothesis-driven framework to examine whether exposure-related factors-including oxygen fluctuation, heat and dehydration, restricted mobility, altered hemodynamics, and inflammatory stress-could modify thrombotic susceptibility, symptom interpretation, or the operational performance of conventional PE pathways. We summarize the environmental and physiological stressors relevant to PE, examine how they may amplify Virchow's triad, and discuss research questions concerning symptom recognition, anticoagulation, reperfusion decision-making, preventive interventions, and the staged development of dynamic risk warning models. This review aims to provide a conceptual foundation for future surveillance, prevention, and clinical research on PE in deep underground occupational populations.

articles.title: From revascularization to multimodal integrated therapy for peripheral arterial disease: immunomodulation, metabolic correction, and tissue engineering.
articles.abstract: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD), a critical manifestation of systemic atherosclerosis (AS), poses substantial therapeutic challenges. Despite pharmacological interventions and revascularization, efficacy remains constrained by high restenosis rates and suboptimal functional recovery. These limitations underscore a necessary transition from localized structural revascularization toward integrated systemic repair, with a particular focus on the underlying immunopathology. The progression of PAD is driven by a dysregulated immune response, characterized by an imbalance in macrophage polarization (M1/M2), overactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, and a vicious cycle of immune-metabolic coupling. Current research trajectories emphasize the synergistic orchestration of the vascular microenvironment through immunomodulation. Beyond modulating localized inflammatory responses, emerging strategies target metabolic homeostasis and advanced tissue engineering, including spatiotemporal growth factor delivery, extracellular vesicle-based therapies, and bioengineered scaffolding systems. These interdisciplinary developments point toward a multimodal integrated therapeutic strategy for PAD. Such a strategy would build on conventional revascularization and may address its limitations, including restenosis, through targeted immunomodulation and local tissue regeneration. Whether this approach can improve long-term outcomes compared with revascularization alone remains to be tested. If validated, it could shift the clinical standard beyond vessel patency toward comprehensive, long-term vascular health.

articles.title: Cause-Specific Endovascular Thrombectomy Time Windows in Basilar Artery Occlusion: ATTENTION Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) outperforms best medical treatment (BMT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO), but the influence of stroke cause on the time sensitivity of EVT remains unclear. We hypothesized nonatherosclerotic BAO would require earlier EVT, whereas atherosclerotic BAO-with chronic stenosis and more robust collaterals-would retain EVT benefit in extended windows. We conducted a post hoc 3-way interaction analysis of the ATTENTION trial (Trial of Endovascular Treatment of Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion) to explore cause-specific EVT time patterns. METHODS: Using randomized ATTENTION trial data (36 Chinese centers, 2021-2022), patients were stratified by onset-to-puncture time (<6 versus ≥6 hours) and TOAST (Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment) cause (atherosclerotic: large-artery atherosclerosis; nonatherosclerotic: cardioembolism/undetermined/other causes). The primary outcome was 90-day favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-3), with relative risk as the primary estimand; the 3-way interaction was tested via joint Wald test. A weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis served as an exploratory tool, with multivariable regression adjusting for confounders. RESULTS: P P P P P P Among 340 patients (226 EVT+BMT, 114 BMT), for onset-to-puncture time <6 hours, patients without atherosclerosis with EVT achieved a significantly higher favorable outcome rate (46.7% versus 20.4%; relative risk, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.25-4.18];=0.007); patients with atherosclerosis showed numerical outcome benefit (40.4% versus 26.1%,=0.259). For onset-to-puncture time ≥6 hours, numerical benefit of patients with atherosclerosis increased from 14.3% to 30.6% (56.9% versus 26.3%;=0.199), accompanied by ordinal modified Rankin Scale score improvement (common odds ratio, 3.30 [95% CI, 1.13-9.62];=0.029) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score reduction; patients without atherosclerosis' benefit decreased from 26.3% to 17.8% with loss of significance (39.5% versus 21.7%,=0.341). The treatment time×cause interaction was not significant (=0.662). The weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis identified a provisional 5.3-hour reference point in patients without atherosclerosis. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with nonatherosclerotic BAO, atherosclerotic BAO appears less time-sensitive, potentially retaining EVT responsiveness over longer windows. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04751708.

articles.title: Comparison of DOAC Versus VKA for Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral venous thrombosis is an uncommon cause of stroke that primarily affects young adults. Several clinical trials and observational studies have compared vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) for treating cerebral venous thrombosis, but the small sample sizes limit the ability to draw firm conclusions. METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing DOACs with VKAs for the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. Studies published between January 2007 and July 2025 were included. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by study design, DOAC class (anti-factor Xa inhibitors versus direct thrombin inhibitors), and VKA. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool 2 for randomized trials and the Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions for observational studies. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models. RESULTS: P Fourteen studies (8 randomized clinical trials [RCTs] and 6 observational studies) were included. Among 3698 patients, 1669 (45.1%) received DOACs and 2029 (54.9%) received VKAs. Rates of recurrent venous thromboembolism (10.24% versus 10.99%), major bleeding (4.26% versus 6.18%), clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (2.63% versus 1.66%), good functional outcomes (95.09% versus 89.25%), and mortality (3.37% versus 3.30%) were similar in DOACs and VKAs. Recurrent venous thromboembolism was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.35-3.24]) and in the overall pooled analysis of all studies (RR, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.55-1.53]). Major bleeding did not differ between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.24-2.22]) or in the overall analysis (RR, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.44-1.25];=0.26). Clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was also comparable in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.25-4.48]) and overall (RR, 1.22 [95% CI, 0.38-3.86]). Good functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-2) were similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.84-1.19]) and in the combined analysis of all studies (RR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.11]). Mortality was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.28-4.68]) and in the pooled analysis. When direct thrombin inhibitors were compared with factor Xa inhibitors, there were no significant differences in outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: DOACs demonstrated comparable efficacy and safety to VKAs in the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. These findings support the use of DOACs as a reasonable alternative.

Several clinical trials and observational studies have compared vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) for treating cerebral venous thrombosis, but the small sample sizes limit the ability to draw firm conclusions. METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing DOACs with VKAs for the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
articles.abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.

articles.title: Determinants of Futile Recanalization and the Influence of Age After Endovascular Therapy for Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives Materials and Methods Results n n Conclusions : Functional independence is not always achieved after successful recanalization with endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, a phenomenon termed futile recanalization (FR). We investigated factors independently associated with FR and explored whether these associations differed by age.: In this retrospective single-center study, 231 consecutive patients treated with EVT between January 2021 and December 2024 were analyzed. FR was defined as a modified Rankin Scale score > 2 at 90 days despite a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) grade of 2b-3. Model 1 included all patients with successful recanalization. Model 2 was restricted to patients with anterior circulation infarction and assessable imaging and additionally included the Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) and collateral status. Age interactions were tested.: Recanalization was successful in 191 patients (82.7%), of whom 114 (59.7%) had FR. In Model 1 (= 191), admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score (odds ratio [OR], 1.29 per point; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.18-1.42), admission glucose (OR, 1.01; 1.00-1.02), and puncture-to-recanalization time (OR, 1.02; 1.00-1.03) were independently associated with FR. In Model 2 (= 146), sufficient collateral status (OR, 0.19; 0.08-0.47), ASPECTS (OR, 0.60; 0.39-0.91), NIHSS score, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), dyslipidemia, and procedural duration were independently associated with FR, whereas glucose was not retained; Model 2 had an area under the curve of 0.88. Age ≥ 80 years was not independently associated with FR; the only significant interaction was with glucose in Model 1.: Stroke severity and procedural duration were independently associated with FR in both models. Imaging variables contributed to prognostic assessment in anterior circulation infarction. Age ≥ 80 years was not independently associated with FR. The NLR association and age-stratified findings remain exploratory.

articles.title: Circulating Lipids, Statins, and Metformin in Thoracic and Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: I I 2 2 Thoracic and abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAA and AAA) progress silently, and no drug has been shown to slow their growth. Circulating lipids, statins, and metformin are candidate disease modifiers, but the evidence is heterogeneous and largely observational. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 24 March 2025, with an update of MEDLINE to 3 October 2026, for randomized and cohort studies of adults with established AAA or TAA. Aneurysm growth was standardized to mm/year and pooled with random-effects models when at least three comparable studies were available. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed with ROBINS-I and GRADE. Thirty-three studies were included, 32 observational and one randomized; fewer than 20% of participants were women. Circulating lipid fractions showed no consistent association with aneurysm growth. Statin use was associated with slower growth (mean difference -0.78 mm/year; 95% CI -1.13 to -0.43;= 92.4%; 95% prediction interval -2.02 to 0.46 mm/year), lower all-cause mortality, and fewer aortic complications. In AAA, metformin use was associated with slower growth in observational studies (-0.34 mm/year; 95% CI -0.48 to -0.20;= 46.3%), while the single randomized trial found no difference. Certainty of evidence was low to very low. In these largely observational data, aneurysm progression was more closely related to statin and metformin use than to circulating lipid levels, a pattern that is hypothesis-generating and from which causality cannot be inferred.

articles.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound Use in Confirmed Acute Aortic Syndrome: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study at the Ljubljana Emergency Medical Unit.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p p p p p Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used in emergency care, but data on its use in acute aortic syndrome (AAS) remains limited. This single-center retrospective cohort described POCUS use among patients with confirmed AAS and explored factors associated with POCUS use and time to completion of diagnostic workup.Records coded ICD10 I71.0-I71.8 from the Emergency Medical Unit, University Medical Centre Ljubljana (2019-2023) were reviewed. Clinical, imaging, and outcome data were extracted, and diagnoses were confirmed by two investigators through manual chart review of ED documentation, radiology reports, and specialist consultation notes. Fisher's exact and Wilcoxon rank sum tests were used for comparisons. Associations with POCUS use and time to completion of diagnostic workup (defined from arrival at triage to completion of the emergency department workup) were assessed with univariable logistic regression and linear regression models, respectively. Survival was explored using univariable Cox proportional-hazards models. Statistical significance was set at< 0.05.Among 120,109 emergency department visits, 73 patients had confirmed AAS (type A: 48; type B: 17; intramural hematoma: 8). POCUS was performed in 62% of patients, more often in those who were hemodynamically unstable (87.5% vs. 54.4%;= 0.020) or had unclear presentations (40% vs. 7%;= 0.003). Median time to completion of diagnostic workup was shorter with POCUS (110 vs. 213 min), though not statistically significant (= 0.069). Hemodynamic instability was associated with higher odds of POCUS use (OR 5.87, 95% CI 1.22-28.2;= 0.028), whereas a clear clinical presentation was associated with lower odds of POCUS use (OR 0.12, 95% CI 0.02-0.55;= 0.007). Lower triage level was associated with longer time to completion of diagnostic workup (time ratio 5.43, 95% CI 2.21-13.4;< 0.001 for urgent vs. immediate triage), whereas very high D-dimer levels were associated with shorter time to completion of diagnostic workup (time ratio 0.44, 95% CI 0.21-0.93;= 0.031 for highest vs. lowest quartile). In-hospital mortality was 14%, with only age associated with mortality (HR 1.06 per year, 95% CI 1.02-1.11;= 0.007).In this single-center retrospective AAS cohort, POCUS was used more frequently in unstable and diagnostically unclear patients but was not associated with time to completion of diagnostic workup. Findings are descriptive and exploratory; they do not establish that POCUS accelerates diagnosis or improves outcomes.

articles.title: Understanding Venous Remodeling After Minimally Invasive and Noninvasive Treatments for Varicose Veins: A Mechanistic Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: The absence of detectable flow on duplex ultrasound after venous ablation may correspond to different tissue states. This mechanistic narrative review examines histopathological and immunohistochemical responses after thermal, chemical, mechanochemical, adhesive, and focused ultrasound treatments. The PubMed search, conducted on 6 September 2026 for publications available through 31 August 2026, resulted in the inclusion of 45 tissue-based publications; six additional references provided clinical context. Study selection and data extraction were performed by a single author. Human and experimental data were organized by wall compartment, treatment modality, and time point. Depending on the technique, the initial signatures comprised thermal injury, endothelial detergent toxicity, mechanical abrasion, adhesive polymerization, or cavitation. Luminal organization, fibrosis, and recanalization followed heterogeneous trajectories. Cyanoacrylate was distinguished by a biomaterial response with variable persistence. Early occlusion does not demonstrate mature fibrous obliteration. The depth-continuity-topography framework is a working hypothesis without validated predictive value. Combining longitudinal duplex ultrasound follow-up with end-point histological analysis of the same segment, including morphometry, immunohistochemistry, and matrix assessment, could better relate tissue status to clinical outcome.

articles.title: Aspirin-Based Thromboprophylaxis Versus Anticoagulant Regimens After Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives Materials and Methods Results Conclusions : Aspirin is widely used for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, uncertainty remains regarding its efficacy and safety compared with anticoagulant regimens. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated aspirin-based thromboprophylaxis versus anticoagulant regimens following THA or TKA.: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched through July 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing aspirin-based prophylaxis with anticoagulant regimens. The primary outcomes were any deep vein thrombosis (DVT), symptomatic DVT, and symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE). Secondary outcomes included pulmonary embolism (PE), proximal and distal DVT, bleeding outcomes, wound complications, blood transfusion, and mortality. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Additional risk-difference sensitivity analyses incorporated CRISTAL's published cluster-adjusted estimates.: Sixteen trials involving 21,265 participants were included. Aspirin was associated with higher risks of symptomatic DVT (RR 1.79, 95% CI 1.35-2.38), symptomatic VTE (RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.33-2.18), PE (RR 1.89, 95% CI 1.33-2.68), and distal DVT (RR 1.47, 95% CI 1.06-2.06). Aspirin was associated with lower risks of minor bleeding (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.31-0.71) and ecchymosis or bruising (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.39-0.93). No statistically significant differences were detected for the other assessed outcomes. Additional analyses incorporating CRISTAL's cluster-adjusted risk differences did not identify statistically significant differences for the three primary outcomes or PE.: The main pooled analyses associated aspirin-based thromboprophylaxis with higher risks of symptomatic thromboembolic events. However, the symptomatic DVT and symptomatic VTE associations were no longer statistically significant after exclusion of CRISTAL or restriction to trials at low risk of bias. The low-risk analysis identified a significantly higher risk of any DVT with aspirin. Aspirin reduced minor bleeding and bruising without a statistically significant reduction in major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding. These findings require cautious interpretation given dependence on CRISTAL, sensitivity to trial inclusion and analytical approach, and differences in prophylactic strategies and outcome definitions.

articles.title: Early and follow-up results of reinterventions for type 2 endoleak following endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm: The multicenter REinterventions for Type 2 Endoleak study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Type II endoleak (T2EL) is frequent after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair and may require reintervention in selected patients. However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. This study aimed to retrospectively evaluate the perioperative and long-term outcomes of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from 20 high-volume academic centers. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of consecutive patients undergoing first reintervention for T2ELs was conducted across 20 centers over a 10-year period. Patients requiring concomitant treatment for other endoleak types were excluded. A total of 403 patients were included. Primary outcomes included technical success, 30-day AAA-related mortality and reintervention-free survival during follow-up. Secondary outcomes were perioperative complications, early reintervention, overall survival, freedom from aneurysm-related death and rupture, freedom from recurrent endoleaks, freedom from open conversion or semiconversion in patients previously treated endovascularly and sac behavior during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression analyses were performed to analyze follow-up results. RESULTS: Patients were predominantly male (90%) with a mean age of 77 years. Reintervention was indicated for sac enlargement in 94.5% of cases; 4% presented with rupture. Median time from endovascular AAA repair to reintervention was 4.3 years. Lumbar arteries (55%) and the inferior mesenteric artery (35%) were the main sources. Endovascular treatment was performed in 86% and open conversion/semiconversion in 14%. Technical success was 96%, with 1% mortality and 4% major complications. Overall survival was 80.5% and rupture-free survival 79.2% at 5 years. Recurrent T2EL occurred in 64.2%, and reintervention-free survival was 48.3%. Endovascular group showed significantly lower freedom from reintervention rates when compared to open conversion/semiconversion group [42.4% vs 86.8%; standard error, 0.04 vs standard error, 0.05; P < .001; log-rank, 15.9]. Conversion/semiconversion after endovascular treatment occurred in 14%. No differences were recorded comparing different fabric materials of the endograft in terms of freedom for reintervention and freedom from open surgery. A sac diameter ≥7 cm at the time of reintervention predicted further reinterventions, whereas primary open treatment improved durability. CONCLUSIONS: Reinterventions for T2ELs are safe, with satisfactory immediate technical success and low perioperative mortality. During follow-up, risks of rupture and AAA-related death remain low. However, the endoleak recurrence rate exceeds 60% at 5 years, necessitating reintervention in over 40% of patients. Early intervention for patients with a sac diameter approaching 7 cm can be suggested, whereas a primary open approach may be considered in low-risk patients.

articles.title: Contemporary Analysis of the Volume-Outcome Relationship for Patients With Nontraumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) carries a substantial mortality burden and risk of long-term morbidity. Although prior investigations have demonstrated an inverse association between SAH admission volume and in-hospital mortality, reported thresholds remain broad. Importantly, the relative importance of both admission and procedural volume has yet to be evaluated on a national scale. We examined the association of volume metrics with outcomes in an SAH cohort. METHODS: All adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of nontraumatic SAH were identified from the 2016 to 2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Multivariable regression models were developed to evaluate the independent and joint associations of SAH admission and clipping and coiling procedural volume with in-hospital outcomes. RESULTS: P P Of an estimated 142 271 hospitalizations, index mortality was 20.2%. Following risk adjustment, both increasing SAH admission volume and clipping and coiling procedural volume were independently associated with reduced mortality. When modeled jointly, however, clipping and coiling procedural volume remained an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 0.981 per 10 procedures,<0.001) whereas SAH admission volume was no longer significant (=0.40). CONCLUSIONS: Joint examination of SAH and clipping and coiling procedural volume revealed procedural caseload to be the dominant predictor of in-hospital mortality, suggesting that survival benefits historically attributed to admission volume may be more precisely explained by procedural expertise. These findings support reexamination of volume-based benchmarks in contemporary cerebrovascular care frameworks.

articles.title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year. RESULTS: P P Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively;=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]);for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin. CONCLUSIONS: Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

articles.title: Exercise and Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: A Paradigm Shift Toward Informed, Personalized Activity Guidelines.
articles.abstract: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.

articles.title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: 2 2 2 2 This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models. RESULTS: P P for interaction for interaction In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (<0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80],<0.05). CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

articles.title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. RESULTS: P Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. articles.title: Omega-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Peripheral Artery Disease: An Individual Participant-Level Analysis of 9 International Prospective Studies.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have previously been associated with several peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk factors. We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis. METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline. Omega-6 PUFAs were measured at baseline and with a median follow-up of 14 years. Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were conducted in individual cohorts to evaluate associations of omega-6 PUFAs (continuous cohort-standardized interquintile ranges [difference between the medians of the 10th and 90th omega-6 PUFAs percentiles] and cohort-specific quintiles) with incident clinical PAD adjusting for prespecified covariates. Inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to calculate the combined hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs. RESULTS: P Linoleic acid (LA) was measured in all 9 cohorts, arachidonic acid in 8 (N=33 541; PAD cases=1766), dihomo-γ-LA and γ-LA in 7 (N=29 861; PAD cases=1686), and eicosadienoic acid in 6 (N=27 538; PAD cases=1435). Only LA was associated with a lower risk of incident PAD (quintile 5 versus quintile 1: HR, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.64-0.89];=0.0009). Results did not differ in a statistically significant manner by age, sex, diabetes status, or smoking status. CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the omega-6 PUFA LA may be protective against PAD, and other omega-6 PUFAs are not associated with PAD incidence. This is further evidence that omega-6 PUFA-disease relationships should be evaluated by individual fatty acids rather than grouped as total omega-6 PUFAs.

articles.title: COG5 Whole-Genome Sequencing and Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identify Human Leukocyte Antigen Loci and aVariant in Aortic Dissection.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection (AD) is a lethal cardiovascular emergency with a complex and underexplored genetic basis. METHODS: We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci. To pinpoint functional candidates, we integrated epigenomic profiles and single-cell transcriptomes from human aortic tissues. RESULTS: HLA-A HLA-DQA2 COG5 TPM4 Whole-genome sequencing analysis identified 21 candidate common loci and 2 low-frequency variants associated with AD in this discovery cohort. Two candidate common variants in the human leukocyte antigen region (rs9260945 nearand rs9276409 within) showed strong associations and colocalized with regulatory elements in aortic and immune cells, indicating immune-mediated vascular pathology. A low-frequency missense variant in thegene (rs1203229795, effect allele frequency=0.019) emerged as an independent AD risk factor, likely affecting extracellular matrix glycosylation. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of AD-associated variants in human aortic tissues demonstrated enhanced interactions among fibroblasts, vascular smooth muscle cells, and macrophages, supporting their roles in AD pathogenesis. Integrated gene-based and expression analyses further highlighted, a marker of vascular smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation, as a putative susceptibility gene in AD. CONCLUSIONS: COG5 This multiomics investigation expands the genetic landscape of sporadic AD in Chinese individuals, revealing immune-related human leukocyte antigen loci and a functionally supported candidatevariant. Our findings offer new insights into AD pathogenesis and identify candidate targets for future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Impact of Continuous Baseline and Discharge Blood Pressure on Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence linking pre- and post-transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) blood pressure (BP) with cardiovascular outcomes is scarce. This study investigated the associations of pre- and post-TAVI BP and their changes as a continuous variable with cardiovascular outcomes. METHODS: Patients undergoing TAVI at a tertiary university hospital between 2011 and 2025 with office BP available before and after TAVI were included. The primary outcome was a composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE) at 1 year. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models incorporating restricted cubic splines for continuous variables were fitted. RESULTS: P Among 1191 patients, BP remained relatively stable from pre-TAVI to 1-year follow-up. Both discharge systolic BP and absolute changes therein from pre- to post-TAVI were significantly associated with MACE at 1 year (<0.001 for both), whereas baseline systolic BP showed no significant association. BP values <115 mm Hg or >143 mm Hg were associated with a higher risk of MACE 1 year after TAVI. A decrease in systolic BP of -5 to -25 mm Hg was also associated with a lower risk of MACE compared with no change. CONCLUSIONS: While BP remains generally stable in the year following TAVI, both very low and high systolic BP at discharge were associated with higher 1-year MACE. Furthermore, moderate decreases in systolic BP from baseline to discharge appear to be protective. These findings highlight the potential prognostic value of BP optimization during TAVI follow-up and support the role of BP measurements as a clinically translatable, independently associated with long-term outcomes after TAVI.

articles.title: Inflammatory bowel disease and the heart: how trained immunity shapes cardiovascular outcomes.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), comprising Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, is a chronic relapsing intestinal inflammatory disorder. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death in patients with IBD, with elevated risks of myocardial infarction, heart failure, stroke, and venous thromboembolism that are independent of traditional risk factors. Disease activity and histological inflammation independently predict major adverse cardiovascular events, and Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis differ in cardiovascular risk profiles. This residual risk points to immune mechanisms that remain unclear. Trained immunity (TI), an innate immune memory induced by epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, may link chronic intestinal inflammation to cardiovascular injury. This review integrates epidemiological and mechanistic evidence, outlines cardiovascular risk features in IBD, examines the molecular basis of TI and its roles in atherosclerosis, myocardial injury, and heart failure, and evaluates candidate biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies. We also discuss current limitations and challenges in clinical translation and propose future research directions, to inform mechanistic studies and clinical interventions for IBD-associated CVD.

articles.title: Perioperative prothrombin time activity trajectories and subsequent mortality after surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Perioperative prothrombin time activity (PTA) changes rapidly during surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), but single measurements do not capture heterogeneous longitudinal patterns. We sought to identify recurring perioperative PTA trajectories, characterize their clinical context, and examine their association with subsequent all-cause mortality. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 284 adults who underwent ATAAD repair from 2021 through 2023. Group-based trajectory modeling used the last preoperative and observed postoperative day (POD) 1-7 PTA measurements. Patients required at least three observed PTA measurements for trajectory modeling. Mortality analyses began immediately after POD7. The primary Cox model adjusted for age and sex; Firth regression addressed sparse events. Incremental information beyond last preoperative PTA was evaluated by a prespecified likelihood-ratio comparison. RESULTS: P P P P P The trajectory cohort comprised 268 patients with 1,895 observations and 27 deaths after POD7. Four perioperative PTA trajectory groups were identified: moderate-stable [87 (32.5%)], low-declining [50 (18.7%)], preserved-rapidly-declining [61 (22.8%)], and high-preserved [70 (26.1%)]. Cumulative mortality differed globally (log-rank = 0.00210), and trajectory group remained associated with subsequent mortality in the age- and sex-adjusted Cox model (global = 0.0322) and Firth sensitivity analysis (global = 0.0481). The prespecified direct low-declining-versus-preserved-rapidly-declining comparison did not demonstrate a clear difference. Adding trajectory group to age, sex, and last preoperative PTA did not show clear incremental information (likelihood-ratio = 0.304; Firth = 0.380). After exclusion of mechanical-valve recipients, the principal trajectory structure was largely preserved, although this sensitivity analysis did not exclude treatment-related effects on PTA. CONCLUSION: Four reproducible perioperative PTA trajectories characterized distinct longitudinal patterns and were associated with mortality after the POD7 landmark. These trajectories should be interpreted as composite perioperative patterns reflecting both disease and treatment context rather than as intrinsic coagulation states. They were not ordered mortality-risk tiers and did not show clear incremental prognostic information beyond last preoperative PTA. External validation is required.

We sought to identify recurring perioperative PTA trajectories, characterize their clinical context, and examine their association with subsequent all-cause mortality. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 284 adults who underwent ATAAD repair from 2021 through 2023.

articles.title: TNF-α and IL-8 Are Helpful in the Prediction of Late Post-COVID-19 Venous Thromboembolic Disease-Single-Center Prospective Study.
articles.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 p p p Post-COVID-19 syndrome is associated with persistent inflammation and an elevated risk of late venous thromboembolism (VTE). The role of proinflammatory cytokines has been well documented in the acute phase of the disease, but their potential role in late post-COVID-19 VTE remains unknown. What is the prevalence of VTE among symptomatic post-COVID-19 patients, and which laboratory parameters could enhance the diagnostic accuracy for VTE in these patients? Consecutive patients with objectively confirmed previousinfection, admitted to a single department of lung diseases in a tertiary hospital due to sustained symptoms of dyspnea and/or exercise intolerance, were included. Clinical assessment and laboratory testing, including cytokine profiling (Il-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNF-α), PAI-1, and ferritin, were performed. VTE events (pulmonary embolism and/or deep vein thrombosis) were confirmed by standard imaging. Clinical and laboratory parameters were compared between participants with and without VTE. 108 patients: 69 (63.9%) males and 39 (36.1%) females, entered the study. VTE episodes were diagnosed in 39.8% (16.7% in the course of COVID-19 and 23.1% after the acute phase of the disease). Patients who entered the study ≤6 months and >6 months from acute COVID-19 infection were compared. Median D-dimer concentration was higher in patients with VTE that occurred within 6 months from the COVID-19 diagnosis compared to the non-VTE group (607 ng/mL vs. 428 ng/mL, borderline significance,= 0.0595). Median_IL-8 concentration was significantly higher in those who developed VTE more than 6 months after COVID-19 compared to non-VTE patients: 10.19 pg/mL vs. 6.61 pg/mL, respectively,= 0.048. The same was noted for TNF-α (39.02 pg/mL vs. 24 pg/mL, respectively,= 0.011). The best diagnostic utility for VTE prediction was obtained for TNF-α concentration in symptomatic patients diagnosed >6 months from acute COVID-19 infection (ROC AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.57-0.91). TNF-α was an independent risk factor of VTE episodes in the whole study group. Detection of elevated IL-8 and TNF-α levels later than 6 months from acute COVID-19 disease may help to identify patients at increased risk of late venous thromboembolism; nevertheless, further studies are needed to validate this observation.

articles.title: The Impact of Multiple Biologic Failures on Surgical Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Elective Subtotal Colectomy for Ulcerative Colitis.
articles.abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p Subtotal colectomy (STC) with end ileostomy (EI) is usually the first surgical stage for patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) who fail medical treatment, most often with biological agents. Is there a difference in surgical outcome after failure of one or two biologicals vs. three or four?A retrospective study of all patients who underwent STC with EI for UC (5-2018 to 1-2022). After excluding emergent cases, the elective cohort was divided into patients who failed 1-2 biologicals (group 1-2) vs. patients who failed 3-4 biologicals (group 3-4), and surgical outcomes were compared. Data collected included patients' demographics, preoperative clinical manifestations, and operative and postoperative outcomes.Ninety-eight patients underwent STC for UC, and of them, 53 were elective. Thirty patients failed 1-2 biologics (group 1-2), and 23 failed 3-4 biologics (group 3-4). The groups were similar in average age (37.6 ± 11 vs. 32.7 ± 10), BMI (26.7 ± 6 vs. 27.7 ± 7), number of years with UC (9.5 ± 9 vs. 9 ± 8), rate of steroid dependence (20 (67%) vs. 13 (57%)) but differed in sex; there were 25 (83%) males in group 1-2, and 8 (35%) in group 3-4 (< 0.01). The operative approaches were similar, as was the operative time (217 ± 74 vs. 210 ± 79 min). The length of hospital stay was 3.2 ± 1 days for group 1-2 and 5 ± 6 days for group 3-4 (= 0.14). Postoperative complications were seen in 10 patients (33%) vs. 7 patients (30%) (= 0.82), and of them, two (7%) and two (9%) (= 0.82) had Venous thromboembolism (VTE), respectively. Only 20 patients (67%) in group 1-2 and 16 patients (70%) in group 3-4 (= 0.82) progressed to a second stage of an Ileoanal pouch (IPAA) at 11.1 ± 4 and 9.2 ± 2 months, respectively. The overall average follow-up time was 41.1 months.Ulcerative Colitis patients who fail 3-4 biological agents and choose to go to elective STC with EI have very similar surgical outcomes compared to patients who choose elective surgery after failing only 1-2 biological agents in the same time span of known disease. UC patients with severe colitis and poor quality of life who fail two lines of biological agents may be better off electing surgical treatment than failing more biologics and then going to surgery. On the other hand, patients who try 3-4 biologics may expect no worse surgical outcomes than after 1-2 biologics.

articles.title: Chronic Venous Disease in Pregnancy: Pathophysiology, Diagnostic Pitfalls, and a Trimester-Stratified Management Framework-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Chronic venous disease (CVD) in pregnancy is common, poorly codified, and interpreted with diagnostic thresholds, severity instruments and treatment algorithms all derived outside pregnancy. This narrative review synthesises the mechanistic, epidemiological, diagnostic and therapeutic literature, keeping pregnancy-specific evidence separate from evidence extrapolated from non-pregnant populations. Gestational change is characterised principally by increased venous capacitance and vein-wall distension; ambulatory venous hypertension was not demonstrated in the two pregnancy studies assessing it; and new reflux develops in a minority, undetectable postpartum in the one study reporting it. Physiological adaptation, CVD and thrombotic pathology overlap clinically, deep vein thrombosis and superficial vein thrombosis being at once the principal differential diagnoses and potential complications. Management is correspondingly conservative: compression relieves symptoms but has not been shown to prevent varicose veins, routine initiation of venoactive drugs is not supported, and intervention is deferred other than in exceptional circumstances. A venous finding first detected in pregnancy warrants postpartum reassessment before it is taken for established disease. A trimester-stratified framework spanning preconception to late postpartum reassessment is proposed; it is evidence-informed rather than prospectively validated, and is not a guideline.

articles.title: Coenzyme Q10 for Acute Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection: Protocol for a Prospective, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single-Center Feasibility Trial.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Acute Stanford type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency. Emergency surgery is the standard life-saving treatment, but some patients decline operative repair, and no established pharmacological therapy has been shown to stabilize acute TAAD. Preclinical work by our team implicates mitochondrial dysfunction and smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching in aortic dissection and suggests that coenzyme Q10 may reduce dissection-related injury. This study aims to determine the feasibility of a future definitive randomized trial and to obtain preliminary safety and exploratory efficacy information.This prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single-center feasibility trial will enroll 60 adults with CTA-confirmed Stanford type A aortic dissection within 24 h of symptom onset who decline emergency surgical repair after standard surgical counseling. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to oral coenzyme Q10 100 mg three times daily or matched placebo for 14 days, in addition to the same guideline-directed supportive medical care. The primary feasibility outcome is recruitment feasibility, defined as randomization of 60 participants within 12 months after recruitment initiation. Secondary feasibility outcomes include treatment adherence, follow-up completion, dropout, missingness, outcome-assessment feasibility, and candidate endpoint event rates. The primary exploratory clinical outcome is 14-day all-cause mortality; additional exploratory outcomes include aortic rupture death, false-lumen thrombosis, cardiac tamponade, worsening pericardial effusion, and organ malperfusion syndromes. Safety outcomes include adverse events, serious adverse events, adverse drug reactions, suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions, and prespecified laboratory indices.The trial is designed to establish whether recruitment, blinded treatment delivery, follow-up, outcome collection, and safety monitoring are operationally feasible and to provide estimates for planning a larger confirmatory trial.This feasibility trial will inform the design and conduct of future definitive evaluation of coenzyme Q10 in acute TAAD. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2600123230.

articles.title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control. AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE. METHODS: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index. RESULTS: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).

articles.title: Initial Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025). Eligible patients were adults with imaging-confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis who initiated either a DOAC or warfarin within 30 days after diagnosis. Time zero was the date of the first oral anticoagulant prescription. The primary efficacy outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE within 1 year. Propensity score overlap weighting was used, and weighted Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event. The clinically acceptable noninferiority margin was defined as an absolute increase of 1.5 percentage points in 1-year recurrent VTE risk, corresponding approximately to a relative margin of 1.50 for the primary Fine-Gray analysis. RESULTS: P P Among 2476 eligible patients, 942 initiated a DOAC (rivaroxaban, n=701; dabigatran, n=121; apixaban, n=113; edoxaban, n=7) and 1534 initiated warfarin. Within 1 year, symptomatic recurrent VTE occurred in 36 and 73 patients, respectively. The overlap-weighted 1-year recurrence risks were 3.74% and 5.47%, corresponding to a risk difference of -1.73 percentage points (95% CI, -3.76 to 0.30). DOAC treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.67 compared with that of warfarin ([95% CI, 0.37-1.21];=0.184), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion (for noninferiority=0.004). Major bleeding was rare within 1 year (0 versus 1 patient). Clinical nonmajor bleeding occurred in 18 versus 34 patients, and any bleeding occurred in 48 versus 75 patients. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with cerebral venous thrombosis selected for oral anticoagulation, initial treatment with a DOAC met the noninferiority criterion relative to warfarin for the prevention of symptomatic recurrent VTE at 1 year. Findings regarding bleeding outcomes were exploratory and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative safety or equivalence.

METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025).

articles.title: Impact of prolonged balloon inflation on valve expansion and early clinical outcomes following contemporary balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Incomplete expansion of balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THVs) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may affect valve performance and durability. Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes. METHODS: This single-centre study analysed consecutive TAVI patients treated for native tricuspid aortic stenosis with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA THV using a prolonged balloon inflation strategy (8 seconds). Valve expansion was assessed by fluoroscopy at multiple frame levels and compared with three validated reference standards. Results were also descriptively compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique. Clinical and haemodynamic outcomes at 30 days were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria. RESULTS: A total of 84 patients (mean age 78.8 years, 58% male, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score 3.9%) were included. Prolonged inflation resulted in complete THV expansion at the inflow and outflow levels, with only mild underexpansion (98.5±1.3%) detected at the midframe level when manufacturer-defined nominal values were used as the reference. When compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique, expansion values for the 23, 26, and 29 mm valves were consistently similar or higher, whereas lower expansion was observed for the 20 mm size. Device success was achieved in all cases, with no stroke at 30 days. Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 6% of patients. Haemodynamic performance was favourable (mean gradient 9.2 [interquartile range 7.0-10.3] mmHg at 30 days), with no patients having moderate or severe paravalvular leak. CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged balloon inflation during BE THV deployment is associated with favourable valve expansion, haemodynamic results, and a favourable safety profile, consistent with values reported in double-tap series. If confirmed in larger studies, this strategy may represent a simple alternative to routine double-tap in selected patients.

articles.title: Clinical Risk Factors and Inflammatory Markers as Predictors of Postoperative Delirium in Patients Undergoing Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery.
articles.abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and serious neurological complication following acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair, contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Given the critical role of systemic inflammation in POD pathogenesis, this study aimed to evaluate perioperative inflammatory profiles in patients undergoing ATAAD repair and to develop a predictive nomogram for early POD risk stratification.This retrospective, single-center study included 355 patients who underwent total arch replacement for ATAAD. Serial inflammatory markers were assessed across multiple perioperative time points. A two-stage variable selection process, incorporating variance inflation factor (VIF) and the Boruta algorithm, was utilized to identify robust predictors. A predictive nomogram was constructed via multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples.POD occurred in 29.86% of the cohort. Patients who developed POD had higher inflammatory marker levels at several individual postoperative time points compared to the non-delirium group. The final predictive model integrated 11 key variables: age, EuroSCORE I, CPB time, SIRI_6h, PLR_6h, IL-10_6h, IL-8_6h, IL-8_pre, IL-6_6h, IL-6_pre, and PCT_6h. The nomogram demonstrated acceptable internal discrimination with an AUC of 0.835 (95% CI: 0.794-0.876) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.811. Notably, IL-6_6h and PCT_6h emerged as strong independent risk factors, while SIRI_6h demonstrated an inverse association with POD. Calibration and DCA analyses confirmed the model's acceptable performance and potential clinical utility, though independent external validation remains essential prior to any clinical translation. An exploratory, web-based risk calculator was developed to facilitate bedside implementation.This study develops and internally validates an exploratory biomarker-based prediction model for POD in ATAAD patients. By integrating early inflammatory profiles with established clinical variables, this preliminary model provides a preliminary foundation for early risk stratification, though rigorous prospective multicenter external validation is required before real-world clinical implementation can be considered.

articles.title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

articles.title: Unintended shifts in high-priority adult heart transplant listings after the OPTN's September 2025 policy change.
articles.abstract: The Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network amended Status 2 heart allocation criteria in September 2025, requiring documented failure of high-dose inotropes before candidates could qualify via intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or percutaneous endovascular ventricular assist device (PEVAD) support. Using OPTN data, we compared seasonally matched pre-policy (September 2024 to June 2025, n=4206) and post-policy (September 2025 to June 2026, n=4231) adult candidates. While standard Status 3 high-dose inotrope listings increased 2.0% to 4.1% and standard Status 2 IABP/PEVAD listings decreased 18.2% to 11.0%, Status 1 listings and Status 2 exceptions increased 7.7% to 10.6% and 17.5% to 21.5%, respectively (all p<0.001). Consequently, combined initial Status 1/2 listings were unchanged (44.5% vs 44.0%, p=0.71). Furthermore, overall transplant volume remained similar, but status at transplant shifted from standard Status 2 toward Status 2 exceptions and Status 1. Tightening standard Status 2 eligibility was associated with redistribution across high-priority pathways rather than reduced high-priority listings.

articles.title: Reported items and methods for analysis in diagnostic management studies evaluating venous thromboembolism: a systematic review: Communication from the ISTH SSC Subcommittee on Diagnosis and Prediction in Thrombotic Disease.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Reporting of venous thromboembolism (VTE) diagnostic management studies is not standardized, which contributes to incomplete and variable description of study methods and results. This variability hampers interpretation and appraisal of study results. The aim of this study was to evaluate the reporting of key methodology items in recent VTE diagnostic management studies. METHODS: st th A systematic search was conducted in Embase and MEDLINE from January 1, 2005, to August 6, 2024, to identify prospective diagnostic management studies that included adult patients with suspected VTE with follow-up of patients in whom VTE was excluded at baseline. The primary outcome was the reporting of predefined study items. Secondary outcomes were definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates and efficiency. RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies were included. Reporting varied: study design, inclusion criteria, follow-up and overall VTE prevalence were consistently reported, whereas location of confirmed PE and reasons for loss to follow-up were poorly reported. Fifty-four studies (92%) reported a definition of the diagnostic failure rate, of which 45 (83%) defined it as the incidence of VTE in all patients in whom VTE had been excluded at baseline. Predefined upper safety margin for the diagnostic failure rate was reported in 34 studies (63%), and varied widely, ranging between 1.5% and 8.0%. Only 8 studies (14%) defined diagnostic efficiency. CONCLUSION: Reporting of key study items, as well as definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates varied among VTE diagnostic management studies. Standardization of the reporting and analysis of VTE diagnostic management studies is needed.

articles.title: Plasma neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin levels and risk of future incident venous thromboembolism.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although neutrophils are suggested to play a role in the pathogenesis of venous thromboembolism (VTE), no study has investigated whether neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), a marker of neutrophil activation, is associated with future VTE risk in the general population. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between plasma NGAL levels and the risk of future VTE. METHODS: Plasma NGAL levels were measured in 416 VTE cases and 848 age- and sex-matched controls in a nested case-control study derived from the Tromsø study cohort (1994-2007). Logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs for VTE according to quartiles of plasma NGAL, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, arterial cardiovascular disease, cancer, and C-reactive protein. Separate analyses with follow-up restricted to the first 2 and 5 years after cohort inclusion were conducted to investigate potential short-term associations. RESULTS: We found no association between NGAL levels and risk of future VTE when analyzing the entire study period (OR for highest vs lowest quartile of NGAL: 1.02, 95% CI, 0.70-1.51). However, when follow-up was restricted to 2 years, higher NGAL levels were associated with increased risk of future VTE (OR, 3.87; 95% CI, 1.15-13.03). The association was attenuated when follow-up was extended to 5 years (OR, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.82-2.80). CONCLUSION: Higher plasma NGAL levels were associated with a transiently increased risk of future VTE.

articles.title: Incidence of thrombosis and bleeding in patients with JAK2-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms receiving low-dose aspirin: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with Janus kinase 2 (JAK2) V617F-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are at increased thrombotic risk and commonly receive low-dose aspirin, yet its net clinical benefit is uncertain. OBJECTIVES: We estimated the incidence of thrombotic and bleeding events in patients with JAK2-positive MPNs treated with low-dose aspirin. METHODS: A systematic review was performed for studies evaluating thrombotic and hemorrhagic events in patients with JAK2 V617F-positive MPNs while taking low-dose aspirin. Study-level incidence rates (IRs) per 100 person-years and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) comparing aspirin use with no aspirin were calculated and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 We included 3 randomized clinical trials and 7 observational studies (n = 1760 with aspirin, n = 367 without aspirin). The pooled IR of thrombotic events in patients with JAK2 V617F-positive MPNs receiving low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 2.72 per 100 person-years (95% CI, 1.59-4.65; I= 93%), with pooled IRR receiving aspirin vs no aspirin of 0.59 (95% CI, 0.40-0.86; I= 16%). The pooled IR of major and nonmajor bleeding on low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 1.97 (95% CI, 1.06-3.65; I= 90%) per 100 person-years, with a pooled IRR of 2.43 (95% CI, 1.15-5.11; I= 43%). The GRADE level of confidence for the investigated risks was low. CONCLUSION: Aspirin was associated with a 40% reduction in thrombosis but a 2.5-fold increase in bleeding risk with low certainty of evidence. More studies are needed to gain high-quality evidence to better define the role of aspirin in JAK2 V617F-positive MPNs.
