articles.title: Early stroke after aortic arch repair: Comparative and proportional meta-analyses of open, hybrid, and total endovascular strategies.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Early stroke remains one of the most devastating complications after aortic arch repair. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated early stroke after open, hybrid, and total endovascular aortic arch repair using separate comparative and proportional frameworks. METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through July 27, 2026. Observational studies reporting neurological outcomes after adult open, hybrid, or total endovascular aortic arch repair were included. The primary comparative meta-analysis pooled propensity score-matched or weighted studies comparing hybrid with open repair using random-effects restricted maximum likelihood models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Separate proportional random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled stroke incidences for each strategy. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions and the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. The protocol was prospectively registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420261461659). RESULTS: 2 Thirty-four studies were included. Seven propensity score-matched or weighted cohorts comprising 948 patients (474 open and 474 hybrid repairs) contributed to the primary comparative meta-analysis. No significant difference in early stroke was identified between hybrid and open repair [odds ratio, 1.99; 95% confidence interval, 0.46-8.58; P = .292; I= 52.9%). Post hoc comparative analyses restricted to dissection cohorts (3 cohorts; 572 patients) and zone 0 hybrid repair (3 cohorts; 448 patients) were also inconclusive and highly imprecise. In descriptive proportional analyses, pooled early-stroke incidences were 5.3% after open, 7.5% after hybrid, and 6.4% after total endovascular repair. Technique-stratified incidences were 6.1% for conventional open repair, 4.4% for open repair with frozen elephant trunk, and 5.3% for branched total endovascular repair. CONCLUSIONS: Adjusted comparative evidence showed no significant difference in early stroke between hybrid and open aortic arch repair. Evidence for total endovascular repair remains predominantly noncomparative. Treatment should be individualized according to aortic pathology, urgency, anatomy, operative risk, and institutional expertise.

articles.title: ArtAssist sequential compression biomechanical device as a cost-dominant limb salvage strategy for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia: A decade and half, single-center cohort study with health economic and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Major lower limb amputation for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) costs the Irish Health Service Executive a median €88,820/patient; the long-term health economic and quality-adjusted survival evidence for ArtAssist Sequential Compression Biomechanical Device (SCBD) is lacking. METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with nonreconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary center (January 2008-June 2025). Primary end points were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness vs primary amputation, and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity. Kaplan-Meier analysis of limb salvage, multivariable Cox regression for major amputation, competing-risks analysis, and health economic modelling using contemporaneous cost data were performed. RESULTS: Overall crude limb salvage, defined as freedom from major amputation, was achieved in 85% (294/347 patients). At last follow-up, 48% of patients were alive without major amputation. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year limb salvage at 95%. The cumulative incidence of major amputation at 5 years was 8% when accounting for death as a competing event, confirming durable limb preservation despite substantial long-term mortality in this elderly, comorbid population. Male sex, hypertension, and ischemic heart disease independently predicted major amputation or limb-salvage failure (hazard ratio: 1.70, 1.80, 1.71; all P ≤ .012). Comorbidity burden showed a dose-response relationship (P = .008). Ninety-day rental (€1373/patient) reduced total expenditure sixfold vs primary amputation (€5.3M vs €30.8M), saving €76,500/patient. Quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity yielded a gain of 3.37 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) per patient; incremental cost-effectiveness ratio €21,900/QALY confirms a dominant strategy. CONCLUSIONS: ArtAssist SCBD achieves a sixfold reduction in costs vs primary amputation, +3.37 QALYs/patient, and an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €21,900/QALY a dominant strategy supported by durable limb preservation, with 85% overall crude limb salvage and an estimated 5-year limb salvage of approximately 95% in the largest single-center cohort reported. These findings support universal commissioning of ArtAssist SCBD for nonreconstructible CLTI.

METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with nonreconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary center (January 2008-June 2025). Primary end points were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness vs primary amputation, and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Serial Alkaline Phosphatase-to-Albumin Ratio for Mortality After Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt.
articles.abstract: Background: Methods: Results: p p p Conclusions: Prognostic assessment after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) remains challenging, and currently available scores are based mainly on pre-procedural variables. The alkaline phosphatase-to-albumin ratio (APAR) is a simple laboratory-derived marker that may provide additional prognostic information during the early post-TIPS period.This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 45 adults who underwent TIPS between February 2019 and December 2024. APAR was calculated at baseline, 48 h, and 1 week after the procedure. The primary outcome was one-year all-cause mortality; 90-day mortality was a secondary outcome. Prognostic performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and associations with mortality were examined using Cox regression adjusted for age and baseline MELD score.Within one year, 17 patients (37.8%) died; nine (20.0%) died within 90 days; and 22 (48.9%) died during overall follow-up. Median APAR was higher in patients who died within one year than in those alive at one year at baseline (5.98 vs. 3.89;= 0.006), 48 h (10.79 vs. 3.78;< 0.001), and 1 week (13.93 vs. 4.57;< 0.001). ROC areas under the curve were 0.748 (95% CI, 0.578-0.893), 0.876 (0.748-0.964), and 0.873 (0.726-0.977), respectively. After adjustment for age and MELD, APAR remained associated with one-year mortality at baseline (hazard ratio [HR] 1.140; 95% CI, 1.049-1.238), 48 h (HR 1.225; 1.111-1.350), and 1 week (HR 1.193; 1.092-1.302).Serial APAR measurements were associated with one-year mortality after TIPS and may support early post-procedural risk assessment. Prospective multicenter validation is needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Peripheral Arterial Disease: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate and Interleukin-6 as Markers of Disease Severity and Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
articles.abstract: p p p p Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a manifestation of systemic atherosclerosis in which chronic inflammation contributes to disease severity. This retrospective study included patients who underwent arteriography for PAD at a single center in 2019. Of 238 arteriographies performed, inflammatory and hematologic biomarker panels were available for a subset of 71 patients with angiographically confirmed PAD. Serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), white blood cell count, platelet count, and uric acid were compared across sex, age, diabetes, and obesity subgroups, correlated with disease severity by the Leriche-Fontaine classification, and analyzed for their association with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI; Fontaine stages III-IV vs. IIA-IIB). ESR (r = 0.408,= 0.001) and IL-6 (r = 0.310,= 0.009) correlated significantly with disease severity, whereas TNF-α, white blood cell count, platelet count, and uric acid did not. Both markers showed modest but significant discriminative performance for CLTI (IL-6: area under the curve = 0.674,= 0.012; ESR: area under the curve = 0.673,= 0.021). ESR and IL-6 were both associated with PAD severity suggesting a more pronounced systemic inflammatory phenotype in CLTI; their prognostic value after revascularization warrants evaluation in larger, prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Heart Failure Is Associated with Limb-Related Adverse Events in Patients Hospitalized for Diabetic Foot Ulcers.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p p To evaluate the impact of heart failure (HF) on one-year outcomes in patients hospitalized for diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs).A retrospective observational study including consecutive patients admitted in 2024 to a tertiary multidisciplinary diabetic foot service for DFUs. Patients were stratified according to the presence of HF (HF+ vs. HF-). One-year outcomes included wound healing, major amputation, non-fatal major adverse limb events (NF-MALCE), including myocardial infarction, stroke, recurrent chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) requiring revascularization, and mortality.Overall, 270 patients were included (104 HF+ [38.5%] vs. 166 HF- [61.5%]). Patients with HF exhibited a more severe cardiorenal phenotype, with worse cardiac and renal biomarkers. At one-year follow-up, patients with HF showed lower wound healing rates than patients without HF (58.6% vs. 71.7%,= 0.03), higher incidence of NF-MALCE (43.3% vs. 18.7%,< 0.001), mainly driven by recurrent CLTI requiring revascularization (48.9% vs. 27.0%,< 0.001), and higher mortality (21.1% vs. 7.2%,= 0.001). Conversely, no differences were observed in major amputation, myocardial infarction, or stroke. After multivariable adjustment for age, sex, ischaemic heart disease, atrial fibrillation, dialysis, haemoglobin, albumin, foot infection and peripheral arterial disease (PAD), HF remained independently associated with NF-MALCE (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 2.90, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.38-6.09,= 0.005) and recurrent CLTI requiring revascularization (aOR 2.43, 95% CI 1.11-5.32,= 0.026); the association remained consistent in the subgroup with PAD.HF identifies a high-risk cardio-renal phenotype and is independently associated with increased limb-related adverse events in patients hospitalized for DFUs, supporting closer vascular surveillance and integrated multidisciplinary cardio-renal-foot care.

articles.title: Midterm Outcomes of the Minos Ultralow Profile Endograft: Results from the Multicentre MINER Registry.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess midterm outcomes of the ultralow profile Minos endograft in a physician initiated registry. METHODS: A non-sponsored registry collected consecutive patients treated with the Minos device in 20 Italian centres (2021 - 2025). Elective patients (the primary analysis population) were stratified by access quality (hostile vs. standard access); hostile iliac-femoral access was defined by a narrowest iliac diameter < 7 mm, iliac artery tortuosity index > 1.6, aortic bifurcation diameter < 16 mm, or severe circumferential calcification. Proximal neck features were covariates only; urgent and emergent procedures were analysed separately. Outcomes were thirty day technical success, mortality, and major adverse events (MAEs), and midterm freedom from rupture, limb occlusion, type I or III endoleak, and re-intervention. RESULTS: Of 310 patients (mean aneurysm diameter 54.8 ± 10.0 mm), 288 (92.9%) were elective. Among these, 154 (53.5%) had a standard access and 134 (46.5%) a hostile access. The latter were more frequently women (16.4% vs. 6.0%; p = .009) and more frequently had peripheral arterial disease (31.6% vs. 16.8%; p = .006). Elective technical success was 100%, with no thirty day deaths. The thirty day MAE rate was higher with hostile access (8.2% vs. 1.3%; p = .032), mainly from access related events and blood loss > 1 000 mL (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021), as was early re-intervention (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021). At 3 years there were no aneurysm related deaths; freedom from limb occlusion was 97% vs. 100% (p = .025) and from type I OR III endoleak was 98% vs. 100% (p = .18) in the standard and hostile access groups, respectively. CONCLUSION: The Minos ultralow profile endograft was safe and effective for the treatment of elective abdominal aortic aneurysms. Peri-operative morbidity was higher when the iliac-femoral access was hostile, and limb occlusion, type I - III endoleak, and re-intervention were more evident compared with standard access anatomy. An ultralow profile platform can extend endovascular repair to unfavourable access vessels without affecting midterm device performance.

articles.title: Cilostazol and Risk of Major Adverse Limb and Cardiovascular Events after Revascularisation for Peripheral Artery Disease.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain at high risk of major adverse limb events (MALE) and cardiovascular events (MACE) after revascularisation. Cilostazol, a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor with antiplatelet and antiproliferative effects, reduces re-stenosis but its real world impact on clinical outcomes is uncertain. This retrospective, nationwide, propensity score matched cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of cilostazol on MALE, MACE, and all cause mortality after lower limb revascularisation for PAD. METHODS: Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, patients who underwent lower limb revascularisation for PAD from 2010 - 2023, with follow up through 2024 were identified. Patients with prior cilostazol use were excluded. 1:1 propensity score matching (n = 5 464 per group) adjusted for baseline differences. Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models were used to evaluate outcomes. The comparison reflects cilostazol used with or without background antithrombotic therapy. RESULTS: Cilostazol use was associated with significantly lower risks of MALE (78.7 vs. 154.0 events/1 000 person-years; subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 0.50; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.46 - 0.53) and MACE (97.9 vs. 117.1 events/1 000 person-years; hazard ratio [HR] 0.84; 95% CI 0.79 - 0.89). All cause mortality was also reduced (116.0 vs. 127.6 events/1 000 person-years; HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.86 - 0.96). Major bleeding did not differ significantly between groups (SHR 0.90; 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), although the absolute rate was high in both groups (12.1% vs. 13.1%). Subgroup analysis showed greater limb benefit in patients not on other antiplatelet agents. CONCLUSION: Cilostazol after PAD revascularisation was associated with lower risks of limb and cardiovascular events and mortality. These effects were observed without any increase in the rate of major bleeding, although this rate was high in both groups. Randomised trials focused on cardiovascular events are needed.

Cilostazol, a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor with antiplatelet and antiproliferative effects, reduces re-stenosis but its real world impact on clinical outcomes is uncertain. This retrospective, nationwide, propensity score matched cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of cilostazol on MALE, MACE, and all cause mortality after lower limb revascularisation for PAD.

articles.title: Differences in Clinical Presentation of Chronic Pelvic Pain Caused by Iliac Vein Obstruction Impacts Referral Pathway, Time to Diagnosis, and Post-stenting Pain Resolution.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Iliac venous stenting improves chronic pelvic pain (CPP) caused by iliac vein obstruction (IVO). Signs and symptoms vary, but this pain is reproducible and easily identifiable. However, patients can experience significant delays in diagnosis and treatment. This study aimed to determine associations between the referral history, clinical presentation, pain characteristics, and stenting outcomes among women with CPP due to IVO. METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data of women who were referred to a vascular surgeon with signs and symptoms of IVO, including CPP, and who underwent iliac venous stenting. Associations between clinical presentation (signs, symptoms, pain severity), medical and referral history, and stenting outcomes were compared between three patient groups based on number of other specialist consultations prior to stenting (none, one, or at least two). RESULTS: Data were for 113 women (46.5 ± 15.7 years) who had CPP for 6.3 ± 6.6 years with initial severity of 6.7 ± 2.3 (out of 10). CPP was reproducible for all women, with exercise, standing, and intercourse being the most common triggers. More than two thirds had lower limb pain, oedema, and varicose veins. At a median of 7 years post-stenting, the latest pain score was 0.8 ± 1.6, and approximately 80% had full pain resolution. Women who had seen at least two other specialists had the worst initial pelvic pain, the most prescription pain medication, back pain, other abdominopelvic signs and symptoms, and previous interventions, and the fewest varicose veins. These women had 8.5 ± 7.9 years to diagnosis, but 99% still had significant improvement in, and 66% had full resolution of, their pelvic pain. CONCLUSION: All patients had a reproducible pattern of venous origin pelvic pain, but those with worse CPP, more abdominopelvic symptoms, and less varicose veins had a more complex and delayed referral pathway and the lowest pain resolution.

articles.title: Long Term Results of Surgical Treatment of Chronic Venous Thoracic Outlet Syndrome: A Single Centre Experience.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional analysis aimed to evaluate the surgical and long term functional outcomes of a structured treatment algorithm for patients with chronic venous thoracic outlet syndrome (cVTOS). METHODS: Patients with cVTOS and treated at this tertiary centre between 2016 and 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of transaxillary thoracic outlet decompression (TOD), venolysis, and subclavian vein (SCV) recanalisation. In case of persistent venous obstruction during the primary procedure, anticipated repeat percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) was planned. Anticoagulation (rivaroxaban) was prescribed until 48 hours before surgery, resumed the day after surgery for six weeks, or until 48 hours before re-PTA. The primary endpoint included SCV patency and secondary outcomes included functional outcomes (DASH and Derkash scores). RESULTS: Seventy patients were included (mean age 35 years; 56% women). Median time to presentation was 40 (20.0 - 104.0) months after initial upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT). Eleven patients (16%) had an operative complication (haematoma n = 6, pneumothorax n = 1, UEDVT n = 1, transient Horner syndrome n = 1, phrenic nerve injury n = 1, and SCV rupture n = 1). Median length of hospital stay was 1.0 day. Venography post-TOD/PTA showed persistent venous obstruction in 15 patients (21%) for which re-PTA was planned. Over time, 20 patients (29%) developed re-stenosis. A total of 35 (50%) re-PTAs were performed. Primary patency was 56%, primary assisted patency was 86%, and secondary patency was 93% at last follow up (12 months). Median post-operative DASH score decreased significantly (pre-op: 32.9 (15.8 - 48.3) vs. post-op 8.0 (2.3 - 27.8); p < .001) with a mean follow up of 45.7 ± 27.5 months. Zero patients reported a poor Derkash score. CONCLUSION: Chronic VTOS can be effectively treated with good long term functional outcomes. Re-PTAs were necessary in half of the cases (anticipated). This treatment algorithm diminished the need of secondary interventions in 50% of the cases, as well as the need for long term anticoagulation usage.

articles.title: NDUFAF2 promotes abdominal aortic aneurysm formation through mitochondrial dysfunction-induced apoptosis.
articles.abstract: in vitro In vivo 2 Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease closely associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis. Here, we found that NDUFAF2 (NADH dehydrogenase (ubiquinone) 1 alpha subcomplex assembly factor 2) was significantly upregulated in cultured cells and murine AAA tissues. Knockdown of NDUFAF2attenuated Ang II-induced mitochondrial fragmentation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and apoptosis in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), while improving mitochondrial membrane potential and oxygen consumption rate. In addition, NDUFAF2 knockdown reduced the expression of DRP1 (dynamin-related protein 1) while restoring the mitochondrial fusion protein OPA1 (optic atrophy 1), and OPA1 overexpression further enhanced mitochondrial integrity and function., NDUFAF2 knockdown suppressed CaCl-induced AAA formation, preserved aortic structure, reduced apoptosis, and restored mitochondrial complex subunits and smooth muscle cell markers. These results indicate that NDUFAF2 contributes to AAA progression by triggering mitochondrial damage and apoptosis, representing a promising therapeutic target for AAA.

articles.title: Staphylococcus aureus Small-molecule activators of theClpC/ClpP AAA+ protease.
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Staphylococcus aureus in vivo S. aureus bona fide in vitro S. aureus The central AAA+ ClpC/ClpP protease in Gram-positive bacteria is crucial for virulence and stress resistance and has been recognized as drug target. Natural cyclic peptides deregulate the essentialClpC1 and cause cell death. Similarly, overactivated mutants of the non-essentialClpC homolog cause uncontrolled proteolysis and severe toxicity. However, no chemical modulators ofClpC have been described. Here, using a biochemical high-throughput screen, we identify eight distinctsmall molecules that stimulate ClpC ATPase and proteolytic activity. Structural, computational, and mutational analyses define two ligandable regulatory sites within the ClpC N-terminal domain (NTD) as compound targets: a conserved hydrophobic groove and an allosteric pArg1 pocket, both engaged in substrate recognition. These findings establishClpC as chemically targetable and provide mechanistic insight into its regulatory architecture, enabling future development and optimization of chemical probes to deregulate AAA+ protease control.

articles.title: A method for expressing two proteins at a tunable ratio allows for studying the kinetics of creatine transport by MCT12.
articles.abstract: M Interactions between physically or functionally coupled proteins are often studied by co-expression from the same or separate plasmids, but protein ratios can vary widely between individual cells. To overcome this limitation, we developed a strategy to generate tunable and constant expression ratios using a single vector encoding two proteins separated by a P2A site followed by short AAA codon repeats that progressively reduce ribosomal readthrough. After validating this approach with the fluorescent proteins eGFP and mCherry, we applied it to characterize the transport cycle of the electroneutral monocarboxylate transporter MCT12, a task that is otherwise difficult to achieve experimentally. By co-expressing MCT12 with the concentrative creatine transporter CRT1 at defined ratios, we were able to determine the substrate turnover rate of MCT12 and its substrate K. This approach enables precise control of protein stoichiometry, facilitating quantitative mechanistic studies of interacting proteins in cells.

articles.title: An LLM-enhanced AI agent for rapid diagnosis of acute aortic dissection in multi-center settings.
articles.abstract: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) is a high-mortality cardiovascular emergency, yet early diagnosis before computed tomography angiography (CTA) remains challenging. We developed AAD-Agent as a pre-imaging triage aid-not as a replacement for CTA-and evaluated it in a retrospective, multi-center study. Using 869 suspected patients from 3 Chinese hospitals for internal validation and 200 from 2 additional hospitals for external validation, we compared AAD-Agent against a machine learning (ML) ensemble model. The ML-ensemble model performed well internally (accuracy 0.948, F1-score 0.964) but deteriorated externally (0.540, 0.600). In contrast, AAD-Agent maintained external stability across LLMs: DeepSeek-R1 (accuracy 0.715, F1-score 0.820), GPT-3.5 (0.715, 0.825), and GPT-4o (0.710, 0.803). Although the case-enriched design inflates these metrics, prevalence-adjusted negative predictive value (≈99.6% at 1% prevalence) supports AAD-Agent as a safe, low-cost rule-out aid to defer CTA in low-risk patients. Its low external specificity precludes confirmatory diagnosis, limiting use to rule out pending prospective validation.

articles.title: Association of Prethrombectomy Hemorrhagic Infarction on MRI With Further Transformation and Functional Outcomes: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated whether pretreatment MRI HI is associated with 90-day functional dependence, post-MT PH, and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO undergoing MT at 2 stroke centers (2015-2022). Patients required pre-MT T2*-weighted MRI. HI was graded (types I/II) per European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study III criteria in blinded fashion. The primary outcome was 90-day functional dependence (modified Rankin Scale 3-6). Secondary outcomes were post-MT ipsilateral PH and SICH. We used multivariable Bayesian and frequentist logistic regression to adjust for age, sex, NIH Stroke Scale, baseline disability, comorbidities, infarct volume, and procedural factors. RESULTS: p p p Among 479 patients (median age 72 years; 46% female; 50% received IV thrombolysis), pretreatment HI was identified in 25 (5.2%), with excellent inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ = 0.9). Functional dependence at 90 days occurred in 47% of the total cohort, ipsilateral PH in 9.4%, and SICH in 3.1%. In multivariable analysis, pre-MT HI was independently associated with 90-day functional dependence (Bayesian adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.66, 95% credible interval [CrI] 2.15-24.28, Pr[OR > 1] = 1.00; frequentist aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.91-18.52,= 0.002). Pre-MT HI also demonstrated a high posterior probability of association with post-MT ipsilateral PH (Bayesian aOR 2.76, 95% CrI 0.73-9.26, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.94; frequentist aOR 2.84, 95% CI 0.84-9.58,= 0.091) and SICH (Bayesian aOR 5.59, 95% CrI 0.63-34.92, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.95; frequentist aOR 6.02, 95% CI 1.00-36.11,= 0.049). DISCUSSION: HI detected on pretreatment MRI is an independent predictor of poor long-term functional outcomes and correlates with post-MT PH/SICH. Pre-MT HI may reflect significant blood-brain barrier disruption and microvascular fragility, serving as a marker of reperfusion vulnerability. Limitations include the retrospective design and the relatively low frequency of HI, PH, and SICH, which were addressed using Bayesian modeling to quantify uncertainty. Although not a contraindication to MT, identifying HI may aid in periprocedural risk stratification and serve as a candidate marker for future neuroprotective trials.

Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Blood Pressure Dynamics and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Optimal blood pressure (BP) management after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, and whether early BP dynamics differentially affect outcomes among female and male participants is unclear. METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion. Serial BP measurements obtained during the first 72 hours after randomization were used to estimate patient-specific mean BP trajectories and short-term BP variability with a location-scale mixed-effects modeling approach. Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS). RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory. DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT. TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04140110; the Registration Date, October 22, 2019.

articles.title: Metal-based hydrogen-generating therapeutic systems: From reactive chemistry to route-specific exposure and translational design.
articles.abstract: 2 2 2 2 2 2 Molecular hydrogen (H) has shown broad therapeutic relevance in oxidative injury, inflammation, metabolic dysfunction and tissue repair, yet its clinical translation remains limited by rapid diffusion, poor retention and a poorly defined dose-exposure relationship. Metal-based H-generating systems offer an engineering strategy to produce or release Hat pathological sites or material-tissue interfaces, where local exposure can be shaped by material design. This review reframes these platforms as material-formulation-route-indication systems rather than isolated material classes. The field now extends from classical metal hydrides to broader metal-containing platforms that generate or release Hthrough hydrolysis, corrosion, electrochemical reactions or hydrogen storage-mediated release. Their therapeutic behavior is governed by route-specific exposure fields shaped by Hrelease, accompanying reaction chemistry, formulation-defined compartments and tissue environments. Accordingly, route-oriented evaluation is essential because the same reactive core can produce distinct exposure profiles, safety boundaries and translational requirements across oral, local, vascular and implantable contexts. Mechanistically, H-dependent redox and cytoprotective biology provides an important entry point, but therapeutic outcomes arise from a multi-effector local chemical milieu involving metal-derived species, coupled physicochemical changes and, in some platforms, external activation. Translational development therefore requires controlled materials engineering, route-specific exposure metrics, mechanism-matched validation, a PK/PD-like exposure-response framework adapted for reactive material systems and manufacturing strategies aligned with chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) requirements. The field should advance toward route-specific, exposure-defined and mechanism-validated local reaction therapy.

articles.title: Sequential blood-brain barrier-penetrating and microglial-mitochondria-targeting nanosystem for ischemic stroke therapy.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) causes severe neurological deficits closely linked to microglial overactivation after ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury, a process governed by mitochondrial homeostasis. However, restoring microglial mitochondrial function across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains challenging. Here, we report a sequentially targeted nanosystem, M-BPM@TGPB, for I/R injury therapy. It comprises a triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-modified, gadolinium-doped Prussian blue core and a mannose-modified BV2-platelet hybrid membrane shell. This design integrates mannose for BBB penetration, platelet membrane for lesion targeting, BV2 membrane for microglial uptake, and TPP for mitochondrial localization, enabling precise vascular-to-subcellular delivery. In vitro, the nanosystem crossed the BBB, localized to BV2 mitochondria, scavenged reactive oxygen species (ROS), restored mitochondrial function, and inhibited inflammation. In a mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R), the intravenously administered nanosystem accumulated in microglial mitochondria, scavenged mitochondrial ROS (mtROS), restored mitochondrial homeostasis, promoted M1-to-M2 polarization, suppressed neuroinflammation, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and promoted angiogenesis, thereby reducing infarct volume from 36.61% to 10.57% and the modified neurological severity score (mNSS) from 14 to 2.5. It also exhibited favorable biocompatibility and enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast. Critically, rather than broadly scavenging ROS, this strategy specifically restores microglial mitochondrial function, shifting the therapeutic focus from general antioxidant approaches to organelle-specific intervention. This work may offer a promising design paradigm for nanotherapies targeting central nervous system disorders in which mitochondrial dysfunction and neuroinflammation are core pathological drivers.

articles.title: Role and mechanism of ATF6-mediated endoplasmic reticulum stress in ITLN-1 against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Intelectin-1 (ITLN-1), a novel adipocytokine, exerts neuroprotective effects against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), yet its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study focused on activating transcription factor 6 (ATF6), a key endoplasmic reticulum stress sensor, to explore its role in CIRI-induced neuronal injury and determine whether ITLN-1 mediates neuroprotection through ATF6 regulation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We established an N2a cell hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) model and a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model. Using protein-protein molecular docking, in situ proximity ligation assay, Western blotting, mitochondrial membrane potential assays, and TUNEL staining, we investigated ATF6 activation in neuronal apoptosis and its upstream regulatory mechanisms. KEY FINDINGS: H/R injury markedly induced ATF6 activation in N2a cells, triggering mitochondrial dysfunction and promoting apoptosis. ATF6 overexpression further aggravated these effects, supporting its critical pathogenic role in CIRI. Mechanistic analyses revealed that ITLN-1 physically associates with ATF6. Both ITLN-1 overexpression and exogenous recombinant ITLN-1 administration significantly suppressed excessive ATF6 activation, modulated the JNK signaling pathway, improved cell viability, reduced intracellular calcium overload and reactive oxygen species accumulation, and attenuated neuronal apoptosis. In vivo, ITLN-1 ameliorated neurological deficits, reduced neuronal damage, and alleviated demyelination, whereas ITLN-1 knockdown produced opposite effects. SIGNIFICANCE: Excessive ATF6 activation underlies CIRI-induced neuronal injury. ITLN-1 exerts neuroprotection by inhibiting ATF6 and modulating JNK signaling, thereby alleviating mitochondrial dysfunction and reducing apoptosis. These findings highlight the ITLN-1/ATF6 axis as a promising therapeutic target for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Echinocystic acid alleviates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury through PPARγ-dependent modulation of microglial polarization and pyroptotic signaling.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) worsens outcomes after ischemic stroke, yet effective pharmacological interventions remain limited. Echinocystic acid (EA), a pentacyclic triterpenoid isolated from the fruits of Gleditsia sinensis Lam., has shown neuroprotective activity in CIRI, but its direct molecular target and underlying mechanism remain unclear. In this study, using network pharmacology, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance, and subsequent validation in middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) mice and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-treated BV2 cells, we identified peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) as a potential target of EA and provided evidence supporting direct binding between EA and PPARγ. EA significantly reduced infarct volume and brain edema while improving neurological outcomes in MCAO mice, and also attenuated OGD/R-induced injury in BV2 cells. Mechanistically, EA restored PPARγ expression, promoted microglial M2 polarization, reduced IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α levels, increased IL-10 production, and attenuated NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD-associated pyroptotic signaling in both in vivo and in vitro models. These effects were largely reversed by the PPARγ antagonist GW9662. Collectively, these findings indicate that EA protects against CIRI, at least in part, through a PPARγ-dependent mechanism involving promotion of microglial M2 polarization and attenuation of NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD-associated pyroptotic signaling, highlighting the therapeutic potential of EA in CIRI.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Responsive Iron-Barium Titanate Schottky Heterojunction-Embedded Hydrogel Accelerates Burn Wound Healing through Bidirectional Hydrogen-Piezocatalytic Redox Modulation.
articles.abstract: Burn wound healing is regulated by a spatiotemporal redox hierarchy, where early reactive oxygen species (ROS) overload drives inflammation, while late ROS deficiency hinders regeneration. Programming this bidirectional sequence requires time-phased, counter-directional ROS control. Herein, we report a nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates hydrogen therapy with piezocatalytic therapy, enabling on-demand redox programming across the entire healing cascade. The system constructs a metal-semiconductor Schottky heterojunction derived from the in situ reduction of Fe2+ within the mesopores of barium titanate. The mesoporous confinement and interfacial coupling program the hydrolysis of nanoscale zero-valent iron for sustained, early-stage hydrogen delivery to scavenge toxic ROS, while the established Schottky barrier efficiently suppresses charge recombination, thereby executing ultrasound-triggered piezoelectric polarization and charge separation for on-demand ROS generation in later-stage pro-regenerative signaling. Embedded within a polyacrylamide/carboxymethyl chitosan double-network hydrogel with inherent antibacterial activity, the resulting system exhibits superior antioxidant capacity and piezocatalytic responsivity, as well as promotion of fibroblast migration, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage polarization. In a mouse burn model, this redox-programmable platform orchestrates phased healing, attenuating early inflammation, sustaining neovascularization, and suppressing late fibrosis, achieving accelerated wound closure. Collectively, this work establishes a redox programming paradigm via heterojunction catalysis, coupling spatiotemporal ROS scavenging and generation for dynamic tissue regeneration.

articles.title: Effects of Exercise Preconditioning on Promoting Endogenous Recovery Responses After Ischemic Stroke in Late-Adult Mice.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes substantial neurological impairment, and although poststroke rehabilitation can support recovery, neurological deficits often limit the feasibility of exercise in clinical settings. Prestroke exercise has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance resilience to ischemic injury, but most preclinical studies have relied on young adult rodents, in which spontaneous recovery can sometimes obscure clinically meaningful functional effects. However, the impact of exercise preconditioning in later stages of adulthood remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated whether a treadmill exercise preconditioning regimen confers neuroprotection and improves recovery-related responses in late-adult mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion. METHODS: Eight-month-old male mice were assigned to sedentary or exercise groups. Following 5 weeks of treadmill running (5 days per week after 1 week of acclimatization), mice underwent 45 minutes of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion. Behavioral assessments and body-weight monitoring were performed before and after middle cerebral artery occlusion. Infarct volume and cellular responses were evaluated 14 days after stroke. RESULTS: Fourteen days after stroke, lesion volume was significantly reduced in the exercise group compared with sedentary controls. Exercise preconditioning enhanced neurogenesis, oligodendrogenesis, and CD31-positive vascular responses while suppressing reactive astrocyte activation. Functional improvements were consistently observed across multiple behavioral assays in late-adult mice. CONCLUSIONS: Preconditioning with treadmill exercise provides neuroprotection against ischemic stroke in late-adult mice by reducing infarct volume and promoting recovery-associated cellular responses. These findings demonstrate that the functional benefits of prestroke exercise extend beyond the young adult stage and support the potential value of regular physical activity as a strategy to mitigate ischemic brain injury later in adulthood.

articles.title: Localized Hydrogen Release Driven by Mg-Pd Microgalvanic Cells from 3D-Printed Microneedles Reverses Redox Homeostasis for Psoriasis Treatment.
articles.abstract: 2 2 2 2+ Psoriasis therapy faces multiple challenges, including refractory, recurrence, and various comorbidities, attributed to its complex pathogenesis driven by aberrant keratinocyte proliferation, oxidative stress imbalance, and inflammation. These three factors form a vicious cycle, and cycle disruption holds great therapeutic potential for psoriasis. However, current therapies merely focus on symptom relief or anti-inflammatory effects alone with ignoring the essential cycle. To address the issues, a magnesium (Mg)-palladium (Pd) micro-galvanic cell (MP) with spontaneous electrochemical corrosion was constructed. MP released hydrogen (H), inhibiting keratinocyte hyperproliferation, scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) and •OH, activating KEAP1‑NRF2 antioxidant signaling pathway, while generated Mgexerted anti‑inflammatory effects. Furthermore, hollow microneedles loaded with MP (MP-MN) were fabricated via 3D printing to penetrate the stratum corneum for deep Hdelivery. In the imiquimod-induced psoriatic mouse model, MP‑MN topical treatment restored skin thickness, ameliorated oxidative stress, decreased splenic Th17/Treg ratio, and lowered both local and systemic pro‑inflammatory cytokine levels. Collectively, MP‑MN presented a comprehensive strategy for anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immune-regulatory effects in psoriasis, broadening the applications of Hand micro-galvanic cells in skin disorders.

articles.title: Cerebral Blood Flow-Derived Myogenic Dynamics Reveal Impaired Postischemic Cerebrovascular Recovery in Experimental Stroke.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Restoration of cerebral blood flow (CBF) after ischemic stroke does not necessarily indicate recovery of cerebrovascular regulation. We tested whether myogenic-band dynamics derived directly from CBF signals provide information beyond mean perfusion during cerebral ischemia and after acute stroke. METHODS: Transient focal cerebral ischemia was induced in 29 Sprague-Dawley rats using middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion. Bilateral laser-Doppler flowmetry (LDF)-derived CBF signals were decomposed using empirical mode decomposition and Hilbert transform, and myogenic-band activity (0.15-0.4 Hz) was quantified by absolute and relative power. Cross-validated logistic regression models were used to evaluate whether myogenic-band power provided discriminative information beyond mean CBF alone. RESULTS: Ipsilateral mean CBF fell from 73.5±51.8 p.u. at baseline to 52.2±38.0 p.u. during late ischemia (P=0.0088), then increased to 126.6±91.5 p.u. after 3 hours of reperfusion (P=0.0050 versus baseline). Relative myogenic-band power decreased from 37.43±14.65% to 13.35±7.51% during ischemia (P<0.0001) and remained below baseline after reperfusion (20.74±12.02%, P=0.00033 versus baseline); contralateral relative power was comparatively preserved. Combining mean CBF and myogenic-band power improved discrimination of baseline from late ischemia (AUC, 0.99 versus 0.70 for mean CBF alone) and late reperfusion (AUC, 0.88 versus 0.70). CONCLUSIONS: Frequency-specific analysis of LDF-derived CBF reveals persistent, lateralized abnormalities in myogenic-band dynamics that are not captured by mean perfusion alone. The persistence of depressed myogenic activity despite restored or elevated mean CBF demonstrates incomplete recovery of frequency-specific oscillatory dynamics after reperfusion. These findings support myogenic-band power as a potential functional measure of persistent postischemic cerebrovascular dysfunction.

articles.title: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. (Funded by Shenyang Science Tech Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657470).

articles.title: Stage-Associated Efficacy of Systemically Administered Neural Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes in Ischemic Stroke through the Prevention of Cx43 Degradation.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke pathology is highly dynamic, making the optimal timing for biological interventions highly elusive. This study investigated the stage-associated therapeutic efficacy of neural stem cell-derived exosomes (NSC-Exos) for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion. The in vivo evaluations identified a restricted therapeutic window closely associated with the temporal evolution of the ischemic microenvironment. Early exosome intervention (4 or 24 h post-ischemia) significantly reduced infarct volume, restored blood-brain barrier integrity, and improved neurological functional recovery. In contrast, delayed administration (48 h) failed to reduce the mortality rate and provide meaningful neuroprotection. To examine the molecular basis of this time dependence, we integrated temporal proteomic profiling of the ischemic penumbra with small RNA sequencing of NSC-Exos. The analytical and functional data suggest that early NSC-Exo delivery transfers miR-9-5p to suppress Nedd4 expression, thereby restoring the Connexin 43 protein pool and stabilizing the astrocytic network to halt initial microenvironmental collapse. Collectively, this study underscores the critical importance of intervention timing and provides a potential translational strategy for utilizing NSC-Exos as a targeted, stage-specific therapy in acute ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
articles.abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

articles.title: Outcomes of Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Endovascular Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke Due to Cardioembolism: A Secondary Analysis of the POST-UK Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis improves outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion. METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of the POST-UK (Adjunctive Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Near-Complete to Complete Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke) trial, which was conducted from November 15, 2022, to March 29, 2024. Patients were randomly assigned to the intra-arterial urokinase group or the control group. The primary outcome was disability-free survival at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 1. Safety outcomes included 90-day all-cause death, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours. RESULTS: P P Among 209 patients with cardioembolism (median age 73 [interquartile range, 63-81] years; 45.9% men), 106 were assigned to the control group and 103 to the intra-arterial urokinase group. Compared with the control group, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly increased the odds of disability-free survival at 90 days (adjusted risk ratio, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.08-2.06];=0.01; inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted risk ratio, 1.47 [95% CI, 1.04-2.09];=0.03). No significant differences were found between groups in 90-day mortality rate, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, or any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly improved disability-free survival at 90 days without increasing the risk of death or intracranial hemorrhage. articles.title: Thrombus stiffness depends on occlusion site and influences thrombectomy outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Only 60% of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) achieve successful reperfusion after the first endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) attempt. In vitro studies have shown that thrombus stiffness influences thrombus-device interaction and retrieval efficacy. This prospective observational study investigates how thrombus stiffness relates to clinical factors, thrombus imaging characteristics and histological composition. It further explores the association between thrombus stiffness and EVT success, as measured by the modified first-pass reperfusion (mFPR). PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 281 thrombus samples were collected from 51 AIS patients undergoing EVT. Thrombus stiffness was quantified using compressive mechanical testing, composition from histological staining and radiological characteristics from pre-interventional non-contrast computed tomography (CT) and CT angiography. Statistical analysis was performed using linear and logistic mixed-effects regression models. RESULTS: Thrombi retrieved from the proximal M2 segment of the middle cerebral artery showed significant lower stiffness (0.236 kPa, 95% CI, 0.136-0.409) compared to those from the M1 segment (0.760 kPa, 95% CI, 0.492-1.174) and from the ICA (1.106 kPa, 95% CI, 0.558-2.192). Occlusion location was the strongest clinical marker of thrombus stiffness. Adjusted mFPR probability was 40.4% (95% CI, 24.5-67.0) for thrombi retrieved from the ICA, 89.7% (95% CI, 79.5-97.0) for M1 occlusions, and 53.0% (95% CI, 30.8-84.7) for M2 occlusions. CONCLUSION: Thrombi in distal vessels of the anterior cerebral circulation are significantly softer than those in proximal intracranial arteries. First-pass EVT success is lower for the stiffest thrombi from the ICA and for the softest thrombi from M2, providing a foundation for future biomechanically informed thrombus removal strategies to optimise AIS treatment.

articles.title: Intranuclear localisation of KLF3-AS1 under the balance of histone acetylation and methylation in BMSCs ameliorates cerebral ischaemia‒reperfusion injury by preserving microglial mitochondrial function and inhibiting inflammatory polarisation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischaemic stroke occurs when blood flow to the brain is obstructed. Rapid restoration of blood supply frequently induces cerebral ischaemia‒reperfusion injury (CIRI). Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC)-derived exosomes exhibit promising therapeutic potential for CIRI. In-depth exploration of their therapeutic mechanisms holds crucial significance for CIRI management. METHODS: 2+ The middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO) model was established in mice. An in vitro ischaemic stroke model was established by treating BV-2 cells with oxygen‒glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Exosomes were isolated from BMSCs and intranasally administrated into mice or added into BV-2 cells. Neurological deficits, grasping and coordination function were evaluated. Cell viability, apoptosis, proliferation and migration were examined. The localisation of KLF3-AS1 was examined by combined staining of immunofluorescence and fluorescence in situ hybridisation. Intracellular Caand adenosine triphosphate levels, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and membrane potential were assessed. RESULTS: KLF3-AS1 enhanced BMSC viability, proliferation and migration, accompanied by epigenetic reprogramming at its promoter characterised by increased H3K27 acetylation (H3K27Ac) and decreased H3K27 trimethylation (H3K27Me3). BMSC-derived KLF3-AS1-enriched exosomes indicated therapeutic efficacy in both in vivo and in vitro models of cerebral ischaemia. In MCAO-induced mice, these exosomes alleviated neurological deficits and shifted microglial polarisation from pro-inflammatory M1-like to anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotypes. Similar effects were observed in OGD/R-treated BV-2 microglia, where KLF3-AS1-enriched exosomes attenuated oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction while upregulating Silent Information Regulator 3 (SIRT3) expression. Mechanistically, KLF3-AS1 facilitated ETS Variant Transcription Factor 4 (ETV4) nuclear translocation to activate SIRT3 transcription in microglia, and inhibition of SIRT3 abolished the neuroprotective effects of exosomal KLF3-AS1. CONCLUSION: BMSC-derived exosomes delivering KLF3-AS1 ameliorates CIRI by preserving microglial mitochondrial function and inhibiting inflammatory polarisation, highlighting KLF3-AS1 as a critical epigenetic regulator and exosome-mediated therapeutic agent for CIRI through the ETV4/SIRT3 axis. KEY POINTS/HIGHLIGHTS: KLF3-AS1 enhances bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) function via promoter H3K27Ac/H3K27Me3 reprogramming. KLF3‑AS1 directly binds ETS Variant Transcription Factor 4 (ETV4) to activate Silent Information Regulator 3 (SIRT3), preserving mitochondrial integrity. BMSC‑derived exosomal KLF3‑AS1 promotes M2 microglial polarisation and ameliorates cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Translating Stroke Microenvironment Cues Into Materials Design: Intelligent Nanomaterials for Ischemic Stroke Therapy.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS), caused by cerebral blood vessel occlusion, leads to ischemia, hypoxia, and irreversible brain tissue damage. Current treatments primarily rely on thrombolytic agents like alteplase, urokinase, and streptokinase for rapid reperfusion. However, these therapies are limited by narrow therapeutic windows, rapid clearance, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, off-target effects, and the complex ischemic microenvironment. These have led to increased interest in nanomaterial-based platforms to improve the precision and efficacy of IS treatment. The IS microenvironment, characterized by oxidative stress, inflammation, ionic imbalance, acidosis, and BBB disruption, provides valuable cues for designing responsive nanomaterials. Nanomaterials engineered to respond to reactive oxygen species, pH, enzymes, light, ultrasound, or magnetic fields can enable targeted drug delivery, controlled release, and multi-modal interventions, enhancing therapeutic precision. This review discusses the IS microenvironment, limitations of traditional therapies, recent advances in intelligent nanomaterials for IS treatment, and the major barriers that currently limit clinical translation.

articles.title: Current and emerging neuromodulation techniques for motor recovery after ischemic stroke: a 2026 update.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Neuromodulation technologies have emerged as promising tools to enhance motor recovery following ischemic stroke. Acute reperfusion therapy remains highly time-dependent, underscoring the need for interventions that augment post-stroke neuroplasticity. Brain stimulation techniques aim to modulate cortical excitability and promote adaptive reorganization of motor networks during the critical recovery period after stroke. AREAS COVERED: The authors review recent advances in neuromodulation strategies for post-stroke motor recovery, as well as the key principles underlying neuromodulation. Major noninvasive modalities, including transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), and low-intensity focused ultrasound stimulation (LIFUS), are reviewed alongside emerging applications of invasive techniques such as deep brain stimulation (DBS) and vagus nerve stimulation (VNS). Recent randomized clinical trials and translational studies are also highlighted. This article is based on literature obtained through PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov searches for content published between 1 January 2020 and 30 March 202630 March 2026 and was supplemented by earlier landmark studies relevant to stroke recovery and neuromodulation. EXPERT OPINION: Although neuromodulation technologies demonstrate encouraging safety profiles, clinical trial results feature notable neutral results. Future studies bear the burden of refining stimulation paradigms, patient selection, and rehabilitation dosing, possibly leveraging personalized, biomarker-driven patient selection.

articles.title: Extracellular lactate enhances IL-10 transcription via H4K5 lactylation and promotes an A2-like reactive-astrocyte phenotype after ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke triggers a rapid rise in lactate levels in the brain tissue. The neuroprotective role of exogenous lactate administered during the reperfusion phase has recently garnered attention. A neuroprotective A2 phenotype of reactive astrocytes (RACs) is characterized by interleukin-10 (IL-10) upregulation, which mitigates neuroinflammation. However, whether exogenous lactate drives A2-like polarization of RACs remains unknown. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which lactate regulates this process. METHODS: Rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) and in vitro primary RACs models were established. Western blotting, immunofluorescence staining, and RT-qPCR were used to assess A1/A2 polarization markers, IL-10 expression, histone lactylation, and related neuroimmune signaling molecules. Ubiquitination, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and dual-luciferase reporter assays were performed to clarify the mechanism by which lactate regulates IL-10 expression and A2-like polarization of RACs. RESULTS: Our results demonstrated that increased lactate levels after ischemic stroke correlated with A2 polarization of RACs. Lactate treatment significantly enhanced A2 polarization and reduced infarct volume in the rat MCAO model. Mechanistically, lactate activated signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) signaling while suppressing sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) expression and synergistically enhancing H4K5 lactylation (H4K5la) and IL-10 expression, thereby driving RACs toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed that elevated extracellular lactate in the acute phase of ischemic stroke drove RACs toward an A2-like phenotype through the Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP1)/STAT3/IL-10 and YAP1/SIRT1/H4K5la signaling axes. These findings provide a theoretical basis for targeting RAC lactylation as a potential therapeutic strategy to limit inflammatory damage after stroke.

articles.title: Mitochondria-associated ferroptosis in ischemic stroke: Pathophysiological evolution, interorganelle crosstalk, and therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) results from an acute interruption of cerebral blood flow and the ensuing collapse of energy metabolism. Although vascular recanalization can salvage the ischemic penumbra, its overall benefit remains constrained by a narrow therapeutic window and reperfusion injury. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, contributes to neuronal injury after IS and can amplify ischemia/reperfusion injury. By integrating energy metabolism, iron homeostasis, and redox balance, mitochondria can shape ferroptosis susceptibility within the energy-depleted, iron-dysregulated, and oxidatively stressed ischemic brain. However, most studies have examined iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation at the whole-cell level, leaving the temporal and interorganelle dimensions of mitochondrial regulation of ferroptosis insufficiently integrated. Here, we organize mitochondria-associated ferroptosis across the pathological course of IS, from metabolic reprogramming and substrate accumulation during ischemia to the reverse electron transport-associated reactive oxygen species burst during early reperfusion and subsequent disruption of mitochondrial quality control. We further examine mitochondrial crosstalk with the endoplasmic reticulum, lysosomes, lipid droplets, and nucleus, compare ferroptosis susceptibility across neurovascular unit cell populations, and map these mechanisms onto pharmacological interventions and mechanistically plausible therapeutic windows. Finally, we assess barriers to the clinical translation of mitochondria-targeted therapies and provide a stage-resolved framework for developing neuroprotective strategies in IS.

articles.title: Activatable MRI-Trackable Spherical Nucleic Acids for Idebenone Delivery Against Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
articles.abstract: 2 Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a key driver of poor prognosis in ischemic stroke. Idebenone (IDBN) shows promise for mitigating IRI, but its efficacy is limited by poor brain accumulation. Moreover, IDBN cannot be visually tracked, making it difficult to confirm whether it reaches the ischemic brain and exerts therapeutic effects. Here, IDBN functionalized with a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-cleavable bond is grafted onto phosphorothioate-modified DNA strands and co-assembled with ultrasmall superparamagnetic iron oxide (USPIO) to form USPIO-IDBN-SNAs, where SNAs stands for spherical nucleic acids. Exploiting upregulated class A scavenger receptors, USPIO-IDBN-SNAs target the ischemic area without targeting modifications and increase local IDBN concentration. Hydrophobic IDBN inside the SNAs limits water access to USPIO clusters, suppressing their contrast-enhancing ability. Under oxidative stress, IDBN is rapidly released and exerts remarkable protection. This release allows USPIO clusters to re-establish contact with water, activating their contrast-enhancing ability on T-weighted imaging. Collectively, USPIO-IDBN-SNAs provide significant neuroprotection against IRI and offer a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-visible platform to monitor IDBN release in the ischemic brain, presenting a promising theranostic approach for precise, trackable stroke therapy.

articles.title: Deterioration of Peri-Infarct Microvascular Hemodynamics Following Successful Reperfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke Predicts Infarct Growth.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Microvascular hemodynamic deterioration is a proposed mechanism underlying the no-reflow phenomenon in acute ischemic stroke. Experimental studies suggested that relative heterogeneity of capillary transit time (RTH) is a potential imaging biomarker of microvascular impairment. We investigated the relationship between peri-infarct RTH and infarct growth, measured on immediate post-thrombectomy (PT) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with successful reperfusion. METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study from the University of California, Los Angeles, patients with acute ischemic stroke from 2015 to 2020 were included if they had excellent reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2c) and diffusion- and perfusion-weighted MRIs at baseline, immediately PT, and 24 to 48 hours after thrombectomy. Peri-infarct regions were defined as time to maximum ≥6-second regions on baseline MRI that were not infarcted on immediate PT MRI. Following image coregistration, quantitative values of perfusion parameters, including RTH, were obtained from peri-infarct regions on immediate PT MRI. Two primary outcomes were assessed: (1) infarct growth ≥10 mL and (2) poor functional outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale score >2). Associations between clinical and imaging parameters and outcomes were evaluated using univariate analysis. Age, sex, and covariates that were significant in univariate analysis were included in logistic regression analyses. RESULTS: P P P P Among 47 patients included in the analysis (62% women; mean age, 72±13 years; median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, 14), 20 (43%) patients had substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcome. Peri-infarct RTH was significantly (=0.005) higher in patients with infarct growth >10 mL than those without and remained as an independent predictor (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-2.0];=0.04). Similarly, the peri-infarct RTH was significantly higher (<0.001) in patients with poor functional outcomes than those with good functional outcomes and remained as a significant predictor of poor functional outcome (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-1.9];=0.03). CONCLUSIONS: Increased peri-infarct RTH on immediate PT MRI predicts substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcomes in successfully reperfused patients with acute ischemic stroke. Results highlight the role of microvascular dysfunction depicted by elevated RTH as a potential marker of no-reflow phenomenon despite excellent macrovascular reperfusion.

articles.title: Global Burden of Pediatric Stroke (1990-2023): A Shift From Mortality Toward Disability.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric stroke is a significant cause of long-term disability worldwide, with outcomes influenced by age, stroke subtype, and access to care. Our objective was to define the global burden of pediatric stroke by its impact on mortality and disability. METHODS: The Global Burden of Disease study uses advanced statistical modeling to analyze health across locations, synthesizing data on mortality, morbidity, and risk factors. We examined 2023 data from the study to assess deaths, years of life lost, and years lived with disability during 3 eras (1990-2001, 2002-2013, and 2014-2023) across high-income and low- and middle-income countries. We stratified the analysis by sex, age group, and stroke subtype. We calculated the proportion of burden attributable to disability (years lived with disability/[years lived with disability+years of life lost]) to assess shifts from fatal to nonfatal disease over time. RESULTS: Between 1990 and 2023, global age-standardized pediatric stroke incidence declined only modestly, whereas age-standardized years of life lost rates declined significantly, indicating that the lower mortality burden reflected better survival rather than a large reduction in disease occurrence. Because years lived with disability rates remained comparatively stable as mortality declined, the proportion of disease burden attributable to disability rose from 14.6% (1990-2001) to 21.7% (2014-2023). This transition was uneven across settings: high-income countries achieved faster mortality declines and reached a higher disability share, whereas low- and middle-income countries retained a higher mortality burden, reflecting a dual burden of ongoing premature death and rising disability. These patterns were consistent across age and sex strata. CONCLUSIONS: These data indicate that pediatric stroke is undergoing an epidemiological transition from a mortality-dominant burden to one increasingly driven by disability, reflecting improved survival but with uneven distribution worldwide. Reducing the disability burden, through better stroke recognition education and expanded access to prevention, acute stroke care systems, reperfusion, and rehabilitation, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, should be prioritized alongside efforts to close persistent global inequities in outcomes.

articles.title: Poly (Lipoic Acid) Nanoparticles With High Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability and Enhanced Anti-Ferroptotic Activity for Ischemic Stroke Treatment.
articles.abstract: Lipoic acid (LA) scavenges free radicals and was clinically tested for ischemic stroke. However, the short half-life and weak efficacy in penetrating the blood-brain barrier (BBB) limit its use in the brain. Here, we developed poly (lipoic acid) nanoparticles (pLANs) with a half-life of more than 15 h and a high efficiency to penetrate the BBB for ischemic stroke treatment. With intraperitoneal injection, imaging studies using fluorescently labelled pLANs of different sizes revealed that 30 nm pLANs entered the brain most rapidly and provided the strongest protection against ischemic injury. In vitro, 30 nm pLANs significantly prevented cell death induced by oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), reduced total ROS and lipid peroxides, and inhibited GPX4-dependent ferroptosis. In rat models of cerebral ischemia/reperfusion, 30 nm pLANs extended the therapeutic window by 3 h relative to LA monomer and prevented neuronal damage effectively at only half the dose. These findings demonstrate that 30 nm pLANs effectively cross the BBB, sustain drug levels in blood, and protect against neuronal death by suppressing ferroptosis, offering a promising strategy for ischemic stroke and other neurological disorders associated with oxidative stress.

articles.title: Protocatechuic acid protects neural stem cells against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by suppressing JAK2/STAT3 signaling and restoring mitophagy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Neural stem cells (NSCs) are important for endogenous brain repair but are highly vulnerable to mitochondrial dysfunction during cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). Preliminary bioinformatics analysis suggested that immune microenvironment remodeling and JAK/STAT signaling activation are involved in CIRI pathology. This study investigated whether protocatechuic acid (PCA) protects NSCs after ischemia-reperfusion injury and explored the underlying mechanisms focusing on the JAK2/STAT3 pathway and mitophagy. RESULTS: Bioinformatics analysis identified JAK/STAT signaling as a potential regulatory node in CIRI. Transcriptome sequencing further showed that PCA markedly altered the gene expression profile of NSCs, with differentially expressed genes enriched in the JAK/STAT pathway. In vitro, PCA suppressed OGD/R-induced JAK2/STAT3 activation, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced DCFH-DA and MitoSOX Red oxidation-sensitive fluorescence signals, promoted TOMM20/LC3 colocalization, enhanced PINK1/Parkin-related mitophagy, and improved NSC survival. Co-treatment with the JAK2 inhibitor AG490 further supported the protective and pro-mitophagic effects of PCA, whereas co-treatment with the JAK/STAT pathway activator RO8191 weakened PCA-mediated mitochondrial protection and mitophagy restoration. In vivo, PCA improved neurological function, reduced infarct volume, attenuated hippocampal neuronal injury, preserved endogenous NSCs and NeuN-positive cells, and enhanced mitophagy-related signals in MCAO/R rats. Importantly, in vivo Western blot analysis showed that PCA suppressed MCAO/R-induced JAK2/STAT3 phosphorylation, whereas RO8191 co-treatment attenuated this inhibitory effect and weakened the protective effects of PCA, supporting the involvement of JAK2/STAT3 inhibition in PCA-mediated neuroprotection. CONCLUSION: PCA alleviates CIRI and protects NSCs partly by suppressing JAK2/STAT3 activation, restoring mitochondrial function, and promoting PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy. These findings provide experimental evidence supporting mitochondrial quality control and NSC protection as potential therapeutic targets for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Microglial SREBP2 regulate cholesterol-related lipid metabolism and inflammatory levels following ischemic stroke via the autophagy pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dysregulated lipid metabolism and inflammation exacerbate brain injury, with abnormal cholesterol metabolism playing a role in stroke condition. SREBPs are key transcription factors regulating lipid synthesis, and their activation is linked to autophagy. It remains unclear whether autophagy clears lipids and modulates inflammation after ischemic stroke, and whether SREBP2 affect cholesterol metabolism and inflammation via autophagy. This study aims to investigate the role of SREBPs and the mediating mechanism of autophagy in post-ischemic stroke lipid dysregulation and inflammation. METHODS: In vivo mice models of ischemic stroke (middle cerebral artery occlusion, MCAO) and in vitro neuronal oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) models were employed. Through interfering with SREBP2, combined with autophagy inhibitor/activator treatment, we detected cholesterol and cholesteryl ester in microglia and brain tissue, the expression levels of inflammatory factors, and the expression changes of autophagy-related proteins (LC3, p62) and SREBP downstream lipid metabolism-related genes. RESULTS: After ischemic stroke, the expression of SREBP2 in brain tissue was significantly upregulated, the autophagy pathway was activated, accompanied by cholesterol and lipid accumulation and increased expression of inflammatory factors. Interfering with SREBP2 expression significantly inhibited the excessive activation of the autophagy pathway, reduced the content of cholesterol-related lipids in brain tissue and neurons, decreased the release of inflammatory factors, and alleviated cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. In microglia-neuron co-culture experiments, SREBPs interference in microglia significantly improved the survival rate of OGD/R-induced injured neurons and reduced neuronal apoptosis, while behavioral tests revealed that SREBP2 interference remarkably promoted neural function recovery in MCAO mice. CONCLUSION: SREBP2 regulate the autophagy pathway to affect the balance of cholesterol-related lipid metabolism and the intensity of inflammatory responses after ischemic stroke, thereby participating in the pathophysiological process of cerebral ischemic injury, which provides a new target and theoretical basis for the treatment of ischemic stroke.
