articles.title: Morphology matters: Spherical versus rod-shaped selenium nanoparticles exert divergent neuroprotection after cerebral ischemia/reperfusion via redox reprogramming and mitochondrial bioenergetics.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of death and disability, with reperfusion injury-driven oxidative stress representing a key therapeutic target. Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) show neuroprotective potential, yet the influence of nanoparticle morphology remains poorly understood. OBJECTIVE: To compare the neuroprotective effects of spherical (Sph) versus rod-shaped (Rods) SeNPs in models of cerebral ischemia/reperfusion, focusing on redox modulation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, and functional outcomes. METHODS: Primary rat cortical neuron-astrocyte co-cultures were exposed to Sph or Rods (1-10 μg/mL). ROS production, mitochondrial membrane potential, cell viability, gene expression, and neurite outgrowth were assessed. In vivo, transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) was induced in rats, followed by intraperitoneal injection of Sph or Rods (1 μg/g) 1 h post-reperfusion. Neurological outcomes and infarct volume were evaluated at 24 and 48 h. RESULTS: Low concentrations (1-5 μg/mL) of both morphologies upregulated antioxidant genes, suppressed pro-apoptotic factors, enhanced Bcl2 expression, and promoted neuritogenesis without cytotoxicity. High concentration (10 μg/mL) induced pro-oxidant shift, with Sph triggering early apoptosis and Rods causing late apoptosis/necrosis. Both SeNPs restored CO-induced ΔΨm collapse and normalized respiratory chain function. In vivo, Sph improved motor coordination without reducing infarct volume, whereas Rods significantly reduced infarct size but showed less sustained behavioral improvement. CONCLUSIONS: Nanoparticle morphology critically dictates therapeutic strategy: spherical SeNPs prioritize functional preservation, whereas nanorods confer structural tissue salvage. These findings establish morphology as a key determinant of SeNPs bioactivity and provide a rationale for morphology-guided design of nanotherapeutics for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Hydrogen reshapes the senescent microenvironment of callus to enhance the healing of anti-osteoporotic-drug-induced atypical femoral fracture.
articles.abstract: Long-term bisphosphonates (BPs) are widely used to treat osteoporosis, however, they are paradoxically associated with the development of atypical femoral fractures (AFFs), which often characterized by impaired healing. In this study, we induced an AFF model using zoledronate (ZOL) administration in ovariectomized (OVX) osteoporotic rats, following a unilateral femoral fracture. Here we identified that a local pro-senescent microenvironment causes persistent inflammation and impairs effective regeneration in rat AFFs. Molecular hydrogen has demonstrated anti-senescence and anti-inflammatory properties, yet its effects on AFF healing remain unexplored. Therefore, we treated the AFF rats with hydrogen rich water (HRW). The outcomes were assessed by radiographs, histology, micro-CT, and biomechanical tests. The fracture microenvironment was analyzed based on the indicators of senescence, fibrosis, macrophage polarization, cytokine expression, and angiogenesis. We found that HRW significantly promoted callus bridging and resolved the non-union gap in ZOL-induced AFFs, whereas the ZOL group exhibited persistent fibrous tissue. Micro-CT and biomechanical tests confirmed that HRW did not compromise the mechanical strength of the bone mass elevated by BPs. Instead, HRW specifically attenuated the local senescent microenvironment, with a reduction in both SA-β-gal activity and the expression of p16, p21 within the fracture gap. This was accompanied by clearance of pathological fibroblasts, a shift from pro-inflammatory M1 to anti-inflammatory M2 macrophages, a rebalanced cytokine profile, and restored formation of osteogenesis-coupled type-H vessels. Our findings confirm that molecular hydrogen facilitates AFFs healing by locally reversing the senescent microenvironment, rather than boosting systemic bone formation. This creates a favorable niche for callus bridging, representing a novel therapeutic strategy for fracture delayed union or non-union.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal Core-Shell Microspheres Enable Hydrogen-Mediated Redox Priming and Kartogenin-Induced Cartilage Regeneration for Osteoarthritis Bio-Rescue.
articles.abstract: 2 2 The effective management of osteoarthritis (OA) remains a formidable clinical challenge due to a chronically inflamed joint microenvironment and the limited self-regenerative capacity of articular cartilage. To address these barriers, we developed an ultrasound-responsive core-shell microsphere platform engineered via a customized microfluidic capillary device. This system features a kartogenin (KGN)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) core encapsulated within a sodium alginate shell enriched with tin disulfide (SnS) nanosheets (SSN). Following intra-articular injection, non-invasive ultrasound stimulation triggers the localized SSN to generate low-concentration hydrogen gas (H). This in situ Hgeneration rapidly scavenges excess reactive oxygen species to restore redox homeostasis, thereby mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction and preserving chondrocyte viability. Consequently, this targeted antioxidative intervention suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion and polarizes synovial macrophages toward a pro-regenerative M2 phenotype. Within this newly stabilized microenvironment, the sustained release of KGN from the PLGA core successfully reverses extracellular matrix metabolic imbalances to promote cartilage repair. In a rat model of OA, this dual-functional, spatiotemporally controlled platform profoundly halted joint degeneration and preserved histological cartilage integrity. Collectively, this ultrasound-triggered core-shell microsphere system offers a highly promising, disease-modifying strategy for comprehensive OA therapy.

articles.title: Chemical Mechanisms of Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury and Neuroprotection in the Thrombectomy Era.
articles.abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has significantly improved outcomes for patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke. However, restoring the artery does not always re-establish full microvascular blood flow, tissue rescue, or a good neurological outcome. Ischemia-reperfusion injury varies over time, with distinct biochemical mechanisms dominating during ischemia, early reperfusion, and the subsequent hours. During ischemia, factors like adenosine triphosphate (ATP) depletion, ionic imbalance, calcium overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, acidosis, and metabolic changes such as succinate build-up render brain tissue highly vulnerable. When blood flow resumes, oxygen delivery to this stressed tissue can induce rapid mitochondrial redox shifts, electron leakage, reactive oxygen and nitrogen species formation, iron-dependent radical generation, and lipid peroxidation. Damage may then persist for hours through ongoing mitochondrial dysfunction, phospholipid hydroperoxide accumulation, reactive aldehydes, ferroptosis, blood-brain barrier breakdown, microvascular issues, and inflammation. Much of the mechanistic evidence supporting these processes derives from experimental studies, and their relevance to clinical outcomes after thrombectomy requires further validation. This narrative review tracks these chemical changes across the main phases of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and connects them to modern thrombectomy practices. It also explores how the timing of each process may inform neuroprotective strategies, drug delivery methods, patient selection via imaging, and future clinical trial approaches.

articles.title: Remote ischemic preconditioning protects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury through lactate-dependent AMPK/ULK1 signaling and autophagy.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major contributor to ischemic cerebral damage and poor functional outcomes following ischemic stroke, and effective neuroprotective strategies remain limited. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) has emerged as a promising, noninvasive approach; however, its underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether lactate serves as a key metabolic mediator linking RIPC to neuroprotection through regulation of autophagy. Using an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in PC12 cells and a middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model in rats, we demonstrate that I/R impairs autophagic flux, as evidenced by p62 accumulation and reduced LC3-II and Beclin-1 expression, leading to increased cellular apoptosis and injury. Lactate supplementation restored autophagic flux, enhanced cell viability, and suppressed apoptosis under OGD/R conditions. Mechanistically, lactate activated the AMPK/ULK1 signaling pathway, whereas pharmacological inhibition of AMPK or ULK1 attenuated lactate-induced autophagy and cytoprotection. In vivo, RIPC elevated plasma and cerebral lactate levels, activated AMPK/ULK1 signaling, promoted autophagy, reduced infarct volume, and improved acute neurological outcomes. Notably, blockade of lactate transport or inhibition of AMPK/ULK1 signaling attenuated these protective effects. Collectively, our findings suggest that lactate serves as an important mediator of RIPC-induced neuroprotection and reveal a novel lactate-AMPK/ULK1-autophagy axis that mitigates cerebral I/R injury. These results provide mechanistic insight into RIPC and suggest potential therapeutic targets for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: The RETRIAD Study: Comparative First-Pass Reperfusion Performance of EmboTrap III, Trevo NXT, and APERIO Stent Retrievers in Acute Large-Vessel Occlusion Stroke: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: n n n n n n n p Contemporary stent retrievers differ in design, yet direct comparative evidence regarding their first-pass reperfusion performance using a standardized endpoint remains limited. This study compared first-pass reperfusion outcomes among APERIO, Trevo NXT, and EmboTrap III.In this exploratory, single-center retrospective cohort study, 200 patients were screened between 1 March 2024 and 1 August 2026. Forty patients had not completed 90-day follow-up at the time of the initial data analysis. An additional 104 patients were excluded because of tandem occlusion (= 29), recanalization after intravenous thrombolysis before thrombectomy (= 8), distal vessel occlusion (= 30), or successful direct aspiration without stent-retriever deployment (= 37). The final cohort comprised 56 patients treated with first-line combined stent-retriever and aspiration thrombectomy using APERIO (= 28), Trevo NXT (= 14), or EmboTrap III (= 14). The primary endpoint was strict first-pass effect (FPE), defined as first-pass expanded Treatment in Cerebral Ischemia (eTICI) grade 2c-3.Strict FPE was achieved in 16/28 (57.1%), 9/14 (64.3%), and 9/14 (64.3%) patients, respectively (global exact= 0.879). Both comparisons with APERIO yielded an absolute risk difference of +7.1 percentage points (95% CI, -23.2 to +33.6). Exploratory adjusted analyses yielded imprecise estimates. Heidelberg-classified symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in zero, three, and two patients, respectively.No statistically detectable difference in strict FPE was demonstrated among the three device-based treatment strategies. However, the small sample size, wide confidence intervals, and nonrandomized treatment allocation preclude conclusions regarding device equivalence or causal effects.

articles.title: Diffusion-weighted imaging reversal after reperfusion therapy in acute ischemic stroke: associations with white matter hyperintensities and cerebral microbleeds.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) and cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) are common MRI markers of chronic small-vessel brain injury and have been associated with adverse outcomes after ischemic stroke. However, whether these markers influence early ischemic tissue reversibility following reperfusion therapy remains unclear. We therefore investigated their associations with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesion reversal, hemorrhagic complications, and short-term functional outcome after MRI-guided reperfusion therapy. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke undergoing MRI-guided intravenous thrombolysis, with or without additional mechanical thrombectomy, were included. According to the institutional protocol, follow-up MRI was planned 24 ± 6 h after treatment to assess DWI lesion evolution, WMH volume, and CMBs. DWI reversal was defined as a reduction of ≥ 25% in baseline DWI lesion volume. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of DWI reversal, intracerebral hemorrhage, and functional outcome at hospital discharge. RESULTS: Among 345 patients (median age 74 years [IQR 63-82], 48.1% female), 45 (13%) additionally underwent mechanical thrombectomy. DWI reversal occurred in 76 patients (22.0%) and was not associated with baseline WMH volume, CMBs, initial infarct volume, treatment modality, or thrombolysis time window. Higher baseline NIHSS and modified Rankin Scale scores were associated with lower odds of DWI reversal, whereas hypercholesterolemia was independently associated with increased odds of DWI reversal. We found no evidence of an association of WMH burden or CMB presence with intracerebral hemorrhage or of an independent association with functional outcome. Fourteen patients (4.1%) developed new CMBs on follow-up MRI. CONCLUSIONS: We found no evidence of an association between baseline WMH volume or CMB presence and early DWI lesion reversal or hemorrhagic complications following reperfusion therapy in this cohort. These findings provide no evidence that these two chronic MRI markers are major determinants of early infarct tissue reversibility. Larger multicenter studies incorporating comprehensive small-vessel disease phenotyping and long-term follow-up are warranted.

We therefore investigated their associations with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesion reversal, hemorrhagic complications, and short-term functional outcome after MRI-guided reperfusion therapy.

articles.title: Panax notoginseng -Derived Carbon Quantum Dots as a Novel Administration Strategy for Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Therapy.
articles.abstract: Panax notoginseng Panax notoginseng Panax notoginseng The present study aimed to synthesize-derived carbon quantum dots (PN-CDs) and explore their role in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). PN-CDs were synthesized by the hydrothermal method, and characterization and biocompatibility were assessed. Next, CIRI models were established using SH-SY5Y cells, primary neurons were treated with oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R), and rats were subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R). After PN-CDs treatment, inflammation, apoptosis, and oxidative stress were detected in neuronal cells and rats using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, flow cytometry, Western blot, and 2',7'-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate probe. Meanwhile, 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride, terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling, Nissl, and hematoxylin and eosin staining were employed to measure the pathological damage of rats. Additionally, CIRI rats were administered with PN-CDs,saponins (PNS),(PN), or edaravone to investigate whether PN-CDs had the best effect. The findings revealed that PN-CDs exhibited favorable biocompatibility and crossed the blood-brain barrier. In vitro, PN-CD treatment inhibited oxidative stress, apoptosis, and inflammation, as evidenced by the decrease of interleukin-1β (IL-1β), IL-6, Bax, C-caspase-3, tumor necrosis factor-α, malondialdehyde, and reactive oxygen species and the increase of superoxide dismutase, Bcl-2, and glutathione. In CIRI rats, PN-CDs improved pathological damage and suppressed inflammation, apoptosis, and oxidative stress. The therapeutic effect of PN-CDs on CIRI was distinctly better than that of PNS and PN, and comparable to that of the first-line drug edaravone. In short, PN-CDs, a novel and efficient administration strategy, alleviates CIRI by inhibiting apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation.

articles.title: Scutellarin as a multi-target neuroprotective agent: Analytical evidence, pharmacokinetic insights and translational strategies across neurodegenerative disorders.
articles.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders are a leading cause of disability and mortality globally, but effective disease-modifying therapeutic strategies are still largely unavailable. Scutellarin is a flavonoid glycoside extracted from Erigeron breviscapus (Vant.) Hand-Mazz. It has been widely studied in preclinical models of neurodegenerative disorders. In this study, we performed a systematic review of preclinical animal studies. We combined comprehensive database retrieval with quantitative synthesis of eligible outcomes. The pooled results demonstrated that scutellarin significantly reduced cerebral infarct volume and improved neurological deficit scores in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion models. It also ameliorated learning and memory impairments in experimental Alzheimer's disease (AD) models. Consistent neuroprotective effects were also found in models of depression, anxiety, Parkinson's disease, etc. Mechanistic analysis indicated that scutellarin produces multi-level neuroprotective effects. It acts by reducing oxidative stress, inhibiting neuroinflammation, suppressing apoptosis, stabilizing the neurovascular unit and other neurobiological processes. This review first evaluated the preclinical efficacy of scutellarin through systematic review and meta-analysis. It then integrated cross-disease mechanisms with network pharmacology, reverse virtual screening and molecular docking to identify computationally predicted targets. Although scutellarin shows promising preclinical effects, its clinical translation faces major limitations. These limitations include low oral bioavailability, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and insufficient data on brain exposure. Overall, scutellarin is a multi-target neuroprotective candidate. Future studies should focus on target validation, exposure-response modeling, delivery optimization and clinically relevant translational evaluation.

articles.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal mesenchymal stem cell-associated neuroimmune and neuronal signaling patterns after ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke induces coordinated yet spatially heterogeneous neuroimmune and neuronal responses that shape secondary injury and tissue remodeling. However, how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell administration is associated with these cell type-specific responses remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing of the ipsilateral cerebrum on days 1, 7, and 14 after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion with spatial transcriptomic profiling on day 7. A total of 55,520 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from control, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion, and mesenchymal stem cell-treated samples. In this exploratory dataset, the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion samples showed relatively greater representation of inflammatory and antigen-presenting microglial states and elevated expression of selected microglial state-associated genes, including Slfn4, Apoe, and Gpnmb. In the corresponding exploratory comparison, the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample showed relatively greater representation of homeostatic-associated and Lgals3/Spp1-enriched microglial states and lower expression of several inflammatory-associated genes. Spatial mapping further revealed regionally restricted expression of microglial and neuronal markers within the injured tissue. Excitatory neurons displayed preliminary mesenchymal stem cell-associated transcriptional patterns involving mitochondrial transcripts, oxidative phosphorylation, synaptic signaling, calcium-related functions, and apoptosis/autophagy-associated pathways. CellChat analysis computationally predicted relatively high levels of tumor necrosis factor, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand, and complement signaling in the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion sample, whereas the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample had relatively high levels of predicted activity of neuregulin, pleiotrophin and selected semaphorin. Together, these integrated datasets provide a hypothesis-generating framework linking microglial state remodeling, neuronal metabolic and synaptic programs, and predicted neuroimmune communication patterns after ischemic stroke. Because each omics condition or time point was represented by one biological sample, all the transcriptomic findings should be considered preliminary and exploratory and should be validated in independently replicated cohorts.

articles.title: Engineering a Translational Human Thrombus Platform to Evaluate Clinical Therapies in Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Recanalization failure after ischemic stroke remains a major clinical challenge, partly because cerebral thrombi display marked spatial heterogeneity that is poorly reproduced by experimental models. Here, we engineered a translational human blood-based thrombus platform that recapitulates key histological features of patient-derived stroke clots. METHODS: Under controlled conditions, the platform generated reproducible thrombi with pronounced interthrombus and intrathrombus heterogeneity, including alternating red blood cell-rich and platelet-rich territories. Multiscale structural and biochemical analyses confirmed the successful replication of the clinical biphasic organization associated with resistance to rtPA (recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator): a compact outer fibrin shell containing focal accumulations of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, and a dense inner core further stabilized by neutrophil extracellular traps. RESULTS: Functional thrombolysis assays demonstrated that this architecture directly dictates lytic susceptibility. Specifically, artificially breaching the outer fibrin shell (halved thrombi) significantly accelerated early rtPA-mediated lysis, proving its role as an effective physical barrier. Furthermore, lytic response was inherently linked to clot composition: platelet-rich thrombi with dense plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 and neutrophil extracellular trap networks exhibited profound resistance to standard rtPA compared with red blood cell-rich clots. Supporting the platform's translational relevance, this structural resistance was successfully overcome by clinically relevant strategies, including tenecteplase and adjunctive DNAse, consistent with observations from human stroke cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: By accurately reproducing the spatial organization and differential thrombolytic responses of human cerebral thrombi, this translational framework provides a robust preclinical tool to dissect lytic resistance and evaluate next-generation precision reperfusion therapies. Furthermore, developing robust ex vivo human platforms is increasingly critical to align with the replacement, reduction, refinement ethical guidelines for animal research.

METHODS: Under controlled conditions, the platform generated reproducible thrombi with pronounced interthrombus and intrathrombus heterogeneity, including alternating red blood cell-rich and platelet-rich territories.

articles.title: Intranasal Delivery of an Antioxidant Nanoassembly for Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK Signaling.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is caused by reduced cerebral blood flow, leading to excessive oxidative stress and neurological deficits. Curcumin (Cur) is a promising therapeutic agent, but its antioxidant activity is limited by low bioavailability and poor brain penetration. Herein, an intranasal delivery strategy using a tetrahedral framework nucleic acid (tFNAs)-Cur nanoassembly (tFNAs-Cur) was employed for CIRI treatment. tFNAs-Cur was synthesized through self-assembly, achieving a high Cur loading efficiency of 87% and exhibiting potent scavenging activity against reactive oxygen species (ROS) including O2·-, ·OH, and H2O2. In vitro studies showed that tFNAs-Cur inhibited oxygen glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-induced ROS elevation of cytoplasm and mitochondria, and enhanced proliferation and migration of SH-SY5Y cells. In vivo studies demonstrated that intranasal administration of tFNAs-Cur reduced cerebral infarct volume, enhanced neuronal survival, and improved neurological and behavioral outcomes in middle cerebral artery occlusion rats. Further mechanistic investigation using RNA sequencing revealed that tFNAs-Cur exerted its effects by activating the Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK signaling, thereby improving mitochondrial function and upregulating BDNF levels. Furthermore, hemolysis assays, serum biochemical measurements, and histopathological analyses demonstrated that tFNAs-Cur possessed a favorable biosafety profile both ex vivo and in vivo. This study provides an intranasal antioxidant nanoassembly strategy for CIRI and holds potential for clinical translation.

articles.title: Mechanism of Shanhu Qishiwei pills in regulating endoplasmic reticulum stress through GRP78/CHOP signaling pathway for the treatment of cerebral ischemia.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Stroke, a prevalent cerebrovascular condition, is characterized by high occurrence, disability, mortality, and recurrence rates. Shanhu Qishiwei pills (བྱུར་དམར་བདུན་ཅུ།, SHQSWP) are a Tibetan prescription, which were included in the national drug standard ZZ-8432 of the National Food and Drug Administration with approval number Z54020114. SHQSWP can relieve palpitation, tranquilize, and arrest convulsion and is mainly used for cerebral thrombosis, cerebral hemorrhage, and coronary heart disease. This study aimed to investigate the mechanism of SHQSWP for the treatment of cerebral ischemia. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to screen the differential proteins of SHQSWP for the treatment of cerebral ischemia and verify its mechanism in regulating the endoplasmic reticulum stress signaling pathway. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Triple quadrupole liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (HPLC-QqQ-MS) was to quantitatively detect 25 chemical components in SHQSWP. TTC staining, HE staining, Nissl staining, and TUNEL staining were used to verify the effectiveness of SHQSWP for the treatment of cerebral ischemia in middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model rats. Deferentially expressed proteins were screened using a protein chip, and the potential targets and signaling pathways of SHQSWP in the treatment of cerebral ischemia were visually screened using protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. Molecular docking technology was used to predict the binding affinity and binding mode of the key compounds in SHQSWP with related target proteins. RT-qPCR, WB and IF were used to verify the signaling pathways and targets regulated by SHQSWP in the treatment of cerebral ischemia. RESULTS: HPLC-QqQ-MS was used to determine the contents of 25 chemical components in SHQSWP, including neochlorogenic acid, isorhamnetin, chlorogenic acid, gallic acid, hydroxysafflor yellow-A, and crocin I. Each SHQSWP dose can reduce the rate of cerebral infarction in MCAO rats, improve neurobehavioral and pathological changes in the cortical area of brain tissues, increase the number of Nissl bodies in the cortical area, and reduce the rate of positive apoptotic cells in the cortical area. Protein chip prediction showed that SHQSWP may play a therapeutic role by regulating EPhA5, IL-1α, fractalkine, IL-10, IL-7, and IL-3 proteins. Molecular docking revealed that GRP78 may be the common dominant target of 15 components in SHQSWP, and Rutin may be the representative component with the strongest binding force with 7 key targets. SHQSWP can significantly increase the mRNA expression levels of PARP1 and XBP1 in the brain tissue of MCAO rats, significantly reduce the protein expression levels of CHOP, GRP78 and BAX, and increase the protein expression level of XBP1. A medium SHQSWP dose can reduce the fluorescence intensity of NLRP3, BAX, and CHOP in rat brain tissues and enhance the fluorescence intensity of XBP1. CONCLUSIONS: SHQSWP can inhibit endoplasmic reticulum stress-mediated apoptosis by regulating key proteins such as BAX, CHOP, GRP78, and XBP1, thus playing a neuroprotective role in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.

articles.title: RIC-specific cytoprotective profile mediated by microglia in a mouse model of acute ischaemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Background: Remote ischaemic conditioning (RIC) is an endogenous neuroprotective strategy involving repeated, transient occlusion of a limb artery to reduce ischaemic injury at a distant site. We investigated the effects of RIC in a mouse model of focal cerebral ischaemia induced by distal transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO). Animals were randomised into three groups: Stroke (tMCAO, 60 min), Stroke+remote ischaemic preconditioning (RIPerC) (RIC applied during ischaemia) and Stroke+remote ischaemic postconditioning (RIPostC) (RIC initiated 10 min after reperfusion). The RIC protocol consisted of three cycles of 5-minute hindlimb ischaemia followed by 5-minute reperfusion. Results: At 72 hours postischaemia, both RIPerC and RIPostC significantly reduced the infarct volumes in male and female mice. In males, infarct size decreased from 6.31 ± 0.28% (Stroke) to 3.77 ± 0.47% (RIPerC, p<0.0025) and 4.00 ± 0.40% (RIPostC, p<0.0061). However, the RIPerC+RIPostC group significantly increased the infarct volume compared with the Stroke group (8.41± 0.72%). In females, reductions were greater: from 6.69±0.46% (Stroke) to 2.95 ± 0.34% (RIPerC, p<0.0001) and 2.96 ± 0.32% (RIPostC, p<0.0001). Functional recovery was improved, particularly with RIPostC, correlating with infarct size reduction (Pearson’s r=0.5505 in males, r=0.7313 in females). Apoptosis was reduced by over 50% with both treatments, and microglial phagocytic activity (cluster of differentiation 68+/Iba1+ (ionised calcium binding adaptor molecule 1)) increased significantly. Microglial depletion using PLX3397 (71.3% reduction in Iba1+ cells) worsened ischaemic injury, yet RIC preserved its protective effects, suggesting additional microglia-independent mechanisms. Furthermore, RIC enhanced neurogenesis in the subventricular zone and infarct core (doublecortin marker+ cells doubled versus Stroke), with a marked proliferative response in female hippocampi (Ki67+ cells increased by 127%). Conclusion: These findings reveal sex-specific efficacy of RIC, with mechanistic insights obtained in male animals suggesting a dual mode of action via modulation of microglial function and promotion of endogenous neurorepair pathways.

articles.title: Beyond Blood-Brain Barrier Crossing in Reperfusion-Era Ischemic Stroke: Interface-Matched Active-Entity Delivery and Translational Product Design.
articles.abstract: Reperfusion therapy has transformed acute ischemic stroke care, yet large-vessel recanalization does not ensure capillary reperfusion, preservation of the blood-brain barrier and neurovascular unit (BBB/NVU), or durable neurological recovery. Nanomedicine is still commonly judged by BBB crossing or ischemic-hemisphere accumulation, although vascular access, tissue viability, transport phenotype, thromboinflammation, and standard treatment change rapidly during the lifetime of a formulation. This narrative review proposes a conceptual framework that matches the reperfusion state and pathological interface to the compartment in which the therapeutically active entity must act. The framework is intended to organize preclinical evidence and generate testable translational hypotheses; it has not yet been clinically validated. Persistent occlusion may favor intravascular targets, whereas recanalization with no-reflow creates a distinct microvascular delivery problem. Early reperfusion injury may prioritize BBB/NVU stabilization, while later biological contexts may require selective immune, regenerative, or organelle-directed interventions. These contexts may coexist spatially, vary across vascular territories, and shift during treatment; they should therefore not be interpreted as a mandatory chronological sequence. We distinguish BBB crossing, controlled barrier modulation, and BBB/NVU repair as separate therapeutic tasks, and introduce transport attrition as a practical explanation for why sequential targeting, transcytosis, cellular uptake, endosomal escape, and organelle localization can yield little final active-entity exposure despite strong tissue imaging. Recent predominantly preclinical examples illustrate how thrombus-targeted rtPA systems, neutrophil-intercepting particles, NET-degrading polymersomes, lesion-targeted nanoplatforms, and mitochondrial nanomedicines may fit different delivery topologies. Translational credibility requires topology-resolved exposure, target engagement in viable tissue, hemocompatibility under antithrombotic treatment, state-appropriate models, function-linked manufacturing controls, and compatibility with thrombolysis and thrombectomy.

articles.title: Mitochondrial cristae remodeling in ischemic stroke: mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial cristae arrange the respiratory machinery within the inner membrane and change as ischemia gives way to reperfusion. Their organization depends on mitochondrial contact site and cristae organizing system assemblies, optic atrophy 1, adenosine triphosphate synthase, and cardiolipin. Disruption of these systems can impair energy production, facilitate neuronal death, and expose mitochondrial DNA to inflammatory sensors. This review brings structural work together with experimental stroke studies to examine how crista remodeling contributes to injury and recovery. Genetic manipulation of selected regulators has preserved mitochondrial structure and reduced injury in neurons and microglia. Most of these interventions preceded ischemia, leaving the speed and feasibility of repair after stroke onset uncertain. Pharmacological modulation and mitochondrial delivery offer ways to address this gap, particularly around reperfusion. Emerging strategies combine modulation of crista protein assemblies with cardiolipin directed treatment, mitochondrial antioxidant nanomedicine, organelle delivery, and control of local drug exposure. Their therapeutic evaluation can be aligned with distinct opportunities at reperfusion and during subsequent tissue recovery. Progress toward treatment will require evidence that a candidate reaches the affected brain cells, modifies the intended membrane assembly, and produces lasting neurological benefit. The available studies place crista remodeling within neuroprotective pathways and identify the experimental steps needed to evaluate it as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Characterization and treatment of ischemic stroke in patients with infective endocarditis: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke is a common and serious complication of infective bacterial endocarditis. This study aimed to characterize the frequency, clinical and pathological features, treatment strategies, and outcomes of patients with stroke due to infective endocarditis. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed from database inception to October 2022 for studies reporting on stroke in patients with infective endocarditis and performed a meta-analysis. RESULTS: A total of 122 studies comprising 270,211 patients with infective endocarditis were included. Ischemic stroke occurred in 21% and hemorrhagic stroke in 5% of patients. Stroke was observed in 32% of patients with mitral valve endocarditis, 25% with aortic valve, and 11% with tricuspid valve endocarditis. Stroke was associated with significantly higher mortality (OR 2.35; 95%CI 1.74-3.16). Staphylococcus and Streptococcus species were most frequently associated with stroke (33% and 25%, respectively). The risk of stroke did not differ significantly between patients with and without pre-existing antithrombotic therapy (37% vs. 24%; OR 1.24, 95%CI 0.75-2.06). Successful reperfusion was achieved in 80% of patients undergoing mechanical thrombectomy, although mortality remained high at 49%. CONCLUSIONS: Stroke is a common complication of infective bacterial endocarditis and has a substantial impact on patient outcomes. It occurs most frequently in patients with mitral valve endocarditis and in those with infections caused by staphylococcal pathogens. Stroke risk was not reduced in patients with pre-existing antithrombotic therapy, supporting discontinuation where no other indication exists. Mechanical thrombectomy in patients with endocarditis-related large vessel occlusion achieves high recanalization rates; however, overall clinical outcomes remain poor in this population.

articles.title: Cavitation jet treatment-assisted glycosylation of hemp seed protein: Structural regulation and emulsion stability.
articles.abstract: 2 This study employed cavitation jet treatment to facilitate the effective glycosylation of hemp seed protein (HSP) with chitosan (CS). Initially, the treatment disrupted intra- and inter-molecular hydrogen bonds, inducing HSP structural unfolding. This critical conformational transition exposed internal reactive amino groups, enabling them to interact with CS carbonyl groups and achieving a maximum grafting degree of 34.54%. Consequently, the secondary structure of HSP was reorganized from an ordered state into a more relaxed, disordered configuration. The subsequent covalent attachment of hydrophilic CS chains effectively shielded exposed hydrophobic regions, significantly enhancing the complex's water affinity. Therefore, overall functional performances were markedly improved: solution properties were enhanced through increased solubility and decreased turbidity, while emulsion performance was optimized, evidenced by a superior EAI (55.89 m/g), an extended ESI (84.35 min), and improved apparent viscosity and viscoelasticity. This approach provides a practical strategy for the high-value utilization of hemp by-products.

articles.title: Exosomes in remote ischemic preconditioning-mediated organ protection: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.abstract: Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is an endogenous protective strategy that confers resistance against sustained ischemia-reperfusion injury in distant organs. RIPC induces protective responses through complex neuronal, humoral, and systemic signaling pathways. Increasing evidence suggests that exosomes may serve as important mediators of humoral inter-organ communication during RIPC. Exosomes are small extracellular vesicles released by donor cells that transport biologically active molecules, including lipids, proteins, messenger RNAs, and microRNAs, to recipient cells, thereby modulating cellular responses to injury. Emerging evidence indicates that RIPC-associated exosomes and their molecular cargo contribute to protection against ischemia-reperfusion injury in organs such as the heart, brain, kidney, and spinal cord. Several exosomal molecules, including miRNAs, HSP90, HIF-1α, and NOX2, have been implicated in the regulation of cellular pathways associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, mitochondrial function, and tissue survival. In particular, alterations in exosomal miRNAs and protein and metabolite profiles following RIPC suggest that exosomes may participate in the transmission of protective signals from remote ischemic tissues to target organs. The therapeutic potential of exosomes is further supported by their ability to transport multiple bioactive molecules and their potential application as biomarkers or delivery vehicles for therapeutic cargo. However, the specific exosomal components responsible for RIPC-mediated protection and their causal contribution to inter-organ signaling remain to be fully established. Therefore, the present review summarizes the emerging evidence on the role of exosomes in RIPC-mediated organ protection, with particular emphasis on cardiovascular and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, the molecular cargo involved, underlying protective mechanisms, and their potential therapeutic and translational applications.

RIPC induces protective responses through complex neuronal, humoral, and systemic signaling pathways. Increasing evidence suggests that exosomes may serve as important mediators of humoral inter-organ communication during RIPC.

articles.title: Neuroprotective effect by splenic hypothermia in ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether spleen-targeted remote administration of hypothermia (RAH) modulates splenic neutrophil release, attenuates neutrophil-driven cerebral inflammation, and preserves BBB integrity at early reperfusion after stroke. METHODS: Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent 2-h middle cerebral artery occlusion followed by 6-, 24- and 48- h of reperfusion. RAH was applied to the splenic region via surface cooling, with 1-min cycles administered at 5-min intervals. Neurological deficits, infarct volume, neutrophil infiltration, cytokine expression, BBB integrity, and apoptosis were assessed using neurobehavioral scoring, TTC staining, Western blotting, rt-PCR, immunofluorescence, ELISA, and TUNEL, respectively. RESULTS: 0 RAH rapidly reduced splenic temperature from 37to 28 °C without altering body or brain temperatures. At 6 h reperfusion, splenic neutrophil release was suppressed and brain neutrophil infiltration decreased. RAH reduced early elevations of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6. At 24 h, anti-inflammatory effects persisted and BBB integrity was preserved, restoring tight-junction and matrix proteins and suppressing BBB-damaging mediators. Compared to non-RAH stroked rats, RAH reduced apoptosis, body weight loss (9.1 ± 2.8 vs. 19.7 ± 7.2 g, p < 0.05), infarct volume (33.9 ± 4.1% vs. 53.6 ± 1.9%, p < 0.05), cerebral edema (11.2 ± 0.9% vs. 16.3 ± 1.3%, p < 0.05) and Evans blue extravasation (4.8 ± 0.2 vs. 9.8 ± 0.2 mg/g, p < 0.05), and improved neurological outcomes. RAH attenuated stroke-induced spleen weight loss and contraction, consistent with reduced splenic neutrophil mobilization. CONCLUSIONS: RAH induces neuroprotection after ischemic stroke by suppressing splenic neutrophil activation and mobilization, thus attenuating peripheral-to-central inflammatory trafficking and preserving BBB integrity. These findings highlight spleen-targeted cooling may represent a promising early intervention to ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Mechanisms of Spns2 in regulating neuroinflammatory activation of microglia after cerebral ischemia in rats.
articles.abstract: Microglia, the resident innate immune cells of the brain, maintain central nervous system homeostasis but can also mediate inflammatory injury after ischemic stroke. Following ischemia, microglia can adopt pro-inflammatory M1- or reparative M2-like state; thus, regulating the balance between these phenotypes may be therapeutically relevant. Sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling regulates immune responses, angiogenesis, and endothelial barrier integrity. Enhanced sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling in activated microglia after ischemic injury may amplify inflammatory cascades. However, strategies targeting sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling are constrained by the heterogeneous expression of sphingosine-1-phosphate receptors. Spinster homolog 2 (Spns2), a sphingosine-1-phosphate exporter, may provide an alternative target, although its role in ischemic stroke remains unclear. To investigate the role of Spns2 in post-ischemic neuroinflammation, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion was induced in Spns2-deficient (Spns2-/-) and wild-type rats. BV2 microglial cells exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation were used as an in vitro model. Spns2 mRNA expression in the peri-infarct penumbra increased after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion and peaked at 24 hours. Compared with wild-type rats, Spns2-/- rats showed lower neurological deficit scores, improved motor performance, and smaller infarct volumes. In the peri-infarct penumbra, Spns2 deficiency was associated with decreased expression of pro-inflammatory markers, increased expression of anti-inflammatory markers, and attenuated microglia-associated NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome signaling. In BV2 cells, Spns2 knockdown produced similar changes in inflammatory-marker expression and reduced oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-induced NLRP3 inflammasome-associated signaling and oxidative stress. Spns2 knockdown reduced extracellular sphingosine-1-phosphate levels in BV2-cell culture supernatants, whereas exogenous sphingosine-1-phosphate supplementation increased the expression of inflammasome-associated inflammatory mediators in Spns2-knockdown BV2 cells. RNA sequencing identified Itga5 upregulation in Spns2-/- rats and showed that differentially expressed genes between Spns2-/- and wild-type rats were enriched in the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (Akt) signaling pathway. Increased Akt phosphorylation in Spns2-/- rats was further confirmed by western blotting. These findings indicate that Spns2 deficiency limits sphingosine-1-phosphate export and attenuates microglia-associated neuroinflammation after ischemic stroke. Itga5 upregulation and increased Akt phosphorylation may be associated with this neuroprotective effect. Collectively, our results provide a basis for further investigation of the Spns2-sphingosine-1-phosphate axis in ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Oleanolic acid-hesperetin co-assembled nanoparticles alleviate neurological injury after ischemic stroke via the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β axis.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability, while the current clinically applicable adjunctive neuroprotective strategies face substantial limitations. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin exhibit synergistic antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic activities; however, their poor aqueous solubility and limited bioavailability remain major limitations to their therapeutic development. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin were formulated as co-assembled nanoparticles using an emulsion-solvent evaporation method. A 5:2 mass ratio of oleanolic acid to hesperetin produced primarily spherical nanoparticles with a mean hydrodynamic diameter of approximately 282.6 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.197, and a zeta potential of -12.2 mV. Oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticles displayed minimal hemolysis (0.199%) while maintaining a stable hydrodynamic diameter during 30 days of storage. Spectroscopic analyses and a 50 ns molecular dynamics simulation promoted co-assembly via multiple noncovalent-driven interactions. Oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticles effectively reduced oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion-induced viability loss and apoptosis in HT22 cells. In transient middle cerebral artery occlusion mice, Cy5.5-associated fluorescence was observed in brain tissue, whereas oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticle treatment reduced infarct volume and ipsilesional brain water content, preserved neurons, resulting in improved sensorimotor and spatial cognitive outcomes through day 28. Treatment promoted PI3K and AKT phosphorylation, elevated inhibitory phosphorylation of glycogen synthase kinase 3β at Ser9 and BCL-2 expression, and reduced BAX expression. These findings suggest that oleanolic acid-hesperetin co-assembly offers a promising preclinical formulation approach for multifactorial neuroprotection after ischemic stroke and supports further pharmacokinetic, safety, and pathway-causality studies.

articles.title: Development of a biomimetic manganese dioxide nanoreactor delivery system: Combination of biomimetic platelet/M2 microglia hybrid membrane with Astragaloside IV for the treatment of ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Conventional nanotherapeutics suffer from rapid immune clearance and insufficient accumulation in ischemic lesions. To overcome these bottlenecks, a stimuli-responsive biomimetic immunomodulatory delivery system was engineered by fusing platelet and M2 microglial membranes onto hollow mesoporous manganese dioxide nanoparticles loaded with the neuroprotective drug Astragaloside IV. The results show that this integrated nanoplatform fully leverages the synergistic properties of its biomimetic shell. Tracing the nanoparticles with the fluorescent dye Did revealed that the integrated nanoplatform exhibited more pronounced fluorescent enrichment in ischemic brain tissue; both in vivo and ex vivo imaging supported its specific homing ability. In a mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion, the platform significantly reduced the extent of cerebral infarction, alleviated neuronal damage caused by ischemia-reperfusion, and improved neurovascular integrity and neurological function. Furthermore, the platform mitigated oxidative stress in ischemic brain tissue, curtailed the inflammatory response, and facilitated a transition in microglial phenotype toward an anti-inflammatory and reparative state. Bioinformatics results indicate that this platform significantly alters gene expression profiles following cerebral ischemia-reperfusion. Differential expression and functional enrichment analyses further point to biological processes related to inflammation and immune regulation. These findings demonstrate that this biomimetic targeted nanoplatform integrates biomimetic targeting, reactive oxygen species scavenging, and immune modulation capabilities, thereby providing a new therapeutic platform technology for the precise delivery of therapeutic agents and the remodeling of the pathological microenvironment in ischemic stroke.

articles.title: β-Asarone Alleviates Post-stroke Neuroinflammation and Improves Mitochondrial Quality Via the BNIP3/BNIP3L-dependent Mitophagy Pathway.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, with mitophagy playing a central role in post-stroke neurological dysfunction. β-Asarone, a major bioactive component derived from the traditional herb Acorus tatarinowii, possesses antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties. However, whether β-asarone ameliorates IS by regulating mitophagy and its underlying mechanisms remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether β-asarone exerts neuroprotective effects against IS by modulating BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy. A middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) rat model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) cell model were established. Neuroprotective effects were evaluated using neurological behavioral scores, 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining, hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining, and Nissl staining. Mitochondrial function was assessed by measuring reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP). Mitophagy was observed via transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and fluorescence microscopy. Western blot (WB) analysis was performed to detect BNIP3/BNIP3L pathway proteins. Results showed that β-asarone enhanced mitophagy, improved mitochondrial function, and alleviated post-stroke neuroinflammation. Conversely, the autophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA) impaired mitophagic function, exacerbating ischemia-induced brain injury and inflammation, while β-asarone treatment reversed these detrimental effects. In summary, β-asarone mitigates neuroinflammation and neuronal injury after IS, at least partly through promoting BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy, highlighting this pathway as a promising therapeutic target for IS.

However, whether β-asarone ameliorates IS by regulating mitophagy and its underlying mechanisms remains unclear.

articles.title: Continuous Near-Infrared Spectroscopy as a Real-Time Monitor of Intravenous Thrombolysis in Acute Ischaemic Stroke: A Prospective Observational Emergency Department Study.
articles.abstract: Background. Methods. Results. Conclusions. 2 2 2 2 2 p p p p Intravenous (IV) thrombolysis is the standard of care for acute ischaemic stroke (AIS), yet there is still no objective bedside tool for monitoring the brain continuously during the infusion. Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) provides non-invasive, continuous measurement of regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rSO). We evaluated whether bilateral frontal NIRS, and in particular the absolute interhemispheric difference in rSO(ΔNIRS), tracks the clinical trajectory of patients receiving IV alteplase in the emergency department (ED).A prospective observational cohort study was conducted in the ED of a tertiary university hospital. Consecutive adults receiving IV alteplase for AIS were screened, and those enrolled underwent continuous bilateral frontal NIRS monitoring. Bilateral rSO, ΔNIRS, vital signs, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) were recorded at baseline and at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60 and 120 min after the start of the infusion. Patients were classified by clinical trajectory during monitoring as improvement, no change, or deterioration.Forty-one patients were analyzed (26 female, 63.4%; mean age 73.6 ± 14.8 years); 15 (36.6%) improved, 21 (51.2%) showed no change and 5 (12.2%) deteriorated. In the whole cohort, absolute rSOrose only slightly in the affected hemisphere and did not change in the unaffected hemisphere. However, affected-hemisphere rSOrose significantly in the improvement group (median 59 to 67;= 0.001) and fell significantly in the deterioration group (= 0.015). ΔNIRS narrowed from a median of 4 (IQR 3-9) at baseline to 1 (IQR 0-5) at 120 min in the improvement group (= 0.034) and did not change significantly in the other groups. The two patients with acute complications desaturated bilaterally. NIHSS correlated strongly and inversely with GCS at every time point (ρ = -0.74 to -0.84; all< 0.001).During IV thrombolysis in the ED, continuous bilateral frontal NIRS tracked the clinical trajectory. Because recanalisation and reperfusion were not assessed independently, what NIRS paralleled was the clinical course, not reperfusion itself. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant larger studies that validate ΔNIRS against perfusion or vascular imaging.

articles.title: Gut microbiota as a potential mediator of the disease-ameliorating effects of molecular hydrogen: mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.abstract: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 Molecular hydrogen (H) has emerged as a promising bioactive gas with well-documented antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective properties, and its therapeutic potential for a range of human diseases has been increasingly recognized. Accumulating evidence suggests that the gut microbiota (GM) may contribute to some of the biological effects of H. The GM serves as both a key site for endogenous Hproduction and consumption, and a potential site of interaction with exogenous Hsupplementation, with possible implications for intestinal microecological homeostasis. This narrative review critically summarizes current evidence on the bidirectional relationship between Hand the GM, focusing on microbial Hproduction and consumption, the potential role of Hin maintaining gut microbial homeostasis, and the impact of exogenous Hsupplementation on intestinal microecology. The potential therapeutic relevance of H-associated GM modulation is further discussed in metabolic diseases, gastrointestinal disorders, and neurodegenerative diseases. Proposed mechanisms include regulation of microbial composition, reinforcement of intestinal barrier integrity, suppression of inflammation and oxidative stress, modulation of microbial metabolites, and gut-organ axis signaling. Collectively, current evidence supports that Hmay influence the GM ecosystem. However, most supporting data remains preclinical, and whether GM alterations causally mediate the biological or therapeutic effects of Hremains to be established. Elucidating the reciprocal interaction between Hand the GM may provide new mechanistic insight into H-based interventions and facilitate the development of microbiota-targeted therapeutic strategies for human diseases.

articles.title: Essential oil from Angelica sinensis Radix attenuates ischemic stroke via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK pathway: insights from network pharmacology and molecular mechanism evaluation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: As a traditional herbal remedy, the root of Angelica sinensis has long been used to treat headaches, strokes, and dementia. As the primary active ingredient in A. sinensis, A. sinensis essential oil (ASEO) also plays a significant role in the therapy of stroke. Although ASEO has shown clear therapeutic effects, its specific mechanism of preventing ischemic stroke still needs to be further clarified. AIM OF THE STUDY: Through network pharmacological analysis combined with in vitro and in vivo experimental verification, this study investigated the protective effects of ASEO against stroke and elucidated the underlying molecular regulatory mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) was used to analyze the chemical composition of ASEO. Middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) rats were administered different doses of ASEO to evaluate its therapeutic effects. The therapeutic effects were evaluated using behavioral, histopathological, and immunofluorescence assays. In addition, using network pharmacology techniques, the potential molecular mechanisms underlying the treatment of ischemic stroke with ASEO have been preliminarily elucidated. HT22 cells treated with oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) were used as an in vitro model. Subsequently, the key signal transduction pathways involved in the therapeutic effects of ASEO against ischemic stroke were further validated using multiple experimental approaches, including enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), flow cytometry, Western blotting, pathway-specific pharmacological inhibition and PKG-specific siRNA knockdown. RESULTS: Twenty-seven compounds were identified from ASEO by GC-MS. In vivo experiments demonstrated that ASEO treatment exerted significant protective effects on MCAO/R rats by improving impaired neurological function, reducing cerebral infarct volume, alleviating neuronal apoptosis, and modulating the expression of apoptotic proteins. Mechanistically, network pharmacology studies suggested that the protective mechanism of ASEO may involve the cGMP/PKG and MAPK signaling pathways. Subsequent experiments confirmed that ASEO inhibited neuronal apoptosis via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK axis both in vivo and in vitro. Importantly, both pharmacological inhibition and siRNA-mediated genetic knockdown of PKG significantly attenuated the protective effects of ASEO against OGD/R injury in HT22 cells. CONCLUSION: ASEO exerts its anti-ischemic stroke effect by attenuating apoptosis via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK signaling pathway, providing a scientific foundation for its clinical application in ischemic stroke therapy.

articles.title: Pharmacological basis of Suhexiang Wan in ischemic stroke: identification and functional characterization of piperlongumine as a brain-distributed bioactive constituent associated with STAT3-mediated blood-brain barrier protection.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Suhexiang Wan (SHXW) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula that has been traditionally used for stroke-related disorders, including sudden loss of consciousness, neurological dysfunction, and hemiplegia. Although modern pharmacological studies have suggested its neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory properties, the brain-distributed constituents potentially associated with its therapeutic effects in ischemic stroke (IS) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to elucidate the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by identifying brain-distributed constituents and investigating a candidate constituent potentially associated with its protective effects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI), with particular emphasis on blood-brain barrier (BBB) protection. MATERIALS AND METHODS: SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue under middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) conditions were characterized using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Integrated network pharmacology analysis was performed to predict potential therapeutic targets and signaling pathways. Piperlongumine (PIP) was further confirmed and quantified in SHXW and brain tissue using an authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS approach. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, biophysical binding assays, and cellular target-engagement experiments were used to investigate the interaction between PIP and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3). The protective effects and associated mechanisms were evaluated in a mouse MCAO/R model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-induced brain microvascular endothelial cell injury model. RESULTS: Among 1991 putatively annotated constituents of SHXW, 55 SHXW-derived constituents were detected in brain tissue under MCAO/R conditions. In the MCAO/R mouse model, SHXW significantly improved neurological deficits, reduced infarct volume and brain edema, decreased BBB permeability, and restored tight junction protein expression. Among the brain-detected constituents, PIP, a natural alkaloid derived from Piper longum L., was selected for further investigation based on its detection in brain tissue, network topology characteristics, predicted association with STAT3, and reported pharmacological relevance to ischemic injury. Authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS confirmed PIP in SHXW and brain tissue, with a PIP content of 48.21 ± 1.10 μg/g in SHXW and a brain concentration of 159.67 ± 8.37 ng/g at 2 h after SHXW administration. Biophysical and cellular target-engagement assays supported the interaction between PIP and STAT3. PIP partially recapitulated the protective effects of SHXW by alleviating neurological deficits, preserving BBB integrity, restoring endothelial barrier function, and suppressing STAT3-associated inflammatory responses. STAT3 knockdown partially phenocopied the endothelial protective effects of PIP, whereas restoration of STAT3 expression in STAT3-knockdown cells reversed the protective phenotype. PIP treatment attenuated the injury-associated changes following STAT3 restoration, supporting the functional involvement of STAT3-associated signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides new insights into the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by integrating chemical profiling, brain distribution analysis, and pharmacological validation. SHXW exerted protective effects against CIRI and preserved BBB integrity. Among the SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue, PIP was identified and functionally characterized as a bioactive candidate associated with BBB protection. The findings support the involvement of PIP-STAT3 interaction and STAT3-associated inflammatory signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection. These results provide pharmacological evidence linking the traditional application of SHXW with its modern molecular mechanisms while highlighting brain-distribution-guided approaches for investigating the therapeutic basis of complex TCM formulas.

articles.title: Brain cytoprotection in acute ischemic stroke in the reperfusion era: neuroimmune networks, clinical evidence, and translational barriers.
articles.abstract: Intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy have transformed acute ischemic stroke (AIS) care, yet angiographic recanalization does not guarantee adequate tissue reperfusion or long-term functional independence. Brain cytoprotection has therefore expanded from neuron-centered rescue to preservation of the ischemic penumbra, neurovascular unit, blood-brain barrier (BBB), and microcirculation. Using a systems-immunology perspective, this clinically oriented narrative review examines ischemia-reperfusion injury as a dynamic network linking danger-associated molecular pattern sensing, microglia and astrocytes, circulating leukocytes, platelets and complement, endothelium and pericytes, cytokine signaling, edema, no-reflow, and regulated cell-death programs. We integrate classic and recent evidence for excitotoxic, redox and mitochondrial, inflammatory, barrier, microvascular, and cell-death targets; evaluate representative pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic interventions; and distinguish negative primary endpoints from exploratory subgroup or surrogate signals. Confirmatory excitotoxicity trials have remained negative overall. Selected multitarget agents have shown benefit in specific Chinese populations, whereas immune-, edema-, and no-reflow-directed approaches have yielded stage-specific but inconsistent safety, imaging, and functional results. Statins, nitric oxide donors, and phosphodiesterase inhibition have plausible vascular or immunomodulatory actions, but available trials do not establish them as acute cytoprotective therapies. Future development should align the right mechanism, tissue phenotype, treatment time, exposure, target-engagement measure, and patient-centered endpoint, followed by multicenter preclinical testing and independent cross-regional clinical replication. This end-to-end framework reframes brain cytoprotection as precision modulation of a spatially and temporally evolving neuroimmune-vascular system rather than a single undifferentiated treatment class.

articles.title: Diabetes-Associated Fibrin Enrichment in Cerebral Thrombi and Its Procedural Implications for Mechanical Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p Diabetes is associated with altered fibrin biology, but its relationship with fibrin content in cerebral thrombi and the procedural relevance of this relationship during mechanical thrombectomy remain unclear. We investigated the association between diabetes and fibrin content in thrombectomy-retrieved cerebral thrombi and whether diabetes-associated differences in fibrin content mediated procedural outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy.We retrospectively analyzed patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had retrieved thrombi available for histological analysis. Red blood cell, platelet, and fibrin contents were quantified immunohistochemically. The association between diabetes and fibrin content was evaluated using multivariable linear regression, with complementary sensitivity analyses based on intravenous tissue-type plasminogen activator administration and atrial fibrillation status. Mediation analyses were performed to estimate the indirect effects of diabetes on procedural outcomes through diabetes-associated changes in fibrin content.Among 312 patients, 98 (31.4%) had diabetes. Patients with diabetes had greater fibrin content than those without diabetes (median, 37.0% [interquartile range, 26.4-52.9] vs. 30.9% [17.7-45.0];= 0.004), whereas red blood cell and platelet contents did not differ significantly between the groups. Diabetes remained associated with greater fibrin content in the primary adjusted analysis (β = +6.68 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.19-11.18;= 0.004), and the association persisted after additional conditioning on initial glucose and in sensitivity analyses. Among patients with diabetes, neither HbA1c nor initial glucose was associated with fibrin content. Mediation analyses did not identify a detectable indirect effect of diabetes through fibrin content on successful reperfusion, complete reperfusion, first-pass effect, number of passes, or the requirement for ≥3 passes.Diabetes was independently associated with greater fibrin content in cerebral thrombi retrieved during mechanical thrombectomy, supporting the presence of a diabetes-associated fibrin-enriched thrombus phenotype. However, no detectable indirect effect of diabetes-associated differences in fibrin content on the examined procedural outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy was identified. These findings suggest that although diabetes is associated with a distinct quantitative change in cerebral thrombus composition, a corresponding procedural consequence was not detectable in the present study.

articles.title: Microglial Ring1 enhances post-phagocytic myelin debris processing: Attenuation of cognitive dysfunction after hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion induces myelin injury, resulting in cognitive impairment. Efficient clearance of myelin debris is important for neural repair. The E3 ubiquitin ligase Ring1 (RING finger protein 1) participates in ubiquitin signaling and gene expression regulation, However, whether Ring1 ameliorates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury-induced cognitive impairment by promoting microglial post-phagocytic myelin debris processing remains unknown. In this study, we employed a hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion model, a hippocampal myelin debris injection model, and an in vitro microglia-myelin debris co-culture model to simulate cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, and combined these models with proteomic and transcriptomic analyses and Ring1 gain- and loss-of-function approaches. Hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion induced hippocampal myelin injury and cognitive dysfunction, while hippocampal administration of myelin debris further impaired cognition. Transcriptomic analysis identified Ring1 as a candidate regulator associated with postphagocytic myelin debris processing. Ring1 overexpression alleviated cognitive deficits and hippocampal myelin injury and restored mitochondrial DNA-encoded gene expression and adenosine triphosphate levels after hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion. In contrast, Ring1 knockdown in the microglia-myelin debris co-culture model reduced mitochondrial DNAencoded gene expression and adenosine triphosphate levels and delayed post-phagocytic myelin debris processing. Mechanistically, Ring1 interacted with mitochondrial transcription factor B2, with K27-linked ubiquitin signals detected in Ring1- and mitochondrial transcription factor B2-containing immunocomplexes. Ring1 depletion reduced mitochondrial transcription factor B2-associated K27-linked ubiquitin signaling, mitochondrial DNA-encoded gene expression, adenosine triphosphate levels, and post-phagocytic myelin debris processing. Collectively, our findings suggest that Ring1 attenuates hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion-related cognitive impairment by promoting microglial post-phagocytic myelin debris processing through mitochondrial transcription factor B2-associated K27-linked ubiquitin signaling and mitochondrial regulation.

articles.title: Therapeutic potential analysis of Sertoli cell-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury is a core pathological process underlying further neurological deterioration after reperfusion therapy for acute ischemic stroke. Developing more effective neuroprotective agents is therefore a current priority in neuroscience research. Sertoli cells possess unique immunoprivileged and nutritional support functions within the testes and secrete exosomes that serve as important mediators of intercellular communication, with substantial potential for neuroprotection. This review addresses the protective mechanisms of Sertoli cell-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Through a comprehensive literature review, we systematically summarize their neuroprotective effects, including the modulation of immune and inflammatory responses, inhibition of cellular apoptosis, promotion of neurovascular repair, regulation of autophagy, and influence on epigenetic modifications and related signaling pathways. By synthesizing the latest findings in this field, we aim to provide insights into the development and translation of novel neuroprotective strategies based on Sertoli cell-derived exosomes.

articles.title: Persistent Hypoperfusion on Post-Recanalization Digital Subtraction Angiography Perfusion Maps in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite high recanalization rates with endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion stroke, a large proportion of patients remain disabled. This study aims to investigate the clinical impact of persistent hypoperfusion that was detected immediately after recanalization. METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with large vessel occlusion with near-complete or complete recanalization, perfusion maps were generated from post-recanalization digital subtraction angiography. Focal hypoperfusion within the ischemic territory was detected and categorized as regional or cortical according to spatial distribution. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2). The associations of no-reflow and outcomes were examined by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: P P P P P P P Among 375 patients (median age 69 [interquartile range 57-77] years; 67.5% men), persistent hypoperfusion was detected in 29.6% of patients. Patients with hypoperfusion had higher baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (median 14 versus 12,=0.076) and more thrombectomy passes (=0.021). The presence of persistent hypoperfusion was strongly associated with reduced functional independence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=0.23, 95% CI 0.13-0.39,<0.001), higher rates of hemorrhagic transformation (aOR=1.88, 95% CI 1.14-3.11;=0.013) and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (aOR=2.95, 95% CI 1.20-7.23;=0.018). Quantitative analysis revealed minimum regional cerebral blood flow as a key factor of functional outcome (aOR=1.67, 95% CI 1.07-2.60;=0.023). There is no significant agreement with 24-hour computed tomography perfusion-defined hypoperfusion (κ=0.106,=0.524). CONCLUSIONS: Persistent hypoperfusion could be detected immediately post-recanalization in one-third of successfully treated large vessel occlusion strokes. The adverse impact to functional outcome highlights its potential as an intraprocedural biomarker for future adjunctive therapies.

articles.title: USP11 Drives Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Via Promoting Ferroptosis by Deubiquitinating and Stabilizing ASK1.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) represents a pivotal pathological mechanism underlying ischemic cerebrovascular disorders including cerebral stroke. Currently, there are lack of effective preventive or therapeutic methods. Ubiquitin-specific protease 11 (USP11) is a member of the most prevalent ubiquitination-specific protease (USP) family. It has been shown that USP11 plays diverse and significant roles in a variety of diseases, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, prostate cancer, and intervertebral disc degeneration. However, its precise function and molecular mechanisms involvement in CIRI remain unknown. METHODS: USP11 knockout (USP11-KO) and adeno-associated virus 9-mediated USP11 over-expression (USP11-OE) mice were established as a mouse model of CIRI, and USP11 knockdown and overexpression adenovirus were used to establish a cell model, to investigate the effect of USP11 on CIRI in vivo and in vitro. Molecular biological studies were used to clarify the mechanism of USP11 mediated ferroptosis during CIRI. RESULTS: The expression of USP11 is increased during CIRI. Functionally, USP11 deficiency attenuated neurological deficits, cerebral infarction, neuroinflammation, and ferroptosis during CIRI, whereas specific overexpression of USP11 exacerbated these pathological processes. Furthermore, USP11 knockdown inhibited neuronal injury, inflammatory response and ferroptosis, while USP11 overexpression promoted these processes. Mechanistically, USP11 bind to ASK1 and inhibit its K48-linked ubiquitination, thereby enhancing the activity of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling pathway. More importantly, the regulation of USP11 on neuronal ferroptosis and CIRI relied on its regulation of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling axis. CONCLUSIONS: Our study clarified the new functions and mechanisms of USP11 during CIRI. Targeting USP11-ASK1-JNK/p38-ferroptosis may be a new promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of CIRI.

articles.title: The inhibitory effect of gadolinium-conjugated diflunisal on platelet function through regulating outside-in signaling of αIIbβ3 integrin.
articles.abstract: 2 2 3 2+ In vivo The gadolinium-conjugated diflunisal derivative ETN102 has previously been shown to suppress cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) levels, reduce glial activation, and attenuate neuronal damage associated with stroke. In the present study, we investigated whether ETN102 modulates platelet aggregation and activation. ETN102 selectively inhibited thrombin-induced platelet aggregation while sparing platelet responses to other agonists, including collagen, adenosine diphosphate (ADP), and U46619. ETN102 also reduced adenosine triphosphate (ATP) secretion under aggregating conditions without altering thromboxane B(TXB) generation, suggesting that its antiplatelet effect is independent of the COX-1-dependent thromboxane signaling. Flow cytometric and biochemical analyses further demonstrated that ETN102 suppressed thrombin-induced αIIbβ3 integrin activation, platelet spreading, clot retraction, and the phosphorylation of focal adhesion kinase (FAK) and proline-rich tyrosine kinase 2 (Pyk2), without affecting granule secretion, intracellular Camobilization, or phosphorylation of Syk, PI3K, and AKT signaling molecules., ETN102 significantly prolonged carotid artery occlusion time in a ferric chloride (FeCl)-induced thrombosis model and increased tail bleeding time and hemoglobin content. In addition, ETN102 reduced infarct volume and improved neuronal survival markers in a murine model of cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury. These findings demonstrate that ETN102 is a thrombin-context selective modulator of platelet integrin αIIbβ3 outside-in signaling, with antithrombotic and neuroprotective potential.
