articles.title: Novel acylation modifications in cerebrovascular disease: Molecular mechanisms, crosstalk and therapeutic potential.
articles.abstract: Secondary injury in cerebrovascular disease involves energy failure, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Novel lysine acylations, including lactylation, succinylation, beta-hydroxybutyrylation and crotonylation, have emerged as interfaces through which metabolic changes in lactate, succinate, ketone bodies and short-chain acyl-CoA species are translated into transcriptional regulation and altered protein function. This review organizes the evidence according to a framework that links metabolic donors, writer and eraser enzymes, modification sites, cell types and disease stages. We distinguish relatively developed experimental evidence in acute ischemic stroke and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury from limited findings in haemorrhage and predominantly exploratory evidence in chronic hypoperfusion and vascular cognitive impairment. Proteomic studies have identified 1003 lactylation sites across 469 proteins in rats subjected to cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, although most sites have not undergone causal validation. Comparatively strong evidence has accumulated for sites or regulatory axes involving MeCP2, SOD2, NEK7, ACSL4, PLBD1 and ZO-1. Collectively, current findings indicate that the effects of a given acylation cannot be inferred from its global abundance because they depend on substrate function, cellular origin and the therapeutic window. Major limitations include insufficient site-specific causal evidence, difficulty in directly quantifying crosstalk among post-translational modifications, poor correspondence between animal models and clinical heterogeneity and the absence of effective delivery systems and pharmacodynamic biomarkers. Future studies should integrate spatiotemporally resolved multi-omics, endogenous site editing, cell-specific models, measurable target engagement and independent clinical cohorts to evaluate whether selected acylation sites can progress from experimental candidates to independently validated clinical markers or intervention targets.

articles.title: Electroacupuncture Ameliorating Cerebral I/R-Induced Inflammatory Response through the TLR/TRAF6/NF-κB Pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The inflammatory response plays a crucial role in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and may offer a new therapeutic approach for stroke. Electroacupuncture has shown potential in treating cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury. METHODOLOGY: Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to four groups: the sham group, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) group, sham electroacupuncture (SEA) group, and electroacupuncture (EA) group. The SEA and EA groups received 30 min of treatment after 60 min of ischemia. Body weight was measured before and 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Neurological function and infarct volume were assessed 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Protein and messenger RNA (mRNA) expression levels of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB were evaluated using western blot and reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). The mRNA and protein expression of inflammatory markers was assessed using RT-PCR and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). RESULTS: Compared with the MCAO/R group, the EA group exhibited improved neurological function, reduced infarct volume, and down-regulated expression of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB. Additionally, in the EA group, the mRNA and protein expression of proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β) were decreased, while the expression of the anti-inflammatory cytokine (IL-10) was increased. CONCLUSIONS: Electroacupuncture exerts a neuroprotective effect on MCAO/R, potentially through the modulation of the TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB pathways. This treatment may reduce the cerebral I/R-induced inflammatory response by influencing the TLR/TRAF/NF-κB signaling pathway.

articles.title: Neutrophil to Lymphocyte Ratio and Neurological Outcome in Ischemic Stroke at 4.5 to 24 Hours: A Post Hoc Analysis of TRACE-III Trial.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Whether neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR), as a marker of increased inflammatory response, modifies the efficacy and safety of tenecteplase is uncertain in patients 4.5-24 h after stroke onset. We investigated this in the Tenecteplase Reperfusion Therapy in Acute Ischemic Cerebrovascular Events-III (TRACE-III) trial. METHODS: TRACE-III was a phase 3, multicenter, prospective, open-label, randomized, blinded-endpoint trial that enrolled 516 patients from 58 centers in China between January 2022 and November 2023. Patients had anterior large vessel occlusion and evidence of salvageable brain tissue on perfusion imaging, presented 4.5-24 h after symptom onset, and were randomized 1:1 to intravenous tenecteplase (intervention) or standard medical treatment (control). The primary efficacy and safety outcomes were modified Rankin scale score of 0-1 at 90 days and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or death, respectively. This post hoc analysis in 513 patients with complete admission NLR data compared outcomes in patients with elevated NLR (> first quartile) and non-elevated NLR (≤ first quartile). RESULTS: In the elevated NLR group (> 3.0), tenecteplase was associated with increased functional independence (61 [30.2%] vs. 36 [19.6%]; adjusted relative rate [aRR] 1.51; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05-2.17; P = 0.03) compared to standard medical treatment. This benefit was not observed in the non-elevated NLR group (26 [41.9%] vs. 25 [38.5%]; aRR 1.12; 95% CI 0.73-1.73). Safety outcomes did not differ in either the elevated or non-elevated NLR groups. CONCLUSION: Baseline NLR may provide a potential signal for differential treatment response to intravenous tenecteplase in patients with acute ischemic stroke, although these exploratory findings require further validation in independent studies. TRIAL REGISTRATION: TRACE-III is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05141305.

articles.title: Tenecteplase, alteplase, and endovascular thrombectomy in extended-window acute ischemic stroke with intracranial large-vessel occlusion: a Bayesian network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The comparative effects of intravenous thrombolytic agents, endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), and bridging therapy in imaging-selected patients with acute ischemic stroke treated beyond 4.5 hours remain uncertain. We compared these strategies while distinguishing confirmed large-vessel occlusion (LVO) evidence from broader mixed populations. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for randomized trials evaluating reperfusion treatments administered 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset or last known well. The primary network included trials requiring confirmed intracranial LVO or basilar artery occlusion (BAO). An anterior-circulation LVO network and an all-available network were examined as sensitivity and exploratory analyses. Bayesian random-effects consistency models estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). The primary outcome was functional independence, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 at 90 days. RESULTS: Fifteen randomized trials were included, of which 8 contributed to the primary confirmed LVO/BAO network. Compared with placebo or best medical care, EVT significantly improved functional independence (OR, 2.93 [95% CrI, 1.40-6.53]) and excellent functional outcome, defined as mRS 0 to 1 (OR, 2.22 [95% CrI, 1.30-4.11]), reduced 90-day mortality (OR, 0.71 [95% CrI, 0.50-0.98]), and increased trial-defined recanalization or reperfusion at approximately 24 hours (OR, 5.27 [95% CrI, 1.83-16.04]); sICH was also increased (OR, 2.65 [95% CrI, 1.28-5.81]). Compared with EVT, tenecteplase plus EVT showed numerically favorable but statistically inconclusive estimates for functional independence (OR, 1.10 [95% CrI, 0.34-3.52]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.16 [95% CrI, 0.52-2.64]). Direct pairwise analyses of 2 trials were similarly inconclusive. Tenecteplase alone did not show clear differences from placebo or best medical care. Findings were directionally consistent in the anterior-circulation sensitivity and all-available exploratory networks. CONCLUSIONS: Among imaging-selected patients with confirmed intracranial LVO or BAO treated 4.5 to 24 hours after onset or last known well, EVT had the most consistent evidence of benefit versus placebo or best medical care. Tenecteplase plus EVT showed favorable but imprecise estimates, and neither network nor direct pairwise analyses established superiority over EVT alone. The incremental benefit of bridging tenecteplase remains uncertain.

articles.title: Sex dimorphism in vascular trajectories after living-donor kidney transplantation: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular risk remains high after kidney transplantation, reflecting pre-transplant early vascular aging. Arterial stiffness generally improves, but the trajectory of microvascular endothelial function, and its dependence on recipient's biological sex and donor matching, is unclear. METHODS: In 71 living-donor kidney transplant recipients, microvascular endothelial function (reactive hyperemia index, lnRHI) and arterial stiffness [augmentation index at 75 bpm (AI@75)] were measured before transplantation and at a median of 24.6 months. Forty-six of their donors were assessed identically before donation, providing a healthy reference of the same sex. Resistance arteries from 37 recipients and 46 living donors underwent wire myography. RESULTS: P P β P P P Ex vivo P P P AI@75 improved overall (-5.7%; = .003), whereas microvascular function declined in men but not women (male ΔlnRHI -0.149, = .002; sex × time interaction= -0.19, = .026), stable in direction across 11 specifications including tacrolimus exposure and graft function. The greater AI@75 improvement with sex-matched transplantation ( = .020) did not survive adjustment for baseline stiffness ( = .32)., endothelial relaxation showed no detectable sex difference in recipients ( = .83) or donors ( = .94), whereas passive stiffness was higher in female recipients ( = .048). CONCLUSIONS: After living-donor kidney transplantation, arterial stiffness improved in both sexes, while microvascular endothelial function declined in men and not in women. Referenced to healthy donors of the same sex, arterial stiffness in men remained abnormal at follow-up. Sex-matched transplantation conferred no independent vascular benefit. These findings are exploratory and require confirmation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Endohepatology in the Management of Portal Hypertension in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Portal hypertension is the principal driver of decompensation in advanced chronic liver disease, yet in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) it deviates from the classical sinusoidal paradigm. Growing evidence points to a mixed sinusoidal-presinusoidal phenotype in which the hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) may underestimate true portal pressure, and in which decompensation and varices can occur at lower HVPG values than in viral cirrhosis. This biology is compounded by a diagnostic gap: non-invasive tests such as liver stiffness by vibration-controlled transient elastography, FIB-4, ANTICIPATE-NASH, spleen stiffness and the NICER model, are degraded by obesity through technical limitations and altered diagnostic thresholds, even when test discrimination is preserved. Moreover, no non-invasive rule-in for clinically significant portal hypertension reaches a 90% positive predictive value in obese MASLD, leaving a clinically meaningful grey zone. Endohepatology addresses these diagnostic limitations by providing complementary hemodynamic, elastographic, and histological information. Within a single sedated session, EUS-guided shear-wave elastography and EUS-guided liver biopsy can adjudicate F2-F3 fibrosis when treatment eligibility is uncertain; EUS-guided portal pressure gradient measurement can provide a direct gradient when HVPG or non-invasive tests are discordant with the clinical phenotype; and EUS-based vascular assessment can characterize collateral and variceal anatomy. The same platform extends to therapy, including EUS-guided gastric variceal obliteration and pre-bariatric risk stratification. Current evidence is largely early-phase and requires prospective validation. Rather than replacing established tools, endohepatology offers an integrated pathway tailored to the diagnostic and therapeutic problems most characteristic of MASLD.

articles.title: Uncovering the transcriptional hallmarks of endothelial cell aging via integrated single-cell analysis.
articles.abstract: Endothelial cells (ECs) are critical regulators of vascular function and exhibit tissue-specialized roles. During aging, these cells become dysfunctional, resulting in increased susceptibility to cardiovascular disease. Although single-cell transcriptomics has revealed extensive endothelial heterogeneity, a comprehensive atlas of human EC transcriptomes over the course of the adult human lifespan has been lacking. Here, we present the Human Aging Endothelial Cell Atlas (HAECA), a harmonized single-cell transcriptomic compendium of over 375,000 ECs from 12 human tissues throughout adulthood. We identified age-associated transcriptional shifts, including a decline in angiogenic gene expression in venous ECs and widespread alterations in extracellular matrix and mechanotransduction-associated signatures. Furthermore, we uncovered a p21-linked transcriptional program in ECs, which we linked to cellular senescence in both in vitro and in vivo models. Together, our study provides a high-resolution transcriptomic reference of the human endothelium across tissues and age.

articles.title: Magnetoactive Hydrogels to Probe Curvature-Directed Endothelial Cell Mechanosensing.
articles.abstract: The vascular system exhibits complex, nonplanar geometries that become further distorted during pathological remodeling, including arterial tortuosity and aneurysms. Although hemodynamic shear stress is a well-established regulator of vascular function, the direct effects of curvature as an intrinsic geometric cue remain poorly defined. This is largely because existing in vitro models are static and fail to capture the dynamic changes that accompany disease progression. To address this gap, we used a magnetoactive hydrogel platform that enables real-time, on-demand curvature of endothelial monolayers to reproduce clinically established tortuosity metrics. Using this system, we found that elevated curvature increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP), with the strongest response in convex relative to concave regions of highly tortuous endothelial monolayers. This mechanosensitive response was accompanied by reduced VE-Cadherin junctional thickness and increased membrane localization of endothelial nitric oxide synthase. These findings identify local curvature, independent of shear stress, as a regulator of endothelial cell mechanosensing and function, and establish a dynamic hydrogel platform for isolating geometric regulation from shear stress inputs in vascular mechanobiology.

articles.title: Transcription factor EB as a novel target for dimethyl fumarate to restore endothelial function in diabetes.
articles.abstract: + -1 -1 ECKO ECKO Diabetes mellitus-associated endothelial dysfunction represents a pivotal early event in diabetic vasculopathy, linking metabolic derangements to vascular injury. Dimethyl fumarate (DMF), an FDA-approved drug for multiple sclerosis and psoriasis, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, yet whether it protects against diabetic endothelial dysfunction and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, diabetic db/db mice and the non-diabetic db/mlittermates were treated with DMF (100 mg·kg·d) or vehicle for 4 weeks, and vascular function in aortic and mesenteric artery rings was assessed by wire myography. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and endothelial cell (EC)-specific Tfeb knockout (Tfeb) mice were employed to investigate the target of DMF in vitro and in vivo. DMF restored the impaired endothelium-dependent relaxations (EDRs) in db/db mouse aortas and insulin-induced relaxations in mesenteric arteries, improved glucose tolerance, reduced aortic endothelial mitochondrial ROS (mito-ROS) accumulation, and lowered the expression of inflammatory markers. IL-1β induced phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention of TFEB (indicative of TFEB inhibition), mito-ROS production, and inflammatory responses in HUVECs and mouse aortas, all of which were reversed by DMF pretreatment. These protective effects of DMF were largely reversed by TFEB knockdown in HUVECs or in aortas of Tfebmice. RNA sequencing data analysis revealed a substantial overlap between DMF-regulated and TFEB-overexpression transcriptional profiles, implicating a role of TFEB in DMF-induced suppression of inflammatory and oxidative pathways. Together, DMF ameliorates endothelial dysfunction in diabetes by inhibiting TFEB phosphorylation and restoring TFEB nuclear activity. Endothelial TFEB represents a critical mediator responsible for the vaso-protective effects of DMF and a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of diabetic vascular complications.

articles.title: Functional Biomaterials for Vascular Healing After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: From Surface Engineering to Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) creates a dynamic blood-material-tissue interface in which thrombosis, inflammation, smooth muscle cell proliferation, and endothelial recovery evolve simultaneously. This narrative review examines coronary biomaterials using a healing-centered translational framework that links material properties to molecular and cellular responses, tissue-level healing, measurable structural and functional phenotypes, and clinical outcomes. We review the evolution from bare-metal and drug-eluting stents to polymer-free systems, drug-coated balloons (DCBs), bioresorbable scaffolds, and bioactive or biomimetic surfaces. Particular emphasis is placed on strut geometry, polymer chemistry and degradation, drug-release kinetics, surface properties, corrosion behavior, endothelial barrier function, macrophage responses, thrombogenicity, and neointimal growth. Structural coverage on intravascular imaging is distinguished from functional endothelial recovery, which requires complementary biological or physiological assessment. Randomized evidence is interpreted at the level of the tested device, formulation, lesion, and procedural strategy; newer platforms are not assumed to confer class-wide superiority. Future progress will require multifunctional, healing-responsive platforms that integrate antithrombotic, pro-endothelial, immunomodulatory, and controlled-delivery functions while demonstrating mechanical durability, comparative clinical effectiveness, manufacturability, and cost-effective scalability.

This narrative review examines coronary biomaterials using a healing-centered translational framework that links material properties to molecular and cellular responses, tissue-level healing, measurable structural and functional phenotypes, and clinical outcomes. We review the evolution from bare-metal and drug-eluting stents to polymer-free systems, drug-coated balloons (DCBs), bioresorbable scaffolds, and bioactive or biomimetic surfaces.

articles.title: Electrodeposited Heterostructured Fe-Zn Alloy Microtubes for Vascular Stents: Achieving Enhanced Strength, Ductility, and Uniform Degradation.
articles.abstract: - 1 To synergistically enhance the strength-ductility trade‑off and achieve uniform degradation in Fe-Zn alloys, heterostructured alloy microtubes were fabricated via layer‑by‑layer electrodeposition on a rotating soluble aluminum mandrel. Microstructural characterization revealed a columnar‑layered architecture with coherent interfacial bonding after annealing, free of delamination or defects. The heterostructured sample containing ten alternating soft layers (FZ10) exhibited an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 605 MPa and an elongation of about 17.3%, both superior to those of the single-layer alloy. The loading-unloading-reloading (LUR) experiments demonstrated pronounced hetero-deformation induced (HDI) strengthening and HDI strain-hardening effects, indicating the critical role of interfacial constraints in deformation coordination. Electrochemical and simulated body fluid (SBF) immersion tests showed that the heterostructure promoted faster and more uniform corrosion, with an average degradation rate of approximately 0.135 mm·yafter 56 days, suppressing localized pitting. XPS and FTIR analyses identified the corrosion products as Fe/Zn oxides and Ca-P compounds, forming a bilayer degradation film with a dense inner layer and a loose outer layer. Additionally, heterostructured Fe-Zn alloy microtubes exhibited favorable cytocompatibility. These heterostructured microtubes integrate high strength, ductility, and controlled and uniform degradability, making them promising candidates for further development as biodegradable vascular stent materials.

articles.title: Nonlinear radial force attenuation and stress-corrosion-crack induced fracture of biodegradable Zn alloy stents under vascular bioreactor conditions.
articles.abstract: Zinc alloy vascular stents have emerged as promising candidates in the development of biodegradable stents in recent years. However, due to the complexity of the in vivo environment and the high cost of animal experiments, robust experimental evidence regarding stent degradation-induced radial support loss and the underlying failure mechanisms remains lacking. In this study, a bioreactor system capable of simulating both physiological chemical conditions and pulsatile hemodynamics was developed to investigate the degradation behavior and mechanical evolution of Zn alloy stents. The results revealed a pronounced nonlinear relationship between radial force attenuation and mass loss. Specifically, the radial force decreased by >50% when the mass loss was only approximately 25%, demonstrating a distinct "cliff-like" failure pattern. This rapid deterioration was mainly attributed to stress corrosion cracking (SCC) occurring in the V-shaped load-bearing regions of the stent. During expansion, severe stress concentration and high plastic strain developed in these regions, which, combined with micro-galvanic corrosion, promoted crack initiation and propagation. These experimental findings verify that the mechanical failure of Zn alloy stents is dominated by local structural vulnerability rather than uniform degradation, suggesting that geometric optimization of critical regions is more effective than overall material enhancement for improving long-term structural reliability. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: This research has revealed a pronounced non-linear relationship between radial force attenuation and mass loss in biodegradable Zn alloy vascular stents via a customized bioreactor system. The stents exhibited a distinct "cliff-like" failure pattern, which is primarily dominated by stress corrosion cracking (SCC) localized within the V-shaped load-bearing regions of the stent. This finding indicates that geometric optimization of critical high-stress regions is far more effective for ensuring long-term structural reliability than overall material alloying alignment.

However, due to the complexity of the in vivo environment and the high cost of animal experiments, robust experimental evidence regarding stent degradation-induced radial support loss and the underlying failure mechanisms remains lacking. In this study, a bioreactor system capable of simulating both physiological chemical conditions and pulsatile hemodynamics was developed to investigate the degradation behavior and mechanical evolution of Zn alloy stents.

articles.title: The paradigm evolution of biliary stents: from passive drainage to intelligent diagnostic-therapeutic platforms.
articles.abstract: The clinical management of biliary obstruction has long relied on mechanical drainage provided by stents, yet the inherent risks of re-occlusion, infection, and migration underscore the fundamental limitations of this passive support paradigm. This review proposes a four-stage paradigm evolution framework for biliary stent technology, demonstrating a shift from "passive physical support" to an "active therapeutic platform." The first stage, represented by plastic and self-expandable metallic stents, established anatomical drainage but is limited by biofilm deposition, tumor ingrowth, and migration. The first paradigm shift introduced functionalized stents incorporating drug-eluting, radionuclide, or photothermal/photodynamic coatings, transforming stents into active therapeutic carriers. The second paradigm shift emphasizes bio-adaptation through fully biodegradable stents achieving "temporary support followed by disappearance," alongside cell/matrix coatings to promote tissue regeneration. A third paradigm shift is emerging, focusing on intelligent responsiveness and personalization through closed-loop systems integrating biosensors, wireless communication, and artificial intelligence for real-time monitoring and on-demand therapy, combined with 3D/4D printing for patient-specific adaptation. Through critical assessment of each stage, this review dissects translational challenges including evaluation standards, long-term safety, cost-effectiveness, and regulatory complexities. Ultimately, we present a clinical decision-oriented technological spectrum delineating stent positioning across benign and malignant biliary diseases, envisioning future dynamic platforms integrating diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring to advance biliary intervention into an era of data-driven precision therapy. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: This review establishes, for the first time, a four-stage paradigm evolution framework for biliary stent technology-from passive mechanical support to active functionalized intervention, bio-adaptive scaffolds, and ultimately intelligent diagnostic-therapeutic platforms. By systematically dissecting the irreconcilable contradictions inherent to each paradigm, this framework provides a design-philosophy navigational map that transcends conventional chronological classifications. The integration of materials science mechanisms, cross-technology quantitative comparisons, and evidence-based clinical decision pathways offers both clinicians and biomaterials researchers a comprehensive reference for understanding the past trajectory and future direction of biliary stenting.

articles.title: 2 PDA-Engineered 3D-Printed Polymer-ZrOHybrid Scaffolds Enabling Enhanced Radiopacity, Photothermal Therapy, and Cell Migration Modulation.
articles.abstract: 2 The clinical translation of bioresorbable polymer scaffold is limited by radiolucency, insufficient mechanical strength, and the absence of post-implantation therapeutic control. This study introduces a multifunctional scaffold that addresses these challenges through a polymer-ceramic nanocomposite architecture and bioinspired surface modification. ZrOnanoparticles are uniformly embedded into poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) via solution blending and fabricated into vascular scaffold by fused deposition modeling, yielding improved elastic modulus and radial strength while preserving elastic recovery. The ceramic phase provides intrinsic and sustained x-ray visibility in vitro, in vivo, and during 100-day perfusion, outperforming conventional contrast-agent-based strategies. A subsequent polydopamine (PDA) coating step enables efficient near-infrared (808 nm) photothermal functionality, which was leveraged for photothermal therapeutic modulation and repeatable, pulse-controlled release of paclitaxel. Cellular evaluation of vascular smooth muscle cell viability and migration underscores the therapeutic relevance of this externally triggered strategy for restenosis prevention. Overall, by integrating mechanical reinforcement, x-ray imaging capability, and remote therapeutic activation within a single PCL-based hybrid platform, this system addresses the long-standing clinical limitations of polymeric vascular scaffolds and offers a promising strategy for next-generation theranostic vascular implants.

articles.title: Underlying Plaque Type and Neoatherosclerosis After ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction　- Serial Optical Coherence Tomography Substudy of the CONNECT Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The relationship between underlying plaque type and the development of neoatherosclerosis remains uncertain. METHODS AND RESULTS: 2 This was a secondary analysis of the CONNECT trial, which randomized 239 patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) to receive biodegradable polymer or durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents. Patients with serial optical coherence tomography (OCT) were included and post-procedural OCT frames that corresponded to segments showing neoatherosclerosis at the 3-year follow-up (NA-leading segments) were identified by manual frame matching. At the frame level, we compared post-procedural OCT findings in NALS to 2 comparators: non-NA-leading lesions (lesions without neoatherosclerosis); and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions. Of 144 lesions with serial OCT, neoatherosclerosis occurred in 17 (11.8%). In NA-leading segments, compared to non-NA-leading lesions and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions, the proportion of frames with lipid-rich plaque was higher (71% vs. 54% [odds ratio (OR) 2.72; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.23-6.01] and 58% [OR 2.62; 95% CI 0.99-6.96], respectively). Similarly, the mean (±SD) in-stent atherothrombotic material area was larger in NA-leading segments (0.41±0.39 vs. 0.24±0.31 [geometric mean ratio (GMR) 2.00; 95% CI 1.21-3.29] and 0.16±0.16 mm[GMR 2.33; 95% CI 1.26-4.31], respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Underlying lipid-rich plaque and a higher burden of in-stent atherothrombotic material were associated with neoatherosclerosis at 3 years in STEMI patients, indicating that plaque composition at the time of DES implantation may critically influence neoatherosclerosis formation.

articles.title: Multiscale heterostructured Mg-2 Zn alloy for biodegradable implants: Coordinated strength-ductility, moderate degradation, and immunomodulation.
articles.abstract: -1 -1 High-strength lean-alloy magnesium (Mg) has attracted extensive attention for orthopedic and vascular stent implants owing to its favorable biodegradability and biocompatibility. However, while retaining the chemical composition of specimens and ensuring high biosafety, the major challenge is to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off and achieve uniform degradation behavior. In this study, a lean Mg-2 wt% Zn alloy with balanced strength and ductility was fabricated via hot working. The alloy possessed a bimodal heterogeneous structure composed of fine-grained regions containing nanograins and nanotwins, as well as coarse-grained regions. It attained an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 350 MPa with an elongation of 13%. This heterostructured Mg-2Zn alloy exhibits better performance compared with the commercial rare-earth-containing WE43 alloy. Moreover, it demonstrated slow degradation rates (0.07 mm·yearin vitro and 0.11 mm·yearin vivo) driven by multi-phase interface effects. Furthermore, the heterostructured Mg-2 Zn alloy exhibited antibacterial activity in vitro and a relatively mild peri‑implant inflammatory response in vivo. This study differs from conventional rare-earth alloy strengthening strategies, clarifies the formation and regulation mechanisms of heterostructures, and provides theoretical and technical support for the clinical translation of high-performance biodegradable Mg alloys. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: To address the bottleneck of balancing mechanical performance and biocompatibility in rare-earth-free magnesium (Mg) alloys for biodegradable temporary implants, this study employed a multi-pass hot-rolling process with an optimized final rolling temperature to produce the lean-alloyed Mg-2 Zn heterostructured alloy. The alloy achieved a reasonable combination of tensile strength (349 MPa) and elongation (13%), mitigating the common strength-ductility trade-off observed in Mg-2 Zn alloys. Metabolomic analysis showed that metal ions slowly released during alloy degradation could regulate biological energy metabolism, endowing the material with antibacterial activity in vitro and a relatively mild peri‑implant inflammatory response in vivo. This study clarified the mechanisms associated with heterostructure formation, strength-ductility synergistic strengthening, slow degradation, and biological metabolic regulation. It also provided experimental support for the research and development of high-performance rare-earth-free Mg-based biomaterials.

However, while retaining the chemical composition of specimens and ensuring high biosafety, the major challenge is to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off and achieve uniform degradation behavior. In this study, a lean Mg-2 wt% Zn alloy with balanced strength and ductility was fabricated via hot working.

articles.title: Neurovascular coupling in simultaneous EEG-fNIRS studies: A scoping review of analytical frameworks and clinical applications.
articles.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) have been used across cognitive and physiological states and in diverse clinical populations. However, the interpretation of cross-modal coupling remains difficult because findings from different analytical frameworks, populations, and experimental conditions have not been systematically mapped. This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO, and IEEE Xplore were searched through February 10, 2026, for studies that quantitatively related simultaneously recorded EEG and fNIRS signals. Two reviewers independently screened the records. Findings were synthesized narratively, and analytical pipelines were mapped across the signal domain, feature extraction, coupling metric, and temporal lag handling. Fifty-seven studies were included. Amplitude-based studies related event-related potentials and oscillatory EEG features to focal hemodynamic responses, with associations varying across electrophysiological features, cortical regions, and task conditions. Frequency- and scale-specific analyses identified band-dependent relationships, while coupling at ultra-slow scales showed sensitivity to vascular and systemic physiological influences. Studies that explicitly modeled timing identified several-second offsets in some paradigms, while directional estimates varied across tasks and recording states. Network analyses showed partial and context-dependent correspondence between EEG- and fNIRS-derived measures, while model-based approaches characterized multivariate and predictive cross-modal relationships. Across frameworks, observed coupling differed with recording state, frequency band, cortical region, and temporal lag handling rather than representing a single quantity. Clinical findings were heterogeneous, and most condition-specific patterns were supported by small and methodologically diverse evidence bases. These findings support framework-matched analysis and pipeline-explicit reporting when interpreting EEG-fNIRS coupling.

However, the interpretation of cross-modal coupling remains difficult because findings from different analytical frameworks, populations, and experimental conditions have not been systematically mapped. This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR).

articles.title: Electrophysiological and computational analyses of anethole-induced inhibition of L-type calcium channels in rat tracheal smooth muscle.
articles.abstract: 2+ 2+ 2+ + 1/2 Ba Anethole, a naturally occurring phenylpropanoid, is a major constituent of several essential oils and exhibits a broad spectrum of pharmacological activities, including reduction of neuronal excitability, antispasmodic effects, and inhibition of Cainflux. To elucidate the mechanism underlying calcium current inhibition, we investigated the effects of anethole on voltage-dependent calcium channels (VDCCs) in rat tracheal smooth muscle myocytes. Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in dissociated tracheal myocytes were combined with molecular docking analyses. Bawas used as the charge carrier because it generates larger and more stable inward currents through L-type VDCCs than Ca. At 0.67 mM (approximately the IC₅₀ for inhibition of tracheal contraction induced by 60 mM K), anethole reduced the peak current density from -3.58 ± 0.39 to -1.53 ± 0.26 pA/pF (n = 18). In addition, anethole shifted the half-activation voltage (V) from -6.46 to +1.41 mV and the half-inactivation voltage from -25.38 to -36.42 mV, indicating depolarizing and hyperpolarizing shifts in the steady-state activation and inactivation curves, respectively. Both effects reduced channel availability and favored inhibition of I. Computational analyses identified preferential interaction regions within the pore-forming and voltage-sensing domains of the channel, providing a plausible structural basis for both current inhibition and voltage-dependent modulation. Collectively, the electrophysiological and computational findings indicate that anethole inhibits VDCCs through complementary mechanisms involving pore interaction together with modulation of channel activation and inactivation. These effects occur at concentrations that also inhibit tracheal smooth muscle contraction, supporting the hypothesis that VDCC inhibition contributes to the antispasmodic action of anethole.

articles.title: Delayed Cerebral Ischemia as Progressive Neurovascular Unit Failure: A Hypothesis-Generating Perspective.
articles.abstract: Despite decades of investigation, delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) remains the principal cause of secondary neurological injury following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Successive paradigms including angiographic vasospasm, early brain injury, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, cortical spreading depolarization, microvascular dysfunction, oxidative stress, and metabolic failure have each explained important aspects of disease biology. However, these mechanisms have largely evolved as parallel explanations rather than components of an integrated model, leaving the dissociation between vasospasm and DCI, delayed onset, interpatient heterogeneity, and limited efficacy of vasospasm-directed therapies incompletely explained. This perspective proposes, as a hypothesis, progressive neurovascular unit (NVU) failure as a conceptual framework for DCI after aSAH. We integrate experimental, translational, and clinical evidence spanning vascular biology, neuroimmunology, cerebrovascular physiology, electrophysiology, metabolism, biomarker research, and therapeutic trials to develop a hypothesis-generating framework. The established mechanisms of DCI may represent interacting manifestations of progressive disruption of coordinated signaling among endothelial, vascular smooth muscle, pericyte, astrocytic, microglial, and neuronal compartments of the neurovascular unit. Within this framework, early brain injury may initiate NVU dysfunction, which is amplified by interacting vascular, barrier, inflammatory, electrophysiological, and metabolic disturbances, culminating in neuronal metabolic failure and tissue injury. Vasospasm is therefore positioned as one contributor to this process rather than a sufficient explanation for DCI. This framework offers a possible basis for interpreting clinical heterogeneity and therapeutic discordance while generating testable predictions for multimodal biomarker development, biological phenotyping, and mechanism-informed therapeutic strategies. The framework does not introduce new mechanisms; rather, it proposes a testable distinction between compensated NVU dysfunction and NVU failure, frames compartment-specific non-additive interactions as an empirical question, and organizes biomarkers by the NVU compartment they reflect. These proposals remain to be validated.

articles.title: Endothelial Piezo1 Hyperactivity Drives Neurovascular Dysfunction in Hypertension.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major driver of neurovascular dysfunction and cognitive decline, yet the molecular mechanisms linking elevated arterial pressure to impaired cerebral blood flow remain poorly defined. Piezo1, a mechanosensitive cation channel enriched in the brain endothelium, is a candidate mediator of cerebral blood flow deficits during hypertension. METHODS: Using 2 distinct mouse models of hypertension-BPH/2J mice (genetically hypertensive strain) and angiotensin II-infused C57BL/6J mice-we assessed brain endothelial Piezo1 activity using patch-clamp electrophysiology. Endothelial-specific Piezo1 deletion models were used to evaluate the role of the channel in hypertension-associated cerebrovascular impairment. Cerebral blood flow responses were measured in vivo by laser speckle contrast imaging, and super-resolution nanoscopy was used to quantify Piezo1 nanoscale organization. Behavioral testing was used to assess cognition. RESULTS: 2 Genetic manipulation of endothelial Piezo1 had minimal impact on baseline blood pressure. However, cerebral endothelial Piezo1 activity was markedly elevated in different hypertension models. Deletion of endothelial Piezo1 protected against hypertension-induced cerebrovascular deficits, including impaired vasomotion, reduced functional hyperemia, and blunted CO-evoked hyperemia. Super-resolution imaging revealed that hypertension increased Piezo1 clustering, consistent with electrophysiological findings of enhanced channel coupling and open probability. Mechanistically, Piezo1 hyperactivity was PKC (protein kinase C)-dependent, and the PKC-Piezo1 spatial association was enhanced during hypertension. Importantly, PKC inhibition normalized brain endothelial Piezo1 activity, restored cerebral blood flow responses, and rescued cognitive performance. CONCLUSIONS: Hypertension increased the gain of Piezo1 function in brain endothelial cells, promoting dysfunctional neurovascular signaling and cognitive impairment. Targeting Piezo1 or PKC signaling selectively restored cerebrovascular regulation. This work identifies a mechanosensitive pathway that could be leveraged to protect the hypertensive brain.
